items.title: Use free local image-to-3D models only for mid-ground and background props and silhouettes; use a paid 3D…
items.text: Use free local image-to-3D models only for mid-ground and background props and silhouettes; use a paid 3D model for hero objects, faces and close-ups of small hard-surface detail.
items.why: Local output distorts faces and loses small parts and metal finishes, while the paid version keeps them recognisable.
items.when: Choosing a 3D generation route for an ad scene or product set.

items.title: A 3D build counts only once the exact code that made it is saved step by step, so the same build can be…
items.text: A 3D build counts only once the exact code that made it is saved step by step, so the same build can be recreated unchanged in any account; never retype or rewrite a saved step.
items.why: 3D projects cannot be shared or imported between accounts, so the code is the only portable standard.
items.when: Any 3D set, product master or world built for ads.

items.title: Build 3D sets and renders freely, but treat the final print as the only step that spends credits, and print…
items.text: Build 3D sets and renders freely, but treat the final print as the only step that spends credits, and print with the product's casting sheet.
items.why: Sets and renders cost nothing; only a print spends money.

items.title: Before any finished ad drop reaches the person who uploads it, it must pass every handoff check: the handoff…
items.text: Before any finished ad drop reaches the person who uploads it, it must pass every handoff check: the handoff doc carries its own folder link, every picture has real bytes on the server, every ad folder has at least one picture, every ad has copy and no copy names a missing ad, every ad name parses to the naming convention, every funnel link returns 200, and the recipient can open the folder.
items.why: Every defect that cost time lived in the seam between the machines that make, write, name and carry the drop.
items.when: Handing a finished ad drop to {media buyer} or uploader.

items.title: If any handoff check fails, refuse the handoff and name what is missing; never send a link to an incomplete…
items.text: If any handoff check fails, refuse the handoff and name what is missing; never send a link to an incomplete drop.
items.why: A link to an incomplete handoff costs more time than no link.

items.title: A gate refuses and names the owner of the fault; it never fixes the fault itself (a missing picture goes back…
items.text: A gate refuses and names the owner of the fault; it never fixes the fault itself (a missing picture goes back to picture making, a dead link to the funnel).
items.why: Keeps each fault with the stage that produced it so fixes compound there.
items.when: Any quality gate between production stages.

items.title: Add a new check to a gate only when a real failure earned it; never add a precaution somebody imagined.
items.text: Add a new check to a gate only when a real failure earned it; never add a precaution somebody imagined.
items.why: Gates should encode failures that actually cost time, not speculative ones.

items.title: Every ad name must parse to the naming convention before it ships.
items.text: Every ad name must parse to the naming convention before it ships.
items.why: A name that does not parse cannot join ad spend back to the creative, which is the whole point of the name.
items.when: Naming ads before upload to Meta or any ad platform.

items.title: Confirm every ad destination link is deployed and returns 200 before ads go live.
items.text: Confirm every ad destination link is deployed and returns 200 before ads go live.
items.why: Ads were nearly run to 404 pages because destinations sat on an undeployed branch.

items.title: Verify delivered files against the server, never against a local synced folder.
items.text: Verify delivered files against the server, never against a local synced folder.
items.why: A file that exists locally may be a filename with no bytes on the server.

items.title: Every paid scraping run must state its price ceiling first and be hard-capped at that ceiling, with a dry run…
items.text: Every paid scraping run must state its price ceiling first and be hard-capped at that ceiling, with a dry run available before spending.
items.why: Spend on data pulls must be bounded before it starts.
items.when: Paid social or marketplace scraping runs.

items.title: Kill an internal map or dashboard if 4 weeks pass with no kill, reuse or drift decision citing it, or if…
items.text: Kill an internal map or dashboard if 4 weeks pass with no kill, reuse or drift decision citing it, or if keeping it accurate needs manual edits beyond the records people already maintain.
items.why: A view nobody decides from, or one that must be hand-fed, becomes a stale second source of truth.
items.when: Reviewing internal system views and dashboards.

items.title: Report a missing or disagreeing input as drift; never invent a fact to fill a gap or draw around it.
items.text: Report a missing or disagreeing input as drift; never invent a fact to fill a gap or draw around it.
items.why: A gap shown honestly is the most useful thing a map says; smoothing it over is a lie in a picture.
items.when: Compiling any system view or report from records.

items.title: Plan variations of a proven ad by marking every element LOCK (keep exactly) or LEVER (test), with evidence…
items.text: Plan variations of a proven ad by marking every element LOCK (keep exactly) or LEVER (test), with evidence from the {brand}'s whole post corpus, then rank the levers by estimated impact and move the highest-impact ones first.
items.why: Start adjusting the highest-impact opportunities on what already worked instead of guessing.
items.when: Building variations from a winning video ad.

items.title: Call an element a LOCK only when the {brand}'s top posts converge on this ad's value and no near-twin moved…
items.text: Call an element a LOCK only when the {brand}'s top posts converge on this ad's value and no near-twin moved results by changing it, when it is load-bearing in the replication spec, or when a brand rule fixes it; otherwise it is a LEVER. A value the whole corpus shares is not proof it works, only that nothing else was tried.
items.why: The first runs locked too much on corpus counts alone.
items.when: Lock-vs-lever calls on a proven ad.

items.title: Treat a variable as lock-leaning when one value holds 60% or more of the top-quartile posts' views; otherwise…
items.text: Treat a variable as lock-leaning when one value holds 60% or more of the top-quartile posts' views; otherwise treat it as a lever, and always treat on-screen text as a lever.
items.why: Gives a numeric line between what the winners converge on and what is still open to test.
items.when: Reading a brand's variable index across its posts.

items.title: Call the parts of an element separately (the layout can be a lock while the person in it is a lever), and…
items.text: Call the parts of an element separately (the layout can be a lock while the person in it is a lever), and make separate calls for the organic and the paid cut.
items.why: A paid cut plays muted, is cropped to 4:5 and must carry an offer, so an organic lock can be a paid lever.

items.title: Rank only the ten highest-impact levers for the first set and park the rest as 'later'; label every impact…
items.text: Rank only the ten highest-impact levers for the first set and park the rest as 'later'; label every impact rank an estimate weighing how much of the first three seconds the element controls, whether posts show it moving results, and the cost to test.
items.why: Ranking everything swung to 33 levers; nothing in the corpus isolates one variable, so impact is an estimate.

items.title: Each variation changes ONE lever (at most two variables, and two only when they cannot move apart) and never…
items.text: Each variation changes ONE lever (at most two variables, and two only when they cannot move apart) and never changes the ad's format, framework or structure; a variation that changes three variables is two variations.
items.why: Every result stays readable against the original.

items.title: Start every variation set with a control (V00): the original rebuilt only as much as paid placement needs,…
items.text: Start every variation set with a control (V00): the original rebuilt only as much as paid placement needs, and read every variation against it.
items.why: Results only mean something against an unchanged baseline.

items.title: Order variations by estimated impact, cheaper tests of an equal lever first, and cover the levers rather than…
items.text: Order variations by estimated impact, cheaper tests of an equal lever first, and cover the levers rather than one lever many ways; two variations may move the same variable only when aimed at different sub-avatars.
items.why: Spreads the test budget across the most likely wins.

items.title: Before planning paid variations, check the paid cut's needs: works sound-off with captions, subject inside…
items.text: Before planning paid variations, check the paid cut's needs: works sound-off with captions, subject inside the 4:5 zone, one offer and one button at the end, the hero SKU. Each need the original misses gets its own variation.
items.why: An organic winner does not automatically meet paid placement requirements.
items.when: Turning an organic winner into paid ads.

items.title: When {brand} has more than one hero product and a winning ad shows only one, test the ad on another hero…
items.text: When {brand} has more than one hero product and a winning ad shows only one, test the ad on another hero product as its own variation.
items.why: A proven structure may carry a second hero product.

items.title: Never regenerate a real {creator}'s or customer's likeness; cast person-levers (who reacts, pitches,…
items.text: Never regenerate a real {creator}'s or customer's likeness; cast person-levers (who reacts, pitches, demonstrates) from the cleared synthetic cast by name, matched to a sub-avatar, and route any real likeness, cloned voice, public figure or retail claim to the owner as a ruling.
items.why: Likeness, voice and claims are owner-only calls.

items.title: New on-screen words or lines come verbatim from the customer-language bank; if nothing fits, flag a bank line…
items.text: New on-screen words or lines come verbatim from the customer-language bank; if nothing fits, flag a bank line as needed and never invent customer language.
items.why: Customer words carry the response; invented language does not.
items.when: Writing new lines, stickers or captions for variations.

items.title: Label every variation's hypothesis as inference and state the result that would confirm it and the result…
items.text: Label every variation's hypothesis as inference and state the result that would confirm it and the result that would kill it.
items.why: A test is only useful if its outcome can decide something.

items.title: A proposed new format must be built from at least three parts the corpus already proves, must not be a…
items.text: A proposed new format must be built from at least three parts the corpus already proves, must not be a combination the {brand} has already run, and stays marked 'new, untested' until it runs.
items.why: New formats should recombine proven parts, not guesses.

items.title: Numbers in a plan come from computed data (evidence from the index, cost as units times the rate card), never…
items.text: Numbers in a plan come from computed data (evidence from the index, cost as units times the rate card), never from the model; a prompt may quote numbers, never make them.
items.why: Model-made numbers are unreliable.
items.when: Any AI planning or analysis stage.

items.title: Chained AI clips are made in order, each starting from the real last frame of the clip before; at every join…
items.text: Chained AI clips are made in order, each starting from the real last frame of the clip before; at every join the frame-to-frame change must stay within about 2x the clip's median frame step, with an optical-flow bridge only as a fallback.
items.why: Chained generated clips popped at the joins.
items.when: Producing videos from chained AI clips.

items.title: Every AI-made variation must pass its QC gates: the person matches the cast sheet in every sampled frame, the…
items.text: Every AI-made variation must pass its QC gates: the person matches the cast sheet in every sampled frame, the product on screen is the exact SKU named, no repeated frames outside planned holds, faces and product inside the centred 4:5 zone with text off faces and clear of platform UI, only bank words and the brand's never-lists held, organic cuts keep the source's not-an-ad look, re-voiced lines sync within ±0.3 s, and new voices match the person's age and gender.
items.why: Each gate maps to a failure that ships a broken or off-brand ad.

items.title: A cheaper experimental production route may be offered as an alternative in a recipe, never as the default;…
items.text: A cheaper experimental production route may be offered as an alternative in a recipe, never as the default; the locked route stays default until the test route passes.
items.why: Keeps production reliable while still testing cost cuts.

items.title: To make new video ads from a winner, keep the fresh format's structure locked and carry the winner's content…
items.text: To make new video ads from a winner, keep the fresh format's structure locked and carry the winner's content in the winner's order; list anything the format cannot carry as dropped, take product facts only from the brand files, and run one offer only.
items.why: Takes ads that already sold and tells them again in a format someone else proved.
items.when: Proven ad to new format variations.

items.title: Match video winners to video formats only, keep one cut per winner (when two winners are essentially the same…
items.text: Match video winners to video formats only, keep one cut per winner (when two winners are essentially the same ad keep the top seller), and only pair a format that fits the avatar.
items.why: Keeps the variation grid clean and on-avatar.
items.when: Building a winner x format grid.

items.title: The core-message line of a brief built from a winner comes from the winner and the {brand}, never from the…
items.text: The core-message line of a brief built from a winner comes from the winner and the {brand}, never from the format swipe.
items.why: Briefs opened with the swipe's message instead of the brand's.
items.when: Proven ad to new format briefs.

items.title: When a brief fails the viewer check, send it back to the stage that owns the failing part (opening to hooks,…
items.text: When a brief fails the viewer check, send it back to the stage that owns the failing part (opening to hooks, middle to placement, close to the close stage); after two fails, hold it for the owner.
items.why: Fixes land where the fault was made, with a hard stop on loops.

items.title: A swipe's own format always passes the format hold; audit fails on claims, the offer or brand rules are…
items.text: A swipe's own format always passes the format hold; audit fails on claims, the offer or brand rules are fixed, never passed.
items.why: The format is proven; claims and offer accuracy are not negotiable.

items.title: Run one item all the way to the finished brief first, read it and fix what breaks, then run the rest in small…
items.text: Run one item all the way to the finished brief first, read it and fix what breaks, then run the rest in small batches.
items.why: Running everything at once multiplies every rework by the batch size.

items.title: Use the cheaper model for stages that read and check, and the top model only for writing stages.
items.text: Use the cheaper model for stages that read and check, and the top model only for writing stages.
items.why: Every stage on the top model burned usage for no gain.
items.when: Assigning models to AI chain stages.

items.title: The owner picks which items run; nothing is ever queued for him.
items.text: The owner picks which items run; nothing is ever queued for him.
items.why: He directs the work.

items.title: Index footage by what is IN each clip (who, what action, setting, usable-as), never by its file name, so an…
items.text: Index footage by what is IN each clip (who, what action, setting, usable-as), never by its file name, so an edit can ask for a shot instead of someone scrubbing through files.
items.why: File names say nothing about what a clip can be used for.

items.title: Fill a storyboard scene from owned footage first, then AI made from a clean real frame, and only then flag it…
items.text: Fill a storyboard scene from owned footage first, then AI made from a clean real frame, and only then flag it unfilled.
items.why: Owned real footage beats generated footage, and real frames make better AI references.
items.when: Sourcing shots for a video brief.

items.title: Never use {creator} footage in a channel the creator has not cleared: footage whose usage rights refuse that…
items.text: Never use {creator} footage in a channel the creator has not cleared: footage whose usage rights refuse that use or have expired is excluded; email use requires an explicit yes.
items.why: Footage from creators who never agreed to ads had already run as an ad.
items.when: Picking creator footage for ads, website or email.

items.title: Burned-in captions and handles mark a clip, they never remove it from use; every pick carries its marks so…
items.text: Burned-in captions and handles mark a clip, they never remove it from use; every pick carries its marks so the selector knows, and only an AI reference frame must be text-clean.
items.why: Removing marked clips throws away usable footage; marking keeps the choice informed.
items.when: Selecting b-roll and footage for edits.

items.title: Never read a person's ethnicity from a picture; take it only from how the footage was filed.
items.text: Never read a person's ethnicity from a picture; take it only from how the footage was filed.
items.why: Appearance-based ethnicity reads are unreliable and inappropriate.
items.when: Tagging people in footage or images.

items.title: Mark footage that came from a finished ad with the ad it came from, and keep talking-to-camera scenes out of…
items.text: Mark footage that came from a finished ad with the ad it came from, and keep talking-to-camera scenes out of b-roll picks.
items.why: Ad folders hold sourced b-roll, so whoever picks must know its origin.

items.title: Do all free preparation work (frames, transcripts, measurements) before any paid model call, and cap each…
items.text: Do all free preparation work (frames, transcripts, measurements) before any paid model call, and cap each paid pass with a budget.
items.why: A whole drive can be prepared before a penny is spent.
items.when: Any bulk AI indexing or analysis job.

items.title: Pick the smallest model that does the job; a bigger model that costs far more and does not change the outcome…
items.text: Pick the smallest model that does the job; a bigger model that costs far more and does not change the outcome is waste.
items.why: Bigger transcription models cost hours across thousands of clips and change nothing about whether a clip is findable.
items.when: Choosing models for bulk AI work.

items.title: Transcribe every word of a swipe in the language it was said, with who said it and when; never accept a…
items.text: Transcribe every word of a swipe in the language it was said, with who said it and when; never accept a transcript that drops or silently translates speech, and flag every place a person should listen.
items.why: Speech-to-text turned a mother's Korean lines into '[laughs]' and translated her without a word.

items.title: Read a swipe's full sound: voices per person, the music (named, tempo, key, builds and drops), every sound…
items.text: Read a swipe's full sound: voices per person, the music (named, tempo, key, builds and drops), every sound effect timed, and the mix (loudness, ducking, silences), not the words alone.
items.why: Knowing exactly what was heard lets casting and voice generation make the right thing.

items.title: When a reading does not fit the fixed label list, keep it and name it unknown; never force it into the…
items.text: When a reading does not fit the fixed label list, keep it and name it unknown; never force it into the nearest label or drop it.
items.why: Forced labels hide new information.
items.when: Classifying anything against a fixed vocabulary.

items.title: Invest in the record (teardown, research read, idea), not the brief: a brief is a cheap projection of a…
items.text: Invest in the record (teardown, research read, idea), not the brief: a brief is a cheap projection of a record, so a new brief style should print against every record already made.
items.why: A teardown costs about 25 minutes and the brief off it 21 seconds, seventy to one.
items.when: Designing brief formats and research pipelines.

items.title: Name a brief for what asset it makes and who acts on it (asset + actor), never for the stage of a chain that…
items.text: Name a brief for what asset it makes and who acts on it (asset + actor), never for the stage of a chain that printed it.
items.why: A brief outlives the chain that first printed it; stage-number names collided across lanes.

items.title: A brief style or prompt that has produced nothing in 30 days is parked, not live, whatever its config claims;…
items.text: A brief style or prompt that has produced nothing in 30 days is parked, not live, whatever its config claims; 'live' needs a run count and a date as evidence.
items.why: Dead versions read as live, which pinned a config three versions behind.
items.when: Auditing which brief styles and prompts are in use.

items.title: Archive superseded prompts out of live folders, never delete them, and never leave them beside current…
items.text: Archive superseded prompts out of live folders, never delete them, and never leave them beside current versions.
items.why: Superseded prompts sitting beside current ones were read as live.

items.title: Every brief ships with a run sheet that says exactly how to make each asset, the same core for any person or…
items.text: Every brief ships with a run sheet that says exactly how to make each asset, the same core for any person or agent; a change to what gets made goes in the core, never in one rendering of it.
items.why: The workflow and briefs must be agent-agnostic.
items.when: Handing any brief to a maker.

items.title: Pass every generation prompt exactly as written, never retyped, and keep the generator's own record of what…
items.text: Pass every generation prompt exactly as written, never retyped, and keep the generator's own record of what was sent beside each returned asset; the record outranks any receipt.
items.why: A retyped prompt came back corrupted, with words changed and never-rules dropped, and only the record showed it.
items.when: Running any AI generation from a brief.

items.title: Research is not a brief; keep research reads separate from the briefs printed from them.
items.text: Research is not a brief; keep research reads separate from the briefs printed from them.
items.why: Research is its own record with its own life.

items.title: A {creator} brief follows one shape: title, format, inspired-by swipe, primary product, suggested length,…
items.text: A {creator} brief follows one shape: title, format, inspired-by swipe, primary product, suggested length, sound, swipe file, core idea, 2-3 hook directions, 4-5 key story beats, 3-6 must-have shots, 2-3 product points, how to say it, then the script straight through. No pictures.
items.why: One short brief a creator films from.

items.title: Let the {creator} say it their own way: hooks are directions, not scripts, but the guarantee is said word for…
items.text: Let the {creator} say it their own way: hooks are directions, not scripts, but the guarantee is said word for word; never send a creator the internal spec, shot gates or editor notes.
items.why: Creators perform better in their own words; the internal spec is for the team.

items.title: Nothing goes to a {creator} until the owner approves the brief; delivery sends only approved briefs.
items.text: Nothing goes to a {creator} until the owner approves the brief; delivery sends only approved briefs.
items.why: The owner signs off every brief before it leaves.

items.title: An ad built from a {creator}'s returned video must carry the creator's attribution id in its destination link…
items.text: An ad built from a {creator}'s returned video must carry the creator's attribution id in its destination link and at the end of its ad name.
items.why: Without it the ad is unattributed and the creator goes unpaid.

items.title: A brief field whose value is unknown is left empty, never guessed.
items.text: A brief field whose value is unknown is left empty, never guessed.
items.why: A guessed tag corrupts the numbers loop that joins results back to briefs.

items.title: Build an AI character's identity from a real image, never from a written description; a character build with…
items.text: Build an AI character's identity from a real image, never from a written description; a character build with no reference frame is refused.
items.why: A character written as prose is a different person every roll.
items.when: Creating any AI person for ads.

items.title: A reference frame carries the world (room, light, framing, camera register, wardrobe category), never the…
items.text: A reference frame carries the world (room, light, framing, camera register, wardrobe category), never the person: the generated character must be a different person from anyone in the reference.
items.why: Baseline, not likeness; generated shots must cut against filmed footage without a change of world.
items.when: Generating AI characters from owned footage.

items.title: A role the cast bank already covers never gets a new face; cast the banked person, and if they are wrong for…
items.text: A role the cast bank already covers never gets a new face; cast the banked person, and if they are wrong for it, change the bank deliberately rather than adding a second face.
items.why: A second face for a covered role breaks the first across everything already shipped.

items.title: Make AI characters only from existing assets and customer information, always with reference files; a…
items.text: Make AI characters only from existing assets and customer information, always with reference files; a character without a casting sheet is not current and is not used in new work until it has one.
items.why: Only sheet-backed characters stay consistent across shots.
items.when: Choosing who appears in new AI ads.

items.title: Derive every follow-on sheet from the master reference, never from the last output.
items.text: Derive every follow-on sheet from the master reference, never from the last output.
items.why: Nothing derived from a derivative stops drift compounding.
items.when: Building character sheets and image chains.

items.title: When a generated picture fails the judge, hold it and fix the prompt, never patch the picture; nothing later…
items.text: When a generated picture fails the judge, hold it and fix the prompt, never patch the picture; nothing later may reference a held picture.
items.why: A hold is a prompt fault; patching pictures hides it.

items.title: Give the generator the subject noun and the complete wardrobe explicitly; never leave either to inference or…
items.text: Give the generator the subject noun and the complete wardrobe explicitly; never leave either to inference or a default.
items.why: A vague noun is a vague face, and a default decides something about the brand's person nobody asked for.

items.title: Every AI person gets one headshot as the single face reference that every picture takes its face from, plus…
items.text: Every AI person gets one headshot as the single face reference that every picture takes its face from, plus emotional-state, detail and body-part close-up sheets at the same realism; outfits are stored without a face and the banked voice is the only voice.
items.why: One reference headshot keeps the face identical scene by scene, frame by frame.

items.title: Never use a real customer's picture as a reference to seed an AI face, and use only person-free frames as…
items.text: Never use a real customer's picture as a reference to seed an AI face, and use only person-free frames as world references.
items.why: A real customer's likeness may not seed a face; a world frame with a person put that person back in.
items.when: Building avatar test sets for customer groups.

items.title: New work uses only the current cast, sets and product casting sheets; retired people, sets and old product…
items.text: New work uses only the current cast, sets and product casting sheets; retired people, sets and old product photos are refused by name, and a product with no current casting sheet cannot be pictured in an ad until it has one.
items.why: Old faces and packshots are out of new ads.
items.when: Every new image or video ad.

items.title: A {creator}'s likeness stays blocked from AI use until that creator gives a written yes.
items.text: A {creator}'s likeness stays blocked from AI use until that creator gives a written yes.
items.why: Creator likeness needs explicit consent.
items.when: Using creator faces in AI production.

items.title: Never coin a name, id or role for a character, angle or asset; a name not given is left out, never guessed.
items.text: Never coin a name, id or role for a character, angle or asset; a name not given is left out, never guessed.
items.why: Names are the owner's to set.
items.when: Any AI build that needs a name.

items.title: Never rewire a working chain on assumption; build the replacement alongside and retire the old one only once…
items.text: Never rewire a working chain on assumption; build the replacement alongside and retire the old one only once the new one is proven.
items.why: Switching over unproven breaks live work.

items.title: An AI chain stage that would receive no input, or whose input stage was skipped, must fail loudly by name…
items.text: An AI chain stage that would receive no input, or whose input stage was skipped, must fail loudly by name rather than run on empty input.
items.why: A stage handed nothing writes confident prose about a stage that never ran.

items.title: When a chosen model is busy or cannot take the input (for example video sent to a text-only model), fail the…
items.text: When a chosen model is busy or cannot take the input (for example video sent to a text-only model), fail the run; never silently fall back to a different model or drop the media.
items.why: Answering confidently about a video the model never saw is the expensive failure, and a silent swap makes the run record a lie.
items.when: Running AI stages on a declared model.

items.title: Where a person has picked a version, the human pick outranks any automatic default; without one, take the…
items.text: Where a person has picked a version, the human pick outranks any automatic default; without one, take the control version.
items.why: The machine's default is only a stand-in for the human choice.

items.title: Never write ad copy from scratch: every primary text, headline and description copies the structure of one of…
items.text: Never write ad copy from scratch: every primary text, headline and description copies the structure of one of {brand}'s own ads that already sold (top 25 by spend plus top 25 by lowest cost per sale), and only the named blanks change.
items.why: Writing brand-new copy per ad was freeballing off the brief instead of using proven formats.
items.when: Writing Meta ad copy for any new ad.

items.title: Give every new ad 3 primary texts, 2 headlines and 2 descriptions, each filled from a different winning ad's…
items.text: Give every new ad 3 primary texts, 2 headlines and 2 descriptions, each filled from a different winning ad's format; keep headlines at 40 characters or fewer and descriptions at 30 or fewer.
items.why: Each slot carries a proven structure and fits the placement.

items.title: When filling a winning copy format, first write this ad's own elements (who and her era, the moment, the…
items.text: When filling a winning copy format, first write this ad's own elements (who and her era, the moment, the problem, the angle, the picture) and fill every blank from them; keep the {brand}'s own story and claims, and replace any story that belongs to another ad.
items.why: Copy must be relevant to the brief itself, not retell the source ad's story.

items.title: Pick copy formats to fill by matching the ad's awareness level first, then best spend; never use a promotion…
items.text: Pick copy formats to fill by matching the ad's awareness level first, then best spend; never use a promotion or seasonal ad's format for a non-promotion ad, and never use a format cut off mid-sentence.
items.why: The format must fit the ad's market state and be the real ad's own words.
items.when: Choosing copy formats for a new ad.

items.title: No price, deal, pack offer or money-back line in a Meta headline or description unless the ad is clearly a…
items.text: No price, deal, pack offer or money-back line in a Meta headline or description unless the ad is clearly a promotion or value-focused; top-of-funnel copy must be written at unaware levels.
items.why: Prices up top are tip-of-funnel brain rot; the copy should match unaware readers.

items.title: Build every piece of copy on three foundations: the reader's awareness level, the customer's verbatim words,…
items.text: Build every piece of copy on three foundations: the reader's awareness level, the customer's verbatim words, and spice; an empty language pull is stated, never quietly skipped.
items.why: Awareness levels, verbatims and spice are the foundation of the work.

items.title: Copy swiped from an organic source is written in the {creator}'s voice, never the brand's; it is that person…
items.text: Copy swiped from an organic source is written in the {creator}'s voice, never the brand's; it is that person speaking, not brand copy with their name on it.
items.why: Replicated copy most often reverts to brand voice, which kills what made the source work.

items.title: Ship every hook and every email subject line: write the control (the source's own opening, swiped straight…
items.text: Ship every hook and every email subject line: write the control (the source's own opening, swiped straight and never improved) plus variations, and never let the machine rank, pick or recommend one.
items.why: An upgraded control measures nothing; choosing is the owner's call and the numbers decide (held in both the ad copy and email lines).

items.title: Abstract a swipe into a brand-free structure first, then inject the {brand} into that structure by…
items.text: Abstract a swipe into a brand-free structure first, then inject the {brand} into that structure by substitution, never by rewrite.
items.why: Writing from a record produces copy about the brand in the source's rough direction; writing from the structure puts the brand into the source's actual shape.

items.title: Treat existing copy, including your own live ads, as a source to swipe like any video, not as a bank to match…
items.text: Treat existing copy, including your own live ads, as a source to swipe like any video, not as a bank to match against.
items.why: Modelling live ads as a copy bank was wrong.

items.title: A source that is already an ad inherits its commercial structure; an organic source has none, so the…
items.text: A source that is already an ad inherits its commercial structure; an organic source has none, so the expansion (commercial build-out) is written only for organic sources.
items.why: Organic posts lack an offer and close that ads already carry.

items.title: When an AI account runs out of usage, stop the run on the first refusal and say so; never retry it.
items.text: When an AI account runs out of usage, stop the run on the first refusal and say so; never retry it. Ordinary failures get up to three attempts.
items.why: Retrying a usage limit burns time with no chance of success.

items.title: Build creative strategy around exactly what Meta has published about how it picks and groups ads, and use…
items.text: Build creative strategy around exactly what Meta has published about how it picks and groups ads, and use Meta's own vocabulary (creative diversification, iteration, similarity, fatigue, persona) in the system.
items.why: The system is hyper-optimised for marketing on this platform.
items.when: All paid social creative planning for Meta.

items.title: A new creative must be at least 3 moves away from the nearest live creative of the same {brand} account-wide,…
items.text: A new creative must be at least 3 moves away from the nearest live creative of the same {brand} account-wide, across persona (sub-avatar + desire), awareness level, angle, format/structure, face/talent, setting and visual style; 0-1 moves is a variation Meta groups with the original, 2 is risky.
items.why: Meta's Andromeda groups ads that look or feel alike as variations of the same creative and shares delivery between them.
items.when: Scoring a new brief or ad before anything is made.

items.title: Treat hook text, caption, CTA or music swaps as iteration, allowed only inside a creative that already counts…
items.text: Treat hook text, caption, CTA or music swaps as iteration, allowed only inside a creative that already counts as new; they never replace true creative diversification.
items.why: Meta: iteration 'should not replace true creative diversification'.

items.title: Hold one product, one offer page and one core message fixed across every creative and format; diversification…
items.text: Hold one product, one offer page and one core message fixed across every creative and format; diversification happens on the other dimensions.
items.why: The offer and core message never vary; only the creative moves.

items.title: Run fewer ads per ad set, each a flexible ad holding up to 10 diverse assets, never more than 50 ads per ad…
items.text: Run fewer ads per ad set, each a flexible ad holding up to 10 diverse assets, never more than 50 ads per ad set.
items.why: Meta: decrease ads per ad set but keep diverse assets per ad set.

items.title: A new creative must use an image or video not already shown anywhere on the {brand}'s Page.
items.text: A new creative must use an image or video not already shown anywhere on the {brand}'s Page.
items.why: Meta counts fatigue across all recent exposures of the image or video, including other campaigns on the Page.

items.title: Put music or voiceover on every Reel, keep key messages inside the 9:16 safe zone, and run {creator} content…
items.text: Put music or voiceover on every Reel, keep key messages inside the 9:16 safe zone, and run {creator} content as partnership ads.
items.why: Meta reports up to 13% more incremental conversions with sound, 34.5% lower cost per result for 9:16 with audio, and 19% lower acquisition cost for partnership ads.

items.title: Diagnose creative fatigue by cost per result against past ads: above past ads but under 2x is…
items.text: Diagnose creative fatigue by cost per result against past ads: above past ads but under 2x is creative-limited; 2x or more is fatigued and needs a materially different image or video.
items.why: These are Meta's own fatigue thresholds.

items.title: Run text and headline variants as separate assets inside one flexible ad so the platform scores each piece's…
items.text: Run text and headline variants as separate assets inside one flexible ad so the platform scores each piece's spend and purchases, then mix and match the best elements.
items.why: Meta breaks one ad's results down by asset, giving each section swap its own score.
items.when: Testing copy and section variants on Meta.

items.title: Market sophistication is read on every creative and must match the {brand}'s stage; it is not a…
items.text: Market sophistication is read on every creative and must match the {brand}'s stage; it is not a diversification move.
items.why: The market sits at one stage of sophistication.

items.title: Paid or outbound work runs only when a person presses for it; approval is a recorded decision, and nothing…
items.text: Paid or outbound work runs only when a person presses for it; approval is a recorded decision, and nothing executes on its own.
items.why: Spend and sends are human acts.
items.when: Any queue of creative or outbound work.

items.title: Every ad request starts as one ask record carrying {brand}, product, avatar, sub-avatar, funnel stage, the…
items.text: Every ad request starts as one ask record carrying {brand}, product, avatar, sub-avatar, funnel stage, the exact offer lines allowed and never allowed, the moment and its window, the count and who makes it, so no later step asks again what it is for.
items.why: One sentence should be enough to activate the workflows.

items.title: Anything the requester did not say is looked up in the {brand}'s files (offer bank, moment calendar), never…
items.text: Anything the requester did not say is looked up in the {brand}'s files (offer bank, moment calendar), never invented; a fact not found is left empty and reported.
items.why: Invented offer lines or dates ship wrong ads.

items.title: Until the system is producing standout ads, every brief passes manual owner gates: sign-off on the swipes,…
items.text: Until the system is producing standout ads, every brief passes manual owner gates: sign-off on the swipes, reading the sub-avatar, checking every brief, picking the concepts and checking each picture alone. Automation fills the space between gates and never removes one.
items.why: Until you're popping out banger ads, briefs need manual checks to stay pristine.
items.when: The ad workflow from ask to handoff.

items.title: Default swipe mix per ask is 3 paid plus 3 organic, and only what passed the brief check is handed to the…
items.text: Default swipe mix per ask is 3 paid plus 3 organic, and only what passed the brief check is handed to the maker.
items.why: Balanced sourcing and only checked briefs reach makers.

items.title: Find paid swipes by velocity, not copy count alone: sort by new copies in the last 7 days, require 5+ copies,…
items.text: Find paid swipes by velocity, not copy count alone: sort by new copies in the last 7 days, require 5+ copies, 14+ days running and still active, image or video, affiliate or brand, in English-speaking markets by default.
items.why: Velocity shows what is still picking up spend; 5+ copies is above the median of 4.
items.when: Sourcing paid ad swipes from ad libraries.

items.title: Search swipes with keywords taken from the avatar's own words and in categories from the avatar's affinity…
items.text: Search swipes with keywords taken from the avatar's own words and in categories from the avatar's affinity groups (what else they buy and from whom); never a seed list or a category picked by feel.
items.why: The avatar's language and buying habits define where winning creative lives.

items.title: Every brief reads the newest core avatar plus the named sub-avatar's newest profile; a brief drafted before…
items.text: Every brief reads the newest core avatar plus the named sub-avatar's newest profile; a brief drafted before the newest profile existed is re-run before review, and the ask's own offer lines, never-list and deadline override the general offer bank.
items.why: Briefs must always use the most up-to-date avatar; without the ask's offer a brief dropped the deadline.

items.title: Every brief comes out of the chain, never freehand, in one standard brief document with the same sections in…
items.text: Every brief comes out of the chain, never freehand, in one standard brief document with the same sections in the same order and every decision for the owner listed and numbered at the end.
items.why: A standardized briefing document literally.

items.title: Build each missing piece of the system when a real request hits it, not before.
items.text: Build each missing piece of the system when a real request hits it, not before.
items.why: Leverage over speculative setup.
items.when: Deciding what tooling to build next.

items.title: Count only customer-started support tickets in support metrics; exclude notifications, phishing, bounces and…
items.text: Count only customer-started support tickets in support metrics; exclude notifications, phishing, bounces and agent-started tickets.
items.why: Two thirds of tickets on the account are noise, so any count without the filter is inflated.

items.title: Publish weekly metrics for complete weeks only, compute rates on totals rather than averaging weekly rates,…
items.text: Publish weekly metrics for complete weeks only, compute rates on totals rather than averaging weekly rates, and record a missing value as null, never zero.
items.why: A partial week reads as a collapse that has not happened, the mean of weekly rates is not the rate, and null is not zero.

items.title: Pin a metric's denominator to the same filter every other team number uses (for orders: paid and revenue…
items.text: Pin a metric's denominator to the same filter every other team number uses (for orders: paid and revenue above zero) so ratios are comparable.
items.why: Tickets per 100 orders must compare with every other number the team reads.

items.title: Read support tags as what agents tagged, not what happened, and remember a support inbox measures objections…
items.text: Read support tags as what agents tagged, not what happened, and remember a support inbox measures objections well and desire badly.
items.why: An untagged reason reads as zero, and early weeks after a taxonomy change measure adoption.
items.when: Using support data for research or decisions.

items.title: Customer-service reporting publishes aggregates only: no email, name, address, order id, ticket id or message…
items.text: Customer-service reporting publishes aggregates only: no email, name, address, order id, ticket id or message text in any output.
items.why: Standing PII rule.
items.when: Any report built from customer data.

items.title: Read every swipe for its culture: what its people recognise, the references, slang, double meanings, the joke…
items.text: Read every swipe for its culture: what its people recognise, the references, slang, double meanings, the joke in its words and same-kind jokes; a joke the read marks load-bearing stays in every variation.
items.why: A captioned swipe read without culture looked like nonsense; one shared culture read feeds both image and video.
items.when: Image and video swipe teardowns and the writing that follows.

items.title: When one concept needs several ads, write genuinely different versions (awareness, format, face, setting,…
items.text: When one concept needs several ads, write genuinely different versions (awareness, format, face, setting, look), with every pair 3+ moves apart and none copying what is running; six hooks on one ad count as one creative.
items.why: Meta groups ads that look or feel alike into one creative.
items.when: Expanding one concept or brief into multiple ads.

items.title: Every format, style, structure, framework, placement and doctrine value a tool uses must be on its defined…
items.text: Every format, style, structure, framework, placement and doctrine value a tool uses must be on its defined list, and an unknown value is refused with the real options named; every entry stays draft until the owner signs it.
items.why: Elements were not enforced; everything needs to be green light.
items.when: Any production run choosing creative elements.

items.title: Design every email like a short landing page: each send gets a defined format (a stack of fixed sections with…
items.text: Design every email like a short landing page: each send gets a defined format (a stack of fixed sections with a fixed picture count) chosen from its send type.
items.why: Emails are basically many landing pages, and the format fixes how many pictures must be made.

items.title: Every email is either a design email or a letter, never both: design emails (spotlights, offers, objections,…
items.text: Every email is either a design email or a letter, never both: design emails (spotlights, offers, objections, guarantee) carry 5-8 pictures, no block over 30 words and about 90 words in all; letters (VIP thanks, mission, asking for stories) carry one photo hero, 3-4 short paragraphs and about 120 words, ending on one button and one ask.
items.why: The two kinds do different jobs and mixing them blurs both.

items.title: Source email pictures in this order: the real product cut out, brand photos you own, real customer proof as…
items.text: Source email pictures in this order: the real product cut out, brand photos you own, real customer proof as it is (never made), and only then a picture made from a real reference for what nothing owned shows; never make a product or person from words alone.
items.why: Heroes made from the writer's words alone came out generic.

items.title: Before-and-after and proof pictures are always real customer results shown as they are, never generated.
items.text: Before-and-after and proof pictures are always real customer results shown as they are, never generated.
items.why: Proof must be real.
items.when: Proof sections in emails and ads.

items.title: In email design: a headline is followed straight away by its picture and a badge or seal never opens; one…
items.text: In email design: a headline is followed straight away by its picture and a badge or seal never opens; one price, one offer, one button; lead with the page price with the one-delivery price struck through; never invent a deadline.
items.why: Rules from the owner's design reviews.

items.title: No customer face appears twice in a week (once a month at most), a customer's words appear only with that…
items.text: No customer face appears twice in a week (once a month at most), a customer's words appear only with that customer's own face, and no customer photo or made scene repeats across the week's emails.
items.why: Repeated faces read as recycled; mismatched quotes and faces are false.

items.title: Borrow a format, never a person: a homage shows no face, and the villain is the problem.
items.text: Borrow a format, never a person: a homage shows no face, and the villain is the problem.
items.why: Using real people's likeness is off-limits; the problem is the enemy.

items.title: Show the product behaving like itself and only as sold; never show an accessory sold separately as if it were…
items.text: Show the product behaving like itself and only as sold; never show an accessory sold separately as if it were in the box, and rewrite any brief that names the product in a form it never takes.
items.why: Product truth must match what the customer receives.
items.when: Any product picture in emails or ads.

items.title: An email subject names the concept, not the product, and the body under it is two or three short lines.
items.text: An email subject names the concept, not the product, and the body under it is two or three short lines.
items.why: From the owner's design reviews.

items.title: Every email gets one concept from the reader's culture map (a borrowed format, never a person); hold any…
items.text: Every email gets one concept from the reader's culture map (a borrowed format, never a person); hold any email without both a concept and its culture source.
items.why: Emails must never be generic.

items.title: Build emails in gated steps, each starting only after the one before has its OK: job card (reader, one job,…
items.text: Build emails in gated steps, each starting only after the one before has its OK: job card (reader, one job, one belief, proof, one action, how we'll know), concept, phone-scale wireframe, pictures, product check, then build; design starts only on finished copy.
items.why: A step starts only when the one before it has its OK.

items.title: An email passes the final check before approval: every link returns 200, subject and preview set, unsubscribe…
items.text: An email passes the final check before approval: every link returns 200, subject and preview set, unsubscribe and preference tags present, alt text on every picture, no picture over 1MB and the whole email under 2.5MB, no never-use names, product check passed, send day still ahead.
items.why: Broken or oversized emails cannot reach the list.
items.when: Before an email is approved or scheduled.

items.title: Every price in ad copy, an email or a text must be one the offer bank sells today for that offer, and no…
items.text: Every price in ad copy, an email or a text must be one the offer bank sells today for that offer, and no unfilled placeholder may remain; a failure holds the work before it is handed on, and prices are never ruled past: the offer bank is fixed instead.
items.why: The first email sold a size the store no longer carried; wrong prices cannot reach a buyer.

items.title: Never invent a fact in email or SMS copy: no number, timeframe, guarantee term or named quote that is not in…
items.text: Never invent a fact in email or SMS copy: no number, timeframe, guarantee term or named quote that is not in the {brand}'s files; state counts exactly as filed, credit quotes as filed, say guarantee lines word for word, and write around or mark any missing fact.
items.why: Invented facts reached drafts.

items.title: Copy stating a saving or subscribed price must state the condition that saving depends on, and an older…
items.text: Copy stating a saving or subscribed price must state the condition that saving depends on, and an older was-price from a product file is never used.
items.why: A saving without its condition misleads.
items.when: Offer copy in email, SMS and subject lines.

items.title: A quote credited to a customer must actually come from a buyer; a line from a forum or video site credited to…
items.text: A quote credited to a customer must actually come from a buyer; a line from a forum or video site credited to a customer holds the email, and each credit says where it came from.
items.why: Mis-credited quotes are false testimonials.

items.title: Check a send's readiness before spending anything on it: its product and offer product in stock as a shopper…
items.text: Check a send's readiness before spending anything on it: its product and offer product in stock as a shopper sees it, an offer the bank allows on that day, and a calendar slot that binds; a send that is not ready is not written.
items.why: Spend nothing on emails for sold-out products or dead offers.
items.when: Before producing a batch of emails.

items.title: An SMS goes only with its email: every version of the email it follows must be approved or scheduled first.
items.text: An SMS goes only with its email: every version of the email it follows must be approved or scheduled first.
items.why: The text points to the email's offer and link.

items.title: Emails and texts are only ever scheduled on the owner's approval, at least 30 minutes ahead, after every…
items.text: Emails and texts are only ever scheduled on the owner's approval, at least 30 minutes ahead, after every check re-runs and the content matches what was approved; never send now and never from a batch job.
items.why: Sending is the owner's call.

items.title: An offer whose page is marked hidden is written and carded but cannot be approved until the page is opened.
items.text: An offer whose page is marked hidden is written and carded but cannot be approved until the page is opened.
items.why: No send may point to a page that is not live.

items.title: Every link to the {brand}'s own sites in an email carries the tracking standard's tags (source, medium,…
items.text: Every link to the {brand}'s own sites in an email carries the tracking standard's tags (source, medium, campaign = send, content = section, term = segment) so funnel data stitches end to end; an untagged own link holds the email.
items.why: Stitch funnel data end to end.

items.title: Never pad a thin category of emails; a thin category is a finding to call out.
items.text: Never pad a thin category of emails; a thin category is a finding to call out.
items.why: Padding hides gaps.

items.title: When swiping an email, write from its message only; never carry the source's page furniture (logo row, nav,…
items.text: When swiping an email, write from its message only; never carry the source's page furniture (logo row, nav, social row, footer, legal) or its defects into the new email.
items.why: The old email's furniture must never reach the writer.

items.title: After one fix round, any flagged sentence that still fails is cut, not rewritten again; the headline, offer…
items.text: After one fix round, any flagged sentence that still fails is cut, not rewritten again; the headline, offer line, button and lines on file word for word are never cut.
items.why: Stops endless rewrite loops while protecting the load-bearing lines.

items.title: Every correction from a review becomes a stored DO or NEVER rule that every later copy step, design prompt…
items.text: Every correction from a review becomes a stored DO or NEVER rule that every later copy step, design prompt and picture reads.
items.why: Every shift made with feedback needs to be stored and reused.
items.when: Owner reviews of emails and creative.

items.title: Retry only what failed in a batch, never the whole batch; a held item is waiting on a ruling and is not a…
items.text: Retry only what failed in a batch, never the whole batch; a held item is waiting on a ruling and is not a failure.
items.why: Re-running everything wastes spend.

items.title: Collect customer feedback with one question at a time, per customer stage, triggered from email flows; never…
items.text: Collect customer feedback with one question at a time, per customer stage, triggered from email flows; never ask what the flow already knows (order count, subscription, purchase status), and file every answer by stage and business area so it is searchable.
items.why: Feedback should go straight into the system, filed properly and really searchable.

items.title: Only open-text answers count as customer language; taps and scores ride alongside as signals, and test…
items.text: Only open-text answers count as customer language; taps and scores ride alongside as signals, and test submissions are marked and excluded.
items.why: Choices and scores are not the customer's words.
items.when: Turning survey answers into the language bank.

items.title: A feedback page never passes the customer's email to an ad platform: it loads no pixels or tag managers and…
items.text: A feedback page never passes the customer's email to an ad platform: it loads no pixels or tag managers and strips the email from the address.
items.why: Customer contact data must not leak to ad platforms.

items.title: Every Meta ad carries the standard URL tags in its URL-parameters field (source, medium, campaign, ad set, ad…
items.text: Every Meta ad carries the standard URL tags in its URL-parameters field (source, medium, campaign, ad set, ad name in utm_content, ad id also in sub1), never typed into the website link; the ad name is the key every report joins on.
items.why: The store keeps only certain tags on the order, so the ad name and id must ride in those.

items.title: Judge the business and every ad on contribution (revenue minus tax, refunds, product cost, freight,…
items.text: Judge the business and every ad on contribution (revenue minus tax, refunds, product cost, freight, fulfilment and fees, order by order), not on what the pixel reports.
items.why: Break-even should be focused on actual contribution, not what the pixel has picked up.

items.title: Judge live ads by what the store actually received (orders carrying the ad's tags), not by the ad platform's…
items.text: Judge live ads by what the store actually received (orders carrying the ad's tags), not by the ad platform's own reporting.
items.why: The store's own orders are the truth table.

items.title: Call each ad against its funnel's break-even CPA: under 1x break-even spent is too early; no funnel order by…
items.text: Call each ad against its funnel's break-even CPA: under 1x break-even spent is too early; no funnel order by 2x break-even spent, turn it off; at 3x spent with CPA over 1.5x, turn it off; 3+ purchases at CPA up to 0.8x, double down; CPA up to 1.2x, keep; otherwise watch.
items.why: These are the starting lines every ad is judged by (draft, brand desks may set their own).

items.title: Measure what ads add at brand level from periods where spend changed, using any ads-off stretch (under $25 a…
items.text: Measure what ads add at brand level from periods where spend changed, using any ads-off stretch (under $25 a day for 7+ days) as the baseline, and report contribution added per $1 of spend.
items.why: Shows the real incremental value of ad spend.

items.title: Send upsells as their own event, never as a Purchase, so the platform's purchase count stays one per order;…
items.text: Send upsells as their own event, never as a Purchase, so the platform's purchase count stays one per order; track upsell revenue by ad through a custom conversion.
items.why: Upsells counted as purchases inflate conversions.

items.title: Every funnel event carries the ad's attribution (ad name, brief, batch, campaign, ad set, ad id) plus funnel,…
items.text: Every funnel event carries the ad's attribution (ad name, brief, batch, campaign, ad set, ad id) plus funnel, page and step, kept for the visit and 7 days; no email, name or phone is ever sent.
items.why: Each step must be traceable to the ad that brought the visitor.

items.title: Prove a funnel meets the tracking standard before and after any change to it.
items.text: Prove a funnel meets the tracking standard before and after any change to it.
items.why: Tracking breaks silently with page changes.

items.title: Every dollar amount, cutoff hour, transit-day count and closed day on a live funnel's offer box must match…
items.text: Every dollar amount, cutoff hour, transit-day count and closed day on a live funnel's offer box must match the offer bank and the shipping file.
items.why: Offer and shipping claims must be true to the owner files.

items.title: Nothing reaches or changes the ad account without the owner's explicit approval: finished ads wait in a check…
items.text: Nothing reaches or changes the ad account without the owner's explicit approval: finished ads wait in a check folder until he approves, and calls such as turn off, budget up or keep are recorded only until he says go.
items.why: Anything with Meta needs to be very careful.

items.title: Hook versions change only the opening scene's picture: the audio stays the master's on the same beat, no…
items.text: Hook versions change only the opening scene's picture: the audio stays the master's on the same beat, no price or offer in the hook, captions sit in the bottom band and headlines in the top; for a wordless swipe vary picture, motion, caption or sound, never a spoken line. Default 4 hook versions with a set spend cap.
items.why: A hook test must isolate the opening.
items.when: Making hook versions of a video ad.

items.title: Credit a repeat order to an email by its own email tags, the email platform's attribution, or a click in the…
items.text: Credit a repeat order to an email by its own email tags, the email platform's attribution, or a click in the 5 days before the order.
items.why: Gives retention email a consistent credit rule across the journey.

items.title: Keep one registry that says which model does which generative job; no tool writes its own model choice, and…
items.text: Keep one registry that says which model does which generative job; no tool writes its own model choice, and changing a model is one change there that every tool follows.
items.why: Separates model choice from the workflow so it can be adjusted in one place.
items.when: Building any tool that makes pictures, clips, voices or sounds.

items.title: A tool always uses the house default model for a job and never picks another on its own, for cost or because…
items.text: A tool always uses the house default model for a job and never picks another on its own, for cost or because a key is missing; only a person's explicit pick changes it, and an unavailable pick is refused, never silently swapped. Cost is never a reason to pick a model the house does not name.
items.why: Silent swaps make run records lie and quality drift.
items.when: Model selection in any generative tool.

items.title: Use the backup model only when the default refuses a picture or clip you are allowed to make, fails its…
items.text: Use the backup model only when the default refuses a picture or clip you are allowed to make, fails its takes, or is down; keep the same prompt and references, and record which model made each asset.
items.why: Backups exist for failure, not preference, and provenance must stay clear.

items.title: A scene the swipe holds as one continuous take is made as one continuous clip, and its motion is read and…
items.text: A scene the swipe holds as one continuous take is made as one continuous clip, and its motion is read and approved before the take is paid for.
items.why: Paying for takes before motion is right wastes credits; one take keeps the scene continuous.

items.title: Make every voice line as its own read with that shot's delivery, never one long take for the whole piece;…
items.text: Make every voice line as its own read with that shot's delivery, never one long take for the whole piece; narrated pieces are the exception and get one stitched storyteller read.
items.why: Per-line reads carry the right delivery; narration read flat and staccato when split.

items.title: A talking clip is generated with its start picture and the line's own voice read in one call, so nothing is…
items.text: A talking clip is generated with its start picture and the line's own voice read in one call, so nothing is re-voiced afterwards; if a backup model cannot take audio, lay the clip over its locked read rather than lip-syncing.
items.why: Generating picture and voice together keeps sync.

items.title: Make the song in a song ad by hand in the best dedicated song generator; the chain writes its inputs and…
items.text: Make the song in a song ad by hand in the best dedicated song generator; the chain writes its inputs and gates the take.
items.why: For all song ads, the dedicated song tool is the best.

items.title: Never trust automatic speaker labels alone outside English; merge them with the heard lines.
items.text: Never trust automatic speaker labels alone outside English; merge them with the heard lines.
items.why: Speech tools drop or mistranslate non-English speech.

items.title: Make variations and fixes of an approved picture as edits off that picture, never as fresh generations; the…
items.text: Make variations and fixes of an approved picture as edits off that picture, never as fresh generations; the edit instruction carries only the change and never describes what the reference already shows.
items.why: Generating from a description gave wrong wardrobe and blended faces; a delta-only edit held the scene.
items.when: Picture variations, fixes and video frame adjustments.

items.title: One change per edit (two at a push), and an edit instruction over 400 characters is refused because it has…
items.text: One change per edit (two at a push), and an edit instruction over 400 characters is refused because it has started describing the scene.
items.why: Five changes in one sentence come back wrong and nothing says which one did it.

items.title: Every edited picture is judged against its reference on two tests, the change is present and nothing else…
items.text: Every edited picture is judged against its reference on two tests, the change is present and nothing else moved; a result that moved anything else is held and never delivered, and a judge that did not run is a hold, never a pass.
items.why: Edits that drift break the approved picture.

items.title: Every reference picture has a keep/change split: what is load-bearing never moves, and the one change may…
items.text: Every reference picture has a keep/change split: what is load-bearing never moves, and the one change may touch only what is swappable.
items.why: Defines what an edit is allowed to touch.

items.title: Never let an image model generate or fix on-image text; set type over a clean plate, and change wrong words…
items.text: Never let an image model generate or fix on-image text; set type over a clean plate, and change wrong words in the type layer.
items.why: Models redraw labels and headlines every roll; composited type is exact and free.

items.title: When an edit touches a banked product or element, attach that real reference picture to the edit.
items.text: When an edit touches a banked product or element, attach that real reference picture to the edit.
items.why: Attaching the real product photo stopped the label garbling on most rolls.

items.title: Make every picture 9:16 from the start with the centre 4:5 as the safe zone; never outpaint or reframe it…
items.text: Make every picture 9:16 from the start with the centre 4:5 as the safe zone; never outpaint or reframe it afterwards.
items.why: One frame for every placement, with no lossy finishing.

items.title: Every variation runs through the same production path as the original picture, never a side path, and the…
items.text: Every variation runs through the same production path as the original picture, never a side path, and the original is never overwritten; each result is a new version.
items.why: Everything needs to go through the same path to get the same level of output.

items.title: Hand off only briefs from the chain's final stage, addressed to a role (graphic designer, video editor),…
items.text: Hand off only briefs from the chain's final stage, addressed to a role (graphic designer, video editor), never to a named person.
items.why: Earlier-stage briefs are incomplete; roles outlast people.

items.title: Never let an image model draw the product: render it from its 3D model in a pose the product can actually…
items.text: Never let an image model draw the product: render it from its 3D model in a pose the product can actually take, sized from its real measurements against a known object in the scene, never by eye.
items.why: The image model kept drawing the product wrong, standing it on a base it cannot stand on and changing its shape.

items.title: An ad that shows the brand mark shows the real logo file placed on the picture; the image model never draws…
items.text: An ad that shows the brand mark shows the real logo file placed on the picture; the image model never draws the logo.
items.why: Generated logos are wrong.

items.title: Product pictures follow the {brand}'s product-picture standard for their kind (ground, framing, light, label…
items.text: Product pictures follow the {brand}'s product-picture standard for their kind (ground, framing, light, label and bundle rules), measured before filing.
items.why: Store and offer pictures need one consistent standard.

items.title: A picture variation is the 3D set changed and printed again, one print per picture variation; a words-only…
items.text: A picture variation is the 3D set changed and printed again, one print per picture variation; a words-only variation is the same plate with new words.
items.why: Variations stay true to the set and cost only one print.

items.title: Use one image model for every picture in a batch, fresh or edit, person or object.
items.text: Use one image model for every picture in a batch, fresh or edit, person or object.
items.why: One look across a batch, one set of quirks, one prompt style makes all the work easier.

items.title: Keep real source material (photography, product video, CGI) separate from anything generated; nothing…
items.text: Keep real source material (photography, product video, CGI) separate from anything generated; nothing generated ever enters the source set, and where a render and the source disagree, the source wins.
items.why: The source shows what the product actually is.

items.title: When remaking a swipe with a person in it, generate a different person (different face, structure and…
items.text: When remaking a swipe with a person in it, generate a different person (different face, structure and hairstyle) at the same age, pose, distance and expression; never pin one face across many ads.
items.why: Pinning one photo put the same face on 21 ads; the remake must fit the original without copying the person.

items.title: Keep the swipe's medium: an illustration comes back drawn, a photo as a photo, an animated 3D look as…
items.text: Keep the swipe's medium: an illustration comes back drawn, a photo as a photo, an animated 3D look as animated 3D; a person in a drawn swipe is drawn in that style, never a photo of the cast person, while the product stays the real product.
items.why: A cartoon swipe came out as a photo of the cast person.

items.title: In a swipe remake, move the proof (inset, zoom, before/after) onto the skin or body area the {offer} is…
items.text: In a swipe remake, move the proof (inset, zoom, before/after) onto the skin or body area the {offer} is actually for, fill every price, guarantee and discount slot the swipe carries from the offer bank (nothing invented, nothing dropped), and swap the swipe's accent colour for the {brand}'s.
items.why: Drafts missed the offer and a guarantee, used off-brand text colour, and showed proof on the wrong skin.

items.title: Put the product into a remake only where the swipe shows a product, rendered into the scene at the swipe's…
items.text: Put the product into a remake only where the swipe shows a product, rendered into the scene at the swipe's angle (never the same pasted cutout), showing the range where the swipe shows several; competitor products shown for comparison stay.
items.why: The same product cutout was used over and over regardless of the original's subject.

items.title: An organic swipe with no adult in it is remade as its own version of the same photo: no person added, no…
items.text: An organic swipe with no adult in it is remade as its own version of the same photo: no person added, no product, no words; the {brand} stays out of the picture.
items.why: A doodle stays a doodle; the brand not being in the picture is the point of that swipe.

items.title: A picture judge checks verifiable facts (an invented product, the wrong subject, a cloned bystander, an unset…
items.text: A picture judge checks verifiable facts (an invented product, the wrong subject, a cloned bystander, an unset price), not taste, and does not fail a picture for things the owner would not reject.
items.why: Every reject in the standard-setting run was a checkable fact.

items.title: To run a new product or offer on swipes already torn down, reuse the brand-free teardown and replication spec…
items.text: To run a new product or offer on swipes already torn down, reuse the brand-free teardown and replication spec unchanged and re-run only the stages where product and offer enter (injection, headlines, variations, brief).
items.why: The teardown does not know what we sell, so only the brand-side stages need redoing.
items.when: Launching a new product or offer on existing swipe work.

items.title: Lock the draft standard once ruled; any change to its steps or prompts is a change to a ruling and needs the…
items.text: Lock the draft standard once ruled; any change to its steps or prompts is a change to a ruling and needs the owner's word first.
items.why: This is the standard we operate with; do not deviate.

items.title: Make each picture variation as one edit per variation, one call each, and never invent variations for a brief…
items.text: Make each picture variation as one edit per variation, one call each, and never invent variations for a brief that wrote none; a refused call is retried alone before it is believed.
items.why: Bundled calls overwrite each other, and burst refusals succeed when retried alone.

items.title: Keep picture variation batches separate from ad copy; a picture stage never waits on copy.
items.text: Keep picture variation batches separate from ad copy; a picture stage never waits on copy.
items.why: A stage that waits on copy is a stage that does not ship pictures.

items.title: Briefs differ by who makes the asset and what it is: an AI brief, a {creator} static brief and a creator…
items.text: Briefs differ by who makes the asset and what it is: an AI brief, a {creator} static brief and a creator video brief are different documents built from the same teardown.
items.why: A creator video brief is different than an AI video brief, and a creator static brief is different than a creator video brief.

items.title: Make pictures the plain way by default: one call with the swipe, the brand's swaps and words, and the…
items.text: Make pictures the plain way by default: one call with the swipe, the brand's swaps and words, and the product's real in-use pictures, without layers of extra control.
items.why: Too much control was messing results up; the plain way was far better.

items.title: Aim every remake at the run's creative-control preset (default maxed), reading the swipe's level on every…
items.text: Aim every remake at the run's creative-control preset (default maxed), reading the swipe's level on every dial first, and never go below the never-sterile floor; every headline is one idea that reads cold.
items.why: Sterile output is the failure.

items.title: Work unaware and problem-aware ads first in the shared static-ad work list; a sterile or failed ad goes back…
items.text: Work unaware and problem-aware ads first in the shared static-ad work list; a sterile or failed ad goes back on the list and is held after 3 tries.
items.why: Top-of-funnel ads come first, and stuck ads must not loop forever.

items.title: A picture counts as done only after a side-by-side check against the swipe confirms its style, layout, words…
items.text: A picture counts as done only after a side-by-side check against the swipe confirms its style, layout, words and product.
items.why: Style drift from the swipe slipped through.

items.title: A static ad batch is the approved picture plus exactly 5 unique variations, each one change off the approved…
items.text: A static ad batch is the approved picture plus exactly 5 unique variations, each one change off the approved picture and each carrying one of the headline set's variation headlines word for word.
items.why: 6 total images in a batch: 5 unique variations from the initial one.

items.title: Until the system runs full auto, no picture is generated from words the owner has not approved; the copy is…
items.text: Until the system runs full auto, no picture is generated from words the owner has not approved; the copy is reviewed first, and variations vary the approved headline, keeping its shape and reading cold.
items.why: Copy needs sauce before images are made; awareness, verbatims and spice are the foundation.
items.when: Before any static ad picture is generated.
