items.title: Pull customer language for the ad's own avatar at the swipe's awareness level, never the top rows across all…
items.text: Pull customer language for the ad's own avatar at the swipe's awareness level, never the top rows across all avatars, and on a problem-aware ad name the problem in the customer's own word for it.
items.why: A fallback to all avatars put an acne story on a dark-spots ad.

items.title: Every headline is the concept talking, with one named spice device, and never a calendar announcement; the…
items.text: Every headline is the concept talking, with one named spice device, and never a calendar announcement; the moment's name belongs on a prop in the scene, not in the headline.
items.why: Headlines must play the concept, not announce a date.

items.title: Write each picture variation as a change to the 3D set (object, real size in cm, place, material) inside the…
items.text: Write each picture variation as a change to the 3D set (object, real size in cm, place, material) inside the approved concept; the product always stays its true size and the sign on a prop never changes.
items.why: Set changes can be re-printed exactly; scaling the product breaks true size.

items.title: Treat where a swipe came from (paid, organic, own, competitor) as a field, not a separate tool: read every…
items.text: Treat where a swipe came from (paid, organic, own, competitor) as a field, not a separate tool: read every saved swipe into one list, each routed by asset kind to its teardown (video, image/carousel, copy, landing page, email).
items.why: Splitting organic and paid swipes into separate systems fragments the work.

items.title: Never guess a swipe's kind, format or route: an unknown is counted and left unrouted, an empty format stays…
items.text: Never guess a swipe's kind, format or route: an unknown is counted and left unrouted, an empty format stays empty, and a swipe whose asset cannot be found is reported, never dropped.
items.why: Guessed labels create a second vocabulary that drifts.

items.title: File customer language by relationship first (an order on file is a customer, refunded or lapsed is churned);…
items.text: File customer language by relationship first (an order on file is a customer, refunded or lapsed is churned); otherwise by the words: owning or using the product is an assumed customer, interest in getting it is a lead, and everything else is a prospect.
items.why: Language that does not speak to being a customer should be a prospect; this keeps the system clean and drives awareness indexing.
items.when: Filing rows into a {brand}'s language bank.

items.title: Label every customer-language row with the awareness level and market-sophistication signal its speaker's own…
items.text: Label every customer-language row with the awareness level and market-sophistication signal its speaker's own words show, quoting the words that show it, and read each row in its context (source, question, speaker, lane), not the words alone.
items.why: No row said what its speaker knows, so a solution-aware hook was handed problem rows; short answers read alone came back unclear.
items.when: Building or backfilling a language bank.

items.title: A buyer's words are most-aware (or product-aware where they show doubt), and someone who has only tried a…
items.text: A buyer's words are most-aware (or product-aware where they show doubt), and someone who has only tried a competitor's product is solution-aware, not product-aware.
items.why: 'The product' in the awareness doctrine means our product.
items.when: Assigning awareness levels to customer language.

items.title: Keep internal customer language (surveys, tickets, DMs, own database) labelled apart from external language…
items.text: Keep internal customer language (surveys, tickets, DMs, own database) labelled apart from external language (public comments, forums, reviews), and label the brand's own copy as brand voice that never counts as the audience's words.
items.why: Internal customer language is different than forum language, and our own captions must not pose as theirs.

items.title: Write each awareness level from rows at that level: hooks from words at the hook's level, objections from…
items.text: Write each awareness level from rows at that level: hooks from words at the hook's level, objections from product-aware rows, proof and transformation from buyers; a level with no rows is a level you cannot yet write in the customer's words.
items.why: Matching language to the reader's awareness is what makes copy accurate.
items.when: Pulling language for hooks, expansion and close.

items.title: Set a {brand}'s market sophistication stage as one call per brand, and check it against what…
items.text: Set a {brand}'s market sophistication stage as one call per brand, and check it against what customer-language rows say they have already heard (claims, discounted claims, competitor mechanisms, belief in none).
items.why: Rows are evidence for the stage, not the stage itself.

items.title: Before an AI labelling pass runs on a whole dataset, it must agree with a hand-labelled test set (for example…
items.text: Before an AI labelling pass runs on a whole dataset, it must agree with a hand-labelled test set (for example 20 rows per level); it never overwrites a label a person set.
items.why: Automated labels must be proven against human judgment first.

items.title: Pull post comments from TikTok, Instagram and Facebook as the first customer-language sources, each comment…
items.text: Pull post comments from TikTok, Instagram and Facebook as the first customer-language sources, each comment keeping its permalink, likes and pull date, and roll comments on a post that runs as an ad up to that ad.
items.why: Post comments are the first sources and join language to the post's views and spend.

items.title: Run mechanical editing jobs (frame interpolation, upscaling, mattes, tracking, captions, stem separation) on…
items.text: Run mechanical editing jobs (frame interpolation, upscaling, mattes, tracking, captions, stem separation) on free local models, but keep stills and edits where a person's identity must hold through a pose change on the house image model.
items.why: Local models are free and good enough for mechanics, but changed identity in side-by-sides.
items.when: Choosing where an editing job runs.

items.title: List a new model as available only after a real run on your own assets has been logged with its time and…
items.text: List a new model as available only after a real run on your own assets has been logged with its time and memory.
items.why: Claims about a model must come from measured runs on real work.
items.when: Adding AI models to the toolset.

items.title: Build the email calendar from the ground up: real public holidays at their real dates, the {brand}'s own…
items.text: Build the email calendar from the ground up: real public holidays at their real dates, the {brand}'s own cultural moments resolved to real dates, then which segments and avatars are live (every reason citing the record), then sends pinned to those dates, then concepts in order (an offer for every dated ask, then timely concepts, then education).
items.why: Ground up the calendar fundamentally; dates must be real.

items.title: Every offer in the calendar comes from the offer bank, the only place an offer may come from; an offer no…
items.text: Every offer in the calendar comes from the offer bank, the only place an offer may come from; an offer no send can carry is stripped, and a send type the catalogue does not know is dropped, never invented around.
items.why: Invented offers and types ship wrong emails.

items.title: A retail holiday becomes a full arc to the same segment: a build-up scaled by what that holiday earned…
items.text: A retail holiday becomes a full arc to the same segment: a build-up scaled by what that holiday earned before, the ask, and the close; on and after the close only non-asking sends go out.
items.why: Sales need a warm-up and a close to convert.

items.title: A cultural moment (a game day, a finale, a parade) gets one send on the day or the day before and is never…
items.text: A cultural moment (a game day, a finale, a parade) gets one send on the day or the day before and is never sold; only a sale warms up for days ahead.
items.why: Culture sends earn attention, not sales.

items.title: Inside holiday sale windows send 2-3 emails a day (3 on peak days such as Black Friday and Cyber Monday),…
items.text: Inside holiday sale windows send 2-3 emails a day (3 on peak days such as Black Friday and Cyber Monday), every extra send promotional and carrying the period's offer, and open Black Friday at least one week early; outside those windows, one send a day.
items.why: Milk the list on holiday periods and have Black Friday live at least a week ahead.

items.title: Extra holiday sends go only to engaged segments, never to segments that are churned, unengaged, lapsed or…
items.text: Extra holiday sends go only to engaged segments, never to segments that are churned, unengaged, lapsed or sunset.
items.why: No mass sends to the unengaged.

items.title: Each extra send in a holiday period gets its own angle, true for every segment it reaches and held to the…
items.text: Each extra send in a holiday period gets its own angle, true for every segment it reaches and held to the product files and order-by dates; never repeat one argument across all of them.
items.why: 43 holiday sends to six segments, VIPs included, carried the same lead argument.

items.title: For a sale, send VIPs an early-access email the day(s) before the first offer send, and put the last-chance…
items.text: For a sale, send VIPs an early-access email the day(s) before the first offer send, and put the last-chance send on the order-by date when shipping dates govern delivery.
items.why: Rewards the best customers and closes on the real shipping deadline.

items.title: Every week sells something: a week with no offer gets the {brand}'s standing offer on one email.
items.text: Every week sells something: a week with no offer gets the {brand}'s standing offer on one email.
items.why: No week goes by without an ask.

items.title: Plan one partner/affiliate feature a week, every week, when the {brand} has partners on file.
items.text: Plan one partner/affiliate feature a week, every week, when the {brand} has partners on file.
items.why: The affiliate floor keeps partner promotion steady.

items.title: SMS is a companion to email, never standalone: a sale arc gets a text twin on early access, the open, the…
items.text: SMS is a companion to email, never standalone: a sale arc gets a text twin on early access, the open, the moment's own day and the close (same day, audience, offer), sent only to SMS-consented members, outside quiet hours, at most one text a day per segment.
items.why: SMS is part of the strategy, for reminders, engagement and getting responses.

items.title: Send one regular SMS companion per week plus promotional reminders, preferably on Tuesday alongside an…
items.text: Send one regular SMS companion per week plus promotional reminders, preferably on Tuesday alongside an existing email, at least one hour after that email and never on a reminder day.
items.why: A steady weekly text keeps the channel warm without crowding promotions.

items.title: Write each send off a real email whose structure it borrows: the newest of the same type from the {brand}'s…
items.text: Write each send off a real email whose structure it borrows: the newest of the same type from the {brand}'s own sends, else the same category.
items.why: Proven formats beat freehand emails.

items.title: Decide at the calendar which sends are designed emails and which are letters: relationship jobs (asking for a…
items.text: Decide at the calendar which sends are designed emails and which are letters: relationship jobs (asking for a story, the mission, a founder's note, a goodbye, a question back, partner features) are letters; every product argument is designed.
items.why: Mapping and runs must operate on the same principles every two weeks.

items.title: The planner never overwrites or re-approves a person's review decisions, and an unapproved send is never…
items.text: The planner never overwrites or re-approves a person's review decisions, and an unapproved send is never handed on; calendar gates are recorded for review, adoption stays a human act.
items.why: Adoption stays a human act.

items.title: Founder or credential claims in planned sends must come from the {brand}'s own position and story files; a…
items.text: Founder or credential claims in planned sends must come from the {brand}'s own position and story files; a catalogue example is not a founder credential.
items.why: Unsupported credential claims were being planned.

items.title: Default creative stance is absurd, maxed out and hyper-specific; read a swipe's level on every creative dial…
items.text: Default creative stance is absurd, maxed out and hyper-specific; read a swipe's level on every creative dial (intensity, absurdity, humor, specificity, dramatisation, edge, realism, ad-likeness, stopping power) before setting the new piece's levels, using one shared set of dials across copy, video and pictures.
items.why: A real-time matrix of creativity lets every medium be turned up and down in the same language.
items.when: Setting creative direction for any ad.

items.title: Push storytelling, dramatisation and persuasion all the way to the edge, but stay on the right side of a…
items.text: Push storytelling, dramatisation and persuasion all the way to the edge, but stay on the right side of a stated push/never line.
items.why: Amplify creative storytelling and conversion to the edge, ethically.

items.title: Run the same five gates in every marketing chain: inputs, elements, copy, media, delivery.
items.text: Run the same five gates in every marketing chain: inputs, elements, copy, media, delivery. A check only reports, a gate holds failing work, and a person's review is the final say.
items.why: One gate vocabulary across chains means failing work is stopped at the same points everywhere and nothing approves itself.

items.title: Install the same creative QC loop at every stage of every production tool: machine checks, a model review…
items.text: Install the same creative QC loop at every stage of every production tool: machine checks, a model review against what the stage was given and its hard bars, a logged round, the fix at the stage that caused it (a cause that would recur becomes a chain change), then remake only what failed.
items.why: Checking at every stage, not only at the end, is what makes the chain learn and actually work.
items.when: Every creative production tool and stage.

items.title: Keep two layers of checks: in-loop checks that stop or send back one piece, and loop checks on the chain…
items.text: Keep two layers of checks: in-loop checks that stop or send back one piece, and loop checks on the chain itself (is it working, are its prompts and avatar files current).
items.why: A system learns only if the loop itself is audited, not just each output.
items.when: Designing or auditing any production chain.

items.title: A review that cannot run is recorded as unchecked, never as passed, and a review alone never silently stops…
items.text: A review that cannot run is recorded as unchecked, never as passed, and a review alone never silently stops or hides a run.
items.why: An unrun check reported as clean hides failures.

items.title: After writing, run a viewer check: turn the finished brief into what a viewer sees, drop it among 9 real…
items.text: After writing, run a viewer check: turn the finished brief into what a viewer sees, drop it among 9 real posts from {avatar}'s feed, have 5 fresh simulated viewers built from the avatar profile scroll it; viewers only react, code scores against the real posts, and a fail names the part to fix (opening, middle, giveaway, close, audience).
items.why: Judging against the real feed removes taste; 'looks real' is never a score.
items.when: Last step after any brief or script is written.

items.title: Answer each simulated viewer in its own fresh context: a viewer never sees another viewer, the brief or the…
items.text: Answer each simulated viewer in its own fresh context: a viewer never sees another viewer, the brief or the objection bank.
items.why: A viewer that has seen the brief or other reactions is no longer a cold viewer.
items.when: Viewer checks and any panel-style model review.

items.title: Every price in a piece must match {brand}'s offer bank; a person's fact rulings can clear other facts at the…
items.text: Every price in a piece must match {brand}'s offer bank; a person's fact rulings can clear other facts at the gate but never a price.
items.why: Prices are the one fact a ruling must not override.
items.when: Copy gate on any ad, email or page.

items.title: Every link in a send must go to a live product's page (or, on an affiliate send, a partner on the brand's own…
items.text: Every link in a send must go to a live product's page (or, on an affiliate send, a partner on the brand's own roster), and no product that is not live may be named.
items.why: A dead or unrostered money path loses the sale or pays the wrong party.
items.when: Copy and delivery gates on emails and ads.

items.title: A quote's credit (customer, forum, video, follower, panel) must match where the language bank says it was…
items.text: A quote's credit (customer, forum, video, follower, panel) must match where the language bank says it was actually said.
items.why: Mis-crediting a quote is a false claim.
items.when: Any piece quoting customer or community language.

items.title: Keep one marketing doctrine (desire, awareness, sophistication, techniques, sections, mood, close) in one…
items.text: Keep one marketing doctrine (desire, awareness, sophistication, techniques, sections, mood, close) in one place; every prompt binds it by reference and never restates it in its own words.
items.why: A restated framework is a second doctrine that drifts silently.
items.when: Writing or changing any prompt that uses marketing frameworks.

items.title: Every delivery choice (humor, delivery style, register, pacing, reference world) needs a receipt from…
items.text: Every delivery choice (humor, delivery style, register, pacing, reference world) needs a receipt from {avatar}'s own world; a dial with no receipt sits at its plain default and the direction it would have supported is cut.
items.why: Taste that comes from the writer reads as craft but is preference, and nobody downstream can tell.
items.when: Writing and spice passes on any script or ad.

items.title: A reference names a direction for timing, cadence and world, never a likeness or a sound; the voice is always…
items.text: A reference names a direction for timing, cadence and world, never a likeness or a sound; the voice is always a cast voice, cloned then adjusted, with rights on file.
items.why: Imitating a real person's voice or likeness is off-limits.

items.title: Never put humor over a claim: keep jokes out of the proof and offer beats unless the room itself jokes there;…
items.text: Never put humor over a claim: keep jokes out of the proof and offer beats unless the room itself jokes there; the twist may be the product shown working, and a plain proof beat always follows it.
items.why: A joke on a claim undercuts belief.
items.when: Scripts and ads with any humor.

items.title: A planted joke must come from the room: use a meme, format or reference only when the culture read shows this…
items.text: A planted joke must come from the room: use a meme, format or reference only when the culture read shows this audience already laughs at it, and name the receipt; a joke the writer invented is a finding.
items.why: Borrowed in-group humor lands; invented humor reads as an ad.
items.when: Any piece that adds humor not in the swipe.

items.title: The problem may be cast as a character (the bump, the spot, the breakout given a face), always the villain or…
items.text: The problem may be cast as a character (the bump, the spot, the breakout given a face), always the villain or the fool, never the customer.
items.why: Personifying the problem makes it funny without mocking the buyer.

items.title: Set humor on a 0-4 rung (0 straight, 1 problem only, 2 product as a prop, 3 product is the punchline, 4 full…
items.text: Set humor on a 0-4 rung (0 straight, 1 problem only, 2 product as a prop, 3 product is the punchline, 4 full ad wearing the meme) with 0 as default; leave 0 only when the swipe is funny or the culture read names a meme this audience laughs at that the problem fits; rungs 1-2 are organic posts and may carry no product, rungs 3-4 are ads.
items.why: Not every ad is funny; humor is earned by the swipe or the room.
items.when: Concepting any ad or organic post.

items.title: Give every {avatar} a culture map (what they watch, who they trust, references and slang, what they care…
items.text: Give every {avatar} a culture map (what they watch, who they trust, references and slang, what they care about, what they laugh at, what is off-limits) and tag every cultural reference by what it does: laugh, trust, belonging, nostalgia, aspiration, authority, relief, rebellion.
items.why: Culture is the foundation; humor is only one use of it.
items.when: Avatar research and any culture-led creative.

items.title: Write anything that will be voiced for the mouth, not the eye: no em-dash, semicolon, parenthesis or…
items.text: Write anything that will be voiced for the mouth, not the eye: no em-dash, semicolon, parenthesis or ellipsis; one idea per sentence; fragments and contractions allowed; a pause is a full stop or comma; talk to the viewer directly; fillers only at the start of a thought.
items.why: Measured: a voice model added 1.3-1.7 s of silence at every dash, turning a 7 s paragraph into 11 s.
items.when: Every voiceover, spoken script and talking-clip line.

items.title: Colloquialism runs on a 0-4 dial; level 3 slang and level 4 in-group speech are quoted from the room's own…
items.text: Colloquialism runs on a 0-4 dial; level 3 slang and level 4 in-group speech are quoted from the room's own receipted rows, never invented (no row means drop to level 2), and level 4 never sits on the proof, product, offer or call-to-action beats.
items.why: Invented slang reads as cringe; in-group speech on a claim weakens it.
items.when: Scripts and captions written per sub-avatar.

items.title: Where {brand} has measured its own creators' speech (pace, sentence length, fragments, contractions,…
items.text: Where {brand} has measured its own creators' speech (pace, sentence length, fragments, contractions, openers), that measurement defines the spoken band; web sources are only the frame.
items.why: Our own creators who already convert outrank generic research.
items.when: Setting spoken style for any avatar or sub-avatar.

items.title: Strip ad-voice tells and the register the room mocks: no announcer lift at line ends, stacked superlatives,…
items.text: Strip ad-voice tells and the register the room mocks: no announcer lift at line ends, stacked superlatives, too-clean read, sell turn in the first seconds, held smile, or a grade that matches no real room.
items.why: These tells mark a piece as an ad before any claim is heard.
items.when: Delivery direction and review of every video ad.

items.title: In prompts, name a generic person 'the viewer', 'the avatar', 'the speaker' or 'they', never a gendered…
items.text: In prompts, name a generic person 'the viewer', 'the avatar', 'the speaker' or 'they', never a gendered pronoun.
items.why: A gendered pronoun narrows an agnostic system to one reader for no reason.

items.title: Optimize paid social to roughly break even per ad and let the store make the profit: keep an ad on while it…
items.text: Optimize paid social to roughly break even per ad and let the store make the profit: keep an ad on while it spends, makes money, holds CPA in a reasonable range and the store's blended CPA stays solid.
items.why: Ad-level break-even with store-level profit maximizes volume while protecting margin.

items.title: Set each ad's break-even CPA as the store's 30-day contribution per order on that ad's funnel (revenue minus…
items.text: Set each ad's break-even CPA as the store's 30-day contribution per order on that ad's funnel (revenue minus refunds, product, freight, warehousing, card and platform fees, upsells included); a funnel with too few orders falls back to {offer}'s first-order break-even.
items.why: Judging every ad against its own offer's real margin, not a blanket target.

items.title: Store guardrail: if the last 7 days of total store contribution minus total Meta spend is below zero, no…
items.text: Store guardrail: if the last 7 days of total store contribution minus total Meta spend is below zero, no budget goes up anywhere.
items.why: Ad-level wins cannot justify scaling while the store is losing money.

items.title: Judge older ads on their last 7 days and young ads on their whole life.
items.text: Judge older ads on their last 7 days and young ads on their whole life.
items.why: A long-runner's lifetime average hides a bad week.
items.when: Reading ad performance for keep/kill calls.

items.title: Express each desk line as a multiple of the ad's break-even CPA, start lines as drafts tuned from the owner's…
items.text: Express each desk line as a multiple of the ad's break-even CPA, start lines as drafts tuned from the owner's calls, record every call with the flag shown, the suggestion, the decision and the reason, and change the ad account only on the owner's go.
items.why: Recorded calls with reasons let the lines learn; account changes stay a human decision.

items.title: One brief is one flexible ad: all of a brief's finished versions (the control and each hook) go in as that…
items.text: One brief is one flexible ad: all of a brief's finished versions (the control and each hook) go in as that ad's media, and each landing page gets its own copy of the ad.
items.why: Keeps a brief's read in one place and lets the platform rotate versions.

items.title: Ad words come only from the copywriting chain's checked output; never invent copy downstream, and a picture…
items.text: Ad words come only from the copywriting chain's checked output; never invent copy downstream, and a picture with no copy for its format and sub-avatar is left out and listed, never shipped with borrowed words.
items.why: Borrowed or improvised copy breaks the join between creative and results.

items.title: Nothing goes live in the ad account without an approver's click; Approve stays disabled while any machine…
items.text: Nothing goes live in the ad account without an approver's click; Approve stays disabled while any machine check fails, and every imported row lands paused.
items.why: Going live is a human call; failing work must not be approvable.

items.title: Before approval every ad card must pass its checks: media kind and count for its lane, 9:16, at least one…
items.text: Before approval every ad card must pass its checks: media kind and count for its lane, 9:16, at least one primary text and one headline, a valid name, landing pages live and on the funnel list, the card's product equal to the page's product, an open ad set, a campaign, and Page ad-cap headroom.
items.why: Mechanical faults are caught before a human spends attention.

items.title: A disapproval must carry one or more reasons, each naming the upstream step and tool that caused it, plus a…
items.text: A disapproval must carry one or more reasons, each naming the upstream step and tool that caused it, plus a note; the reasons feed back to that step, but no prompt changes from them until the owner has seen the exact text.
items.why: The system learns from rejections without silently rewriting prompts.

items.title: New ads go into existing ad sets (already running, signed new by the owner, or a promo ad set) unless a new…
items.text: New ads go into existing ad sets (already running, signed new by the owner, or a promo ad set) unless a new angle or avatar is clearly defined; the uploader never makes a new ad set on its own.
items.why: Avoids fragmenting budget and learning across needless ad sets.
items.when: Choosing an ad set for a new ad.

items.title: An ad set is one avatar plus one angle and holds many batches; the sub-avatar is not an audience, it picks…
items.text: An ad set is one avatar plus one angle and holds many batches; the sub-avatar is not an audience, it picks the copy and landing page and is read back from ad names and link tracking.
items.why: Sub-avatar ad sets on the same broad audience overlap, compete in one auction and split one budget across many learning phases.

items.title: An ad set earns its own existence only when it buys something genuinely different: a different country, a…
items.text: An ad set earns its own existence only when it buys something genuinely different: a different country, a retargeting pool, a lookalike, or a budget that must be ring-fenced.
items.why: Ad sets are containers, not variables.
items.when: Deciding whether to open a new ad set.

items.title: Where an account does not group ad sets by avatar and angle, every batch gets its own ad set and is never…
items.text: Where an account does not group ad sets by avatar and angle, every batch gets its own ad set and is never added to an old one.
items.why: Clean read (the drop's CPA is the ad set's), clean kill, and no relearning reset on what already works.
items.when: Accounts not structured avatar x angle.

items.title: Split a drop over 50 ads round-robin, not sliced, so every shard holds the same mix of sub-avatars and…
items.text: Split a drop over 50 ads round-robin, not sliced, so every shard holds the same mix of sub-avatars and concepts.
items.why: Sliced shards make shard-vs-shard look like a result when it is an artifact.

items.title: Name a campaign by market, product and funnel only; it persists for months and is compared to its own last…
items.text: Name a campaign by market, product and funnel only; it persists for months and is compared to its own last month, so nothing dated, thematic or batch-specific goes in it, and a second funnel on the same product is a separate campaign.
items.why: A stable campaign is the unit whose CPA is tracked over time.

items.title: Read an account's naming convention off its live campaigns and add only what is missing; never invent a house…
items.text: Read an account's naming convention off its live campaigns and add only what is missing; never invent a house style.
items.why: Accounts differ; a new convention breaks existing reports.
items.when: Naming in an existing ad account.

items.title: Archive dead ads as routine hygiene: paused ads still count against the account's ad limit while archived…
items.text: Archive dead ads as routine hygiene: paused ads still count against the account's ad limit while archived ones do not, and the live-ads-per-Page limit counts only running or in-review ads. Build for the read, not the cap.
items.why: About 20 fully loaded ad sets is the whole live machine; archiving is the release valve.

items.title: An ad made from a paid performance-creator platform's video must carry the creator's id on its link and end…
items.text: An ad made from a paid performance-creator platform's video must carry the creator's id on its link and end its name with it; every creator video submitted is filed as an ad card, no gate.
items.why: Without the tag the creator is unpaid and the sale unattributed.

items.title: A creator video with no brief of its own reuses the words of the newest live ad for its product and points to…
items.text: A creator video with no brief of its own reuses the words of the newest live ad for its product and points to {brand}'s creator funnel.
items.why: New ads reuse proven live copy rather than inventing new words.

items.title: Upload ads with every platform AI creative enhancement turned off.
items.text: Upload ads with every platform AI creative enhancement turned off.
items.why: The approved creative is what runs, unaltered.
items.when: Every ad built through the API.

items.title: Keep nulls null: a day with no spend has no ROAS and shows as a dash, never 0, and is never averaged into a…
items.text: Keep nulls null: a day with no spend has no ROAS and shows as a dash, never 0, and is never averaged into a total.
items.why: A fake zero corrupts every average built on it.

items.title: Recompute ratios (ROAS, CPA, AOV) on totals; never average per-day or per-bucket ratios.
items.text: Recompute ratios (ROAS, CPA, AOV) on totals; never average per-day or per-bucket ratios.
items.why: A quiet day must not weigh the same as the biggest day of the month.

items.title: Sanity-check every data pull: modelled CPA (cost per click divided by conversion rate) must reproduce…
items.text: Sanity-check every data pull: modelled CPA (cost per click divided by conversion rate) must reproduce measured CPA; if they diverge, the pull is wrong, stop and find out why.
items.why: A built-in reconciliation catches broken extracts before anyone acts on them.

items.title: Count only real sales: paid orders with revenue above zero at retail value; exclude test orders, cancelled or…
items.text: Count only real sales: paid orders with revenue above zero at retail value; exclude test orders, cancelled or pending orders, and zero-value seeding orders (a marketing cost), and never use a fulfilment partner's declared customs values.
items.why: Seeded orders made CPA read $49.64 when acquisition CPA was $53.28; customs values once tripled AOV.
items.when: Building any order or CPA metric.

items.title: Stop every pull at the last day all sources are complete; never include today.
items.text: Stop every pull at the last day all sources are complete; never include today.
items.why: Ad platforms sync mid-day, showing half a day of spend against half a day of orders.

items.title: Use fully loaded contribution: payment and platform fees are variable cost on every grain, alongside product,…
items.text: Use fully loaded contribution: payment and platform fees are variable cost on every grain, alongside product, freight and fulfilment.
items.why: Leaving fees out overstates contribution and understates true break-even.

items.title: Measure shipping per month; never apply one flat rate across periods, and flag months that borrow a…
items.text: Measure shipping per month; never apply one flat rate across periods, and flag months that borrow a neighbour's rate.
items.why: A fulfilment move changed the rate; a flat rate understated earlier months' break-even.

items.title: An ad account not wired into the data is not a zero-spend account: its spend reads null, never 0.
items.text: An ad account not wired into the data is not a zero-spend account: its spend reads null, never 0.
items.why: Treating missing data as zero fabricates great ROAS.

items.title: A SKU missing from the product file is flagged, never guessed.
items.text: A SKU missing from the product file is flagged, never guessed.
items.why: Guessed product mapping silently corrupts inventory and margin.

items.title: Judge first versus repeat buyer on the full order history (a renewal is always repeat), and measure price…
items.text: Judge first versus repeat buyer on the full order history (a renewal is always repeat), and measure price gaps on new orders only, since renewals keep their old prices.
items.why: Mixing renewals into price analysis shows false discounts.

items.title: Break-even ROAS is revenue divided by (revenue minus variable cost) for the selected window; break-even CPA…
items.text: Break-even ROAS is revenue divided by (revenue minus variable cost) for the selected window; break-even CPA is AOV times (1 minus variable cost share), the most a customer may cost.
items.why: The bar moves with the window and the cost mix, so it is recomputed, not fixed.

items.title: Label a month's numbers 'measured' only at 95% or more data coverage; anything less is shown as an estimate…
items.text: Label a month's numbers 'measured' only at 95% or more data coverage; anything less is shown as an estimate with its percentage.
items.why: Readers must see which months are real.

items.title: When modelling levers, cheaper clicks only pull ahead of conversion rate or order value on large moves; near…
items.text: When modelling levers, cheaper clicks only pull ahead of conversion rate or order value on large moves; near break-even the three levers are equivalent.
items.why: A 1% cost cut lifts revenue 1.01% while +1% CVR or AOV lifts it exactly 1%.
items.when: Choosing which lever to work on.

items.title: A chain asks for a job, never names a model, and never restates a model's limits or prompt rules in its own…
items.text: A chain asks for a job, never names a model, and never restates a model's limits or prompt rules in its own code or prompt; inputs are checked before every call, an error stops the call and a warning is recorded on the output.
items.why: One source for what each model takes means best quality every time and no drift.

items.title: Cast a product like a person: every picture with {hero product} in it carries its casting sheet (every side,…
items.text: Cast a product like a person: every picture with {hero product} in it carries its casting sheet (every side, labelled, true size) and how it is really held and what it never does; in a hand or on skin it is drawn from its in-use pictures, shown alone from its front photos, and a product in frame with none of its photos is missing.
items.why: Product realism and physics must be 100% accurate.
items.when: Any picture or video frame that shows the product.

items.title: A review board is an interface, never a brain: every rule that shapes the output lives in the chain, and a…
items.text: A review board is an interface, never a brain: every rule that shapes the output lives in the chain, and a chain run without the board makes the same output; logic found only in the board is a bug.
items.why: Results must be reproducible and automatable without a person at a screen.
items.when: Building any review surface over a chain.

items.title: Turn every review note into an agnostic lesson: record it word for word with its source, write the rule for…
items.text: Turn every review note into an agnostic lesson: record it word for word with its source, write the rule for any brand, product, avatar or ad, point to the line that enforces it, keep it draft until the owner approves; a note is never kept for one ad.
items.why: Feedback rolled into the chain makes the next run better automatically.
items.when: Any owner or reviewer feedback on output.

items.title: Before any spend, every input variable must be filled with an allowed value or marked not applicable with an…
items.text: Before any spend, every input variable must be filled with an allowed value or marked not applicable with an allowed reason; a missing one stops the chain with one plain line naming it, and the preview (model, exact prompt, references, settings, cost) is shown free first.
items.why: Spending on an incomplete input wastes money; inputs are hard gates.

items.title: Send a picture model only what to draw: no markdown, tables, explanations, the source's old words, counts or…
items.text: Send a picture model only what to draw: no markdown, tables, explanations, the source's old words, counts or self-checks, and never a dial's level definition verbatim.
items.why: Anything else in the prompt gets drawn or dilutes it.

items.title: A picture made from a swipe keeps the swipe's photo quality (grain, softness, filter, colour cast,…
items.text: A picture made from a swipe keeps the swipe's photo quality (grain, softness, filter, colour cast, compression) and its light; never make it sharper, cleaner or more polished, and anything swapped in takes the swipe's light and quality.
items.why: Polish breaks fidelity to what already performs.
items.when: Statics and frames remade from a swipe.

items.title: Stills default to the swipe: keep its room, light, props, look and a lookalike of its person, changing only…
items.text: Stills default to the swipe: keep its room, light, props, look and a lookalike of its person, changing only what the brief swaps; establish {brand}'s own set and props only after the swipe-based ad has proven itself.
items.why: Defaulting to the swipe keeps fidelity honest.
items.when: Every static ad copied from a swipe.

items.title: A cast member's face comes only from their one plain headshot (and angles sheet) and keeps its width and…
items.text: A cast member's face comes only from their one plain headshot (and angles sheet) and keeps its width and roundness; their hairstyle, clothes, jewellery and headwear come from the swipe's person; outfit or body pictures go in with every face blanked, and no other saved face sits beside them.
items.why: One face source keeps one person consistent; the swipe supplies the look.
items.when: Any picture with a cast member.

items.title: Every picture of a real-looking person carries real skin (pores, peach fuzz, fine lines, real eyes with…
items.text: Every picture of a real-looking person carries real skin (pores, peach fuzz, fine lines, real eyes with feeling), never smoothed, and gets a skin-only realism pass against their headshot after it is made.
items.why: Smoothed skin reads as AI.
items.when: Every generated picture of a person.

items.title: A picture whose words could not be set is never delivered without them.
items.text: A picture whose words could not be set is never delivered without them.
items.why: A wordless version of a word-led ad is a broken ad.

items.title: Every primary text, headline and description is a proven copy format filled with this ad's own elements (who,…
items.text: Every primary text, headline and description is a proven copy format filled with this ad's own elements (who, era, moment, problem, angle, picture); another ad's story is replaced, and each line is checked against the ad's elements before approval.
items.why: Never write from scratch, but never carry another ad's specifics.
items.when: Ad copy for every static or video.

items.title: Name every lane, folder, file and button by its role (designer, video editor), never by the person who fills…
items.text: Name every lane, folder, file and button by its role (designer, video editor), never by the person who fills it, and keep one name, one shape and one place per thing across brands, roles and storage; reuse an existing name before inventing one and make disagreeing pieces match.
items.why: Naming discrepancies cause the issues at scale.
items.when: Any new folder, file, lane or handoff.

items.title: A handoff to a designer or editor takes only a brief that came out of its chain's final stage; a hand-set…
items.text: A handoff to a designer or editor takes only a brief that came out of its chain's final stage; a hand-set brief, a test run or a run short of the last stage is refused by name.
items.why: Only finished, checked briefs should reach makers.

items.title: Every object the action uses or touches is already in the start frame, within reach and placed away from the…
items.text: Every object the action uses or touches is already in the start frame, within reach and placed away from the path the hands move through; the number of product units on screen matches the offer.
items.why: Nothing should appear from nowhere, and the visual must sell the actual offer.
items.when: Start frames for any video shot.

items.title: When the swipe is an offer ad (sale, clearance, deal, event), the reason for the sale is the swipe's idea:…
items.text: When the swipe is an offer ad (sale, clearance, deal, event), the reason for the sale is the swipe's idea: keep it, put {offer} and {hero product} into it, never turn it into a problem ad; its variations each change one thing about the sale.
items.why: The offer mechanic is what performed.

items.title: When {hero product} goes into the swipe's line, fix the grammar around it (count, gender, plural, verb) so it…
items.text: When {hero product} goes into the swipe's line, fix the grammar around it (count, gender, plural, verb) so it reads right for our product.
items.why: A swapped noun with the swipe's grammar reads broken.

items.title: Boxes or packs in a swipe become {brand}'s real box, same shape, size and placement, and closed; our product…
items.text: Boxes or packs in a swipe become {brand}'s real box, same shape, size and placement, and closed; our product appears only where the swipe's hero product is.
items.why: Open boxes force many drawn products, which read fake.

items.title: Copy the swipe's type as it is drawn: outline or filled box, rounded corners, shadow, true weight, emoji, and…
items.text: Copy the swipe's type as it is drawn: outline or filled box, rounded corners, shadow, true weight, emoji, and any arrow or icon that travels with a line.
items.why: The type treatment is part of the format that performed.

items.title: Build every image ad, always an offer or seasonal one, on one concept borrowed from {avatar}'s culture map…
items.text: Build every image ad, always an offer or seasonal one, on one concept borrowed from {avatar}'s culture map and crossed with the moment: the concept dresses the set, props, palette and type while the swipe's layout stays, and the headline is the concept talking with one spice device, never a plain statement of dates or terms.
items.why: Generic offer statics are the failure; culture concepts stop the scroll.

items.title: Words set on a picture widen to the frame before they shrink, a long line breaks onto a second line before…
items.text: Words set on a picture widen to the frame before they shrink, a long line breaks onto a second line before dropping below four-fifths size, scene dressing never lands in the band kept clear for words, and only the words go on (no writer's notes, no emoji the font cannot draw).
items.why: Readability of the headline is the ad.

items.title: A static made from a swipe keeps the swipe's black bars at their measured heights; a video start picture…
items.text: A static made from a swipe keeps the swipe's black bars at their measured heights; a video start picture always fills the full 9:16 frame with no bars.
items.why: Statics copy the native look; video frames must be full-frame for the clip model.

items.title: A picture brief reads the same dated holidays and moments as the email calendar; an ad with no moment takes…
items.text: A picture brief reads the same dated holidays and moments as the email calendar; an ad with no moment takes the nearest fitting one, never one past its end date.
items.why: All channels share one calendar of moments.

items.title: Shoot a flat product straight-on and turn it only in its own plane; any other angle must be asked for by name.
items.text: Shoot a flat product straight-on and turn it only in its own plane; any other angle must be asked for by name.
items.why: Side or overhead angles make a flat product read thicker than it is.

items.title: Every start picture and every take gets a body check: each hand traced to a shoulder, at most two arms and…
items.text: Every start picture and every take gets a body check: each hand traced to a shoulder, at most two arms and two hands, no oversized or fused hand; a wrong body is a hard fail.
items.why: Malformed bodies are the most visible AI slop.
items.when: All generated frames and clips with people.

items.title: Hold every clip with a person to the movement bar: hands keep doing the real task, unhurried and continuous…
items.text: Hold every clip with a person to the movement bar: hands keep doing the real task, unhurried and continuous with no frozen hold; eyes drop to the hands while working and return to the lens between actions; the head moves with the words; the material visibly moves.
items.why: Continuous real movement is what reads human.
items.when: Every generated clip with a person.

items.title: Props make physical sense (a lid comes off before anything is taken out, every ingredient goes somewhere…
items.text: Props make physical sense (a lid comes off before anything is taken out, every ingredient goes somewhere visible and stays the same thing), each action lands on the object the shot names, and an object an earlier scene drew is reused so it stays the same object.
items.why: Physical nonsense breaks belief instantly.

items.title: A talking take must carry the voice and say the line: a silent take, a take that repeats a word the line says…
items.text: A talking take must carry the voice and say the line: a silent take, a take that repeats a word the line says once, or one that skips three or more words fails its word check and is made again.
items.why: Words heard back are the only proof a take says the script.

items.title: Keep zero and unknown as different answers: a cost that is not known is written as unpriced with the reason,…
items.text: Keep zero and unknown as different answers: a cost that is not known is written as unpriced with the reason, never asserted as $0, and a registry never guesses a cost or key.
items.why: A guessed figure is worse than an absent one.
items.when: Any cost, model or data registry.

items.title: The third copy of something is a card to extract it, not another copy; a new shared need extends what already…
items.text: The third copy of something is a card to extract it, not another copy; a new shared need extends what already exists; and a shared component that falls back to one reader is folded into that reader.
items.why: A component earns its wall by being shared, not by being tidy.
items.when: Deciding to build, extract or retire shared tooling.

items.title: If an approval queue backs up for more than a week, add deputies or narrow what needs approval; never bypass…
items.text: If an approval queue backs up for more than a week, add deputies or narrow what needs approval; never bypass the gate.
items.why: A gate that bottlenecks gets bypassed unless it is resized.

items.title: Keep avatar, sub-avatar, angle and format apart with one test each: avatar is a description of a core person;…
items.text: Keep avatar, sub-avatar, angle and format apart with one test each: avatar is a description of a core person; sub-avatar is a narrower person inside a core; angle is one sentence a customer could agree or disagree with; format is a description of construction (camera, layout, beat order, text behaviour).
items.why: All four feel like 'an idea for an ad' and get confused without a taste-free test.
items.when: Filing any new idea into a bank.

items.title: An angle belongs to {brand}, not to an avatar: any angle can be aimed at any avatar, the avatar's language…
items.text: An angle belongs to {brand}, not to an avatar: any angle can be aimed at any avatar, the avatar's language and the swipe decide how it is said, and they meet in the brief and the ad set; sub-avatars are declared per asset, never as another angle.
items.why: Angles are ways to start the conversation; the approach is the same across avatars.

items.title: Treat avatar, angle, channel and format as independent axes multiplied together: an angle is channel-free and…
items.text: Treat avatar, angle, channel and format as independent axes multiplied together: an angle is channel-free and format-free, a channel sets the reading context but owns no claim, and nothing is a value on two axes.
items.why: If a thing only works in one container, it is a format, not an angle.

items.title: Nothing enters a bank because it is interesting: an angle needs a claim and a receipt that resolves, a format…
items.text: Nothing enters a bank because it is interesting: an angle needs a claim and a receipt that resolves, a format needs a mechanic and the posts behind it counted; the default is unreviewed and only the owner signs anything active.
items.why: Banks fill with non-angles and duplicates otherwise.
items.when: Adding entries to angle, format or offer banks.

items.title: Never coin a name: a name not in its bank is an error, and borrowing an existing field name with a new…
items.text: Never coin a name: a name not in its bank is an error, and borrowing an existing field name with a new meaning counts as coining.
items.why: A silently coined name forks the vocabulary and every report built on it.
items.when: Naming assets, fields, angles and formats.

items.title: Set a brief's angle once, when it gets its number: pick one angle from {brand}'s active bank, preferring…
items.text: Set a brief's angle once, when it gets its number: pick one angle from {brand}'s active bank, preferring angles whose ad set is already running, with a one-line reason quoting the brief, or record no-fit; every later stage reads it and a different angle downstream is refused.
items.why: One field, one writer, every stage reads it.

items.title: Pick a brief's landing page when the brief is written: it sells the brief's product, carries its offer, is…
items.text: Pick a brief's landing page when the brief is written: it sells the brief's product, carries its offer, is the same page type as the swipe's page (advertorial, quiz, offer page, store page), and answers live.
items.why: The page must match the ad's promise and the format that performed.

items.title: Run page tests by the scientific method: one page, one test at a time; hypothesis written first; control…
items.text: Run page tests by the scientific method: one page, one test at a time; hypothesis written first; control versus one variant; primary metric checkout reached, confirm metric purchase; stop point set before it starts; gated on compliance plus the owner's dated approval. A design test keeps one offer in both groups; an offer test changes only the offer.
items.why: One variable at a time gives a readable result.
items.when: Every landing page or funnel test.

items.title: Ads never point at a variant build and never change when a page test starts; live page addresses are never…
items.text: Ads never point at a variant build and never change when a page test starts; live page addresses are never renamed, and a page ID is never reused or re-pointed (a materially different page gets a new name).
items.why: Tests run on the page so ad delivery and attribution stay stable.

items.title: Observed examples are evidence, not choices: keep captured layouts and swipe blocks as proof and never offer…
items.text: Observed examples are evidence, not choices: keep captured layouts and swipe blocks as proof and never offer them as options to pick.
items.why: Giving evidence the shape of a choice is how it ends up in a menu.

items.title: Take the cheapest route that does the job for a generated asset, then finish it locally.
items.text: Take the cheapest route that does the job for a generated asset, then finish it locally.
items.why: Spend where it buys quality, nowhere else.

items.title: Nothing ships unseen: every generated object is looked at beside its reference (shape, colours, text,…
items.text: Nothing ships unseen: every generated object is looked at beside its reference (shape, colours, text, proportions), and the prompt used is kept verbatim next to it.
items.why: Visible prompts and eyes-on checks are how quality is controlled.

items.title: In review notes, say what was measured, not just what you want (a number the next render can be checked…
items.text: In review notes, say what was measured, not just what you want (a number the next render can be checked against).
items.why: 'Too bright' is an opinion; a measurement is checkable.

items.title: Measure a page's geometry off the built page in a real browser; never copy sizes from a brief.
items.text: Measure a page's geometry off the built page in a real browser; never copy sizes from a brief.
items.why: A hand-typed brief size was wrong and every asset derived from it was wrong.

items.title: Review copies and live checks of a page strip or block analytics, ad pixels and messaging tools so a review…
items.text: Review copies and live checks of a page strip or block analytics, ad pixels and messaging tools so a review never counts as a visit.
items.why: Reviews must not pollute live data.

items.title: Tear a competitor page down to its bones: the sections in order and the persuasion job of each, with none of…
items.text: Tear a competitor page down to its bones: the sections in order and the persuasion job of each, with none of the source's words, offer, brand, people, places or claims.
items.why: The structure is what transfers; the source's identity must not.
items.when: First stage of any page remake.

items.title: Write page words only from the brand's sources: customer language from language-bank rows (a quote word for…
items.text: Write page words only from the brand's sources: customer language from language-bank rows (a quote word for word, citing the row), offer and guarantee word for word from the offer file (no guarantee the file does not state), product facts from the product file; past winning ads are not a source.
items.why: Every word must trace to a verified source.

items.title: Keep the torn-down structure's job order and arc, adapt forms to the format with every change listed, and…
items.text: Keep the torn-down structure's job order and arc, adapt forms to the format with every change listed, and fail any page where the source's names, offers, calls to action, headings, claims or any 8-word run survive; fix only the flagged blocks, up to three rounds.
items.why: Copy the persuasion structure, never the competitor's identity.
items.when: Checking a written page against its source.

items.title: Every picture on a built page comes from the house 3D picture process; a slot nothing fits shows a marked…
items.text: Every picture on a built page comes from the house 3D picture process; a slot nothing fits shows a marked frame describing what it must hold, and the page chain never deploys anything itself.
items.why: One picture process; going live is a separate step.

items.title: Classify each promo moment from the files, not its name: it is a SALE only if it names an offer; every other…
items.text: Classify each promo moment from the files, not its name: it is a SALE only if it names an offer; every other moment is CONTENT (emails, SMS when planned, organic posts) with no offer, margin, stock, ads, funnel or storefront steps.
items.why: Not every holiday warrants an offer and the full ad build.

items.title: Quote an offer only from the named offer-bank section's lines marked usable in ads, word for word; never a…
items.text: Quote an offer only from the named offer-bank section's lines marked usable in ads, word for word; never a ruling, lane note, struck-through or refused line, and never an offer matched by overlapping dates.
items.why: Offer words must be exactly what is approved and live.

items.title: A promo opens on its date minus the holiday's lead days, and its own date is the peak; the tool never picks…
items.text: A promo opens on its date minus the holiday's lead days, and its own date is the peak; the tool never picks the opening, shows every opening on file with its source, and lists a moment with no resolvable date with the reason instead of guessing.
items.why: The opening is the strategist's call in the home that owns it.

items.title: Work back from launch: decide 42 days out, brief 28, plan 21, produce 14, load and check 7, launch on day 0,…
items.text: Work back from launch: decide 42 days out, brief 28, plan 21, produce 14, load and check 7, launch on day 0, read back 7 days after the end; seasonal ads are made from day -28 and ready by day -14.
items.why: A fixed timeline keeps every piece ready before the moment.

items.title: A sale moment's pieces enter the team queue when its start is 70 days out or less (and it has run under 7…
items.text: A sale moment's pieces enter the team queue when its start is 70 days out or less (and it has run under 7 days); promo pieces rank by days to due, overdue first, and evergreen 14-day sprints fill the rest; default per sale is 3 image ads, 2 video ads, 1 creator video, 1 funnel and 1 storefront piece unless the strategist's ask gives counts; a person's queue decision always wins.
items.why: Promos get priority by urgency without starving evergreen.

items.title: An offer marked hidden until a date is a gate, not a failure: its sends are written and wait, and approval is…
items.text: An offer marked hidden until a date is a gate, not a failure: its sends are written and wait, and approval is refused until the mark is removed.
items.why: Work proceeds without leaking an offer early.

items.title: Find where {avatar} talks rather than listing rooms by hand: one unrestricted, posts-only search in the…
items.text: Find where {avatar} talks rather than listing rooms by hand: one unrestricted, posts-only search in the avatar's own desire words, sorted by relevance, rooms tallied by score (loudest topical room, not busiest), top 5 kept; a block a person confirmed always wins.
items.why: Hand-typed room lists are guesses; relevance finds topical rooms, score picks the loudest.
items.when: Starting research on any new avatar.

items.title: Reconcile research against {avatar}'s demographics: drop rooms plainly for someone else before pulling, never…
items.text: Reconcile research against {avatar}'s demographics: drop rooms plainly for someone else before pulling, never claim a room is plainly ours, and let unknown demographics rule nothing out.
items.why: Research from the wrong people is irrelevant for that avatar.

items.title: Never file a research row without a permalink; a row the labelling reads cannot classify is held, never…
items.text: Never file a research row without a permalink; a row the labelling reads cannot classify is held, never guessed.
items.why: Every claim must trace to a receipt.

items.title: Automate only research sources that cost nothing (ad comments, support tickets, surveys, reviews, interview…
items.text: Automate only research sources that cost nothing (ad comments, support tickets, surveys, reviews, interview transcripts); paid scraping runs only on request with its price shown and approved first.
items.why: Prevents open-ended spend on scrapers.

items.title: Lane customer language by relationship first: a verified buyer, customer-survey answer or customer interview…
items.text: Lane customer language by relationship first: a verified buyer, customer-survey answer or customer interview is a customer, a refund-survey answer is churned, the rest are read from the words; never read emails, names or phone numbers into a row.
items.why: Who said it decides how it can be used; personal data stays out.

items.title: A creator with under 100 measured words is listed as thin and left out of the spoken-style band.
items.text: A creator with under 100 measured words is listed as thin and left out of the spoken-style band.
items.why: Too little speech gives an unreliable voiceprint.

items.title: Find the page that loses the most money before checkout: price each landing or cart page as visitors who left…
items.text: Find the page that loses the most money before checkout: price each landing or cart page as visitors who left there times revenue per visitor who reached checkout; pages under 200 visitors are listed, not ranked; work on the top page with no test running.
items.why: Fix the biggest dollar leak first.

items.title: Read session recordings in both groups: the newest 30 visitors who left and 10 who reached checkout over 14…
items.text: Read session recordings in both groups: the newest 30 visitors who left and 10 who reached checkout over 14 days, each with at least 5 active seconds; hold the run if fewer than 5 leavers exist.
items.why: Comparing leavers with buyers shows what actually differs.

items.title: Split recording findings into a fix list for the team (one element each: friction, words, size, broken,…
items.text: Split recording findings into a fix list for the team (one element each: friction, words, size, broken, layout) and at most three big swings for the owner (offer, positioning, order, angle), each a full hypothesis for its own 50/50 test; price every item in dollars a month as an upper bound for ranking, never a forecast.
items.why: Small fixes are the team's; the owner takes only the big swings.

items.title: A team page fix goes live only on a compliance pass and the owner's click (one click per page batch), becomes…
items.text: A team page fix goes live only on a compliance pass and the owner's click (one click per page batch), becomes the new control, and never lands while a test is running on that page.
items.why: Keeps tests clean and live changes accountable.

items.title: Every page test carries its stop point before it runs: 7-21 days, 800-3,000 visitors and at least 25 orders…
items.text: Every page test carries its stop point before it runs: 7-21 days, 800-3,000 visitors and at least 25 orders per group; the variant wins only at 95%+ chance AND 20%+ more checkouts reached with orders per visitor not lower; stop early after 400 per group if 95%+ likely the variant is worse by 30%+; at the cap the control holds.
items.why: Pre-set stopping rules prevent peeking and false wins.

items.title: Drop any proposed page fix the live page contradicts, with the reason, and never mock up a change with a…
items.text: Drop any proposed page fix the live page contradicts, with the reason, and never mock up a change with a price, percentage or picture the store and page do not have.
items.why: Fixes must address what visitors really see.

items.title: Check a live page as the majority visitor sees it: on the device most recordings used (phone wins ties) and…
items.text: Check a live page as the majority visitor sees it: on the device most recordings used (phone wins ties) and from the country most visitors came from.
items.why: A capture from the wrong market shows wrong prices or stock.

items.title: Store promo changes are read-only by default and written only on a person's typed go; the write is refused if…
items.text: Store promo changes are read-only by default and written only on a person's typed go; the write is refused if the live store changed since the plan, or the start date is missing or still in the future.
items.why: A store write goes live the moment it runs.

items.title: When the files give more than one start date for a promo (offer bank, moment, early-access offset of 7 days…
items.text: When the files give more than one start date for a promo (offer bank, moment, early-access offset of 7 days by default), show them all and let the person choose; the tool never picks.
items.why: The start date is the person's call.

items.title: Storefront banner and offer-box words are the offer bank's own lines in its order; pop-up voice words come…
items.text: Storefront banner and offer-box words are the offer bank's own lines in its order; pop-up voice words come from the customer-language bank with the row cited and two alternates shown, no row reused across slots, and a slot with no passing row left unset, never typed.
items.why: No invented words reach the store.
items.when: Storefront banners, offer boxes and sign-up pop-ups.

items.title: The sign-up pop-up offers the moment's own offer during a promo window (early-access sign-up), else {brand}'s…
items.text: The sign-up pop-up offers the moment's own offer during a promo window (early-access sign-up), else {brand}'s standing pop-up offer; if none exists it is an open call for the owner. It captures email first, then phone.
items.why: The pop-up should sell what the store is running.

items.title: Only set a discount code whose terms the offer bank states as a percent off, and never rewrite a funnel's own…
items.text: Only set a discount code whose terms the offer bank states as a percent off, and never rewrite a funnel's own offers from the storefront.
items.why: Codes must match approved terms; funnels own their offers.

items.title: Where the offer bank names a lead product for the storefront, the store's bar and pop-up lead with that…
items.text: Where the offer bank names a lead product for the storefront, the store's bar and pop-up lead with that product in every window, while funnels keep the moment's own offer.
items.why: The store and funnels can sell different things.

items.title: Run every recurring-billing offer through one chain: offer passes audit, variables filled, pages built from…
items.text: Run every recurring-billing offer through one chain: offer passes audit, variables filled, pages built from the standard wording, checklist run on the built funnel, legal review, then live; nothing goes live on its own.
items.why: Auto-renewal law (ROSCA, California) needs the same disclosure everywhere.

items.title: Show one refill notice per page in one fixed sentence ('Refills {price} with {shipping} every {days} days…
items.text: Show one refill notice per page in one fixed sentence ('Refills {price} with {shipping} every {days} days until you cancel. Cancel anytime at {cancel way}.'): under the button on offer pages and upsells, under the tier cards before every way to pay at checkout, never inside product cards; the terms line above the checkout button names refills.
items.why: One consistent, visible disclosure satisfies the law without clutter.

items.title: Read the refill amount from a real test subscription, never from the page, and confirm it matches the notice;…
items.text: Read the refill amount from a real test subscription, never from the page, and confirm it matches the notice; a first-order saving may not carry over.
items.why: The disclosed price must be what actually bills.
items.when: Before a subscription funnel goes live.

items.title: Check every subscription funnel for: refill price, frequency, runs until cancelled, how to cancel, terms next…
items.text: Check every subscription funnel for: refill price, frequency, runs until cancelled, how to cancel, terms next to and standing out by the button, free gift explained, consent to the refill itself (express-pay and upsell yes buttons included), consent record kept, terms on thank-you page and confirmation email, online cancel, cancel requests processed, yearly reminder and price-change notice.
items.why: Each item maps to a ROSCA or California auto-renewal requirement.

items.title: A seed list is a hypothesis, not research: seed just enough to reach real people, take the people who show up…
items.text: A seed list is a hypothesis, not research: seed just enough to reach real people, take the people who show up in the comments, read their whole feeds, and let topics and formats fall out as findings ranked by how many separate people carry them.
items.why: A list only contains what somebody already thought of; real results surface what nobody named.

items.title: Research presents opportunity, it does not try to be right: never filter a finding for being off-avatar;…
items.text: Research presents opportunity, it does not try to be right: never filter a finding for being off-avatar; report two bands, what confirms the room and what is unexpected; format travels further than topic.
items.why: Off-target findings are where novel concepts come from; a system tuned to return the expected tells you nothing.

items.title: Rank content by engagement, but do not choose who to follow by it: harvest both niche posts (they confirm the…
items.text: Rank content by engagement, but do not choose who to follow by it: harvest both niche posts (they confirm the avatar) and escaped viral posts (they surface other worlds), label which is which, and weight each commenter by how many seeded posts they appear on as a confidence score, not a cut.
items.why: A viral post's comment section is the whole internet, not the room.
items.when: Choosing commenters to follow in research.

items.title: Research is aggregate only (clusters and named entities, never a file about a person), and nothing goes in…
items.text: Research is aggregate only (clusters and named entities, never a file about a person), and nothing goes in without a receipt: a view count, like count, comment, or a line saying where a source came from.
items.why: Privacy and traceability.

items.title: Avatar feeds keep entertainment (and educational as its own filter), never selling or junk: an ask names…
items.text: Avatar feeds keep entertainment (and educational as its own filter), never selling or junk: an ask names whose scroll it is and never turns the feed into content about their problem; only shop or remake feeds and a person's own saves may keep selling posts.
items.why: Entertainment is what people open the app for, before they are aware of any problem.

items.title: Run every organic research round in order: read the avatar first and list their top worlds by count; give…
items.text: Run every organic research round in order: read the avatar first and list their top worlds by count; give every top-three world at least one seed (coverage gate); one avatar per plan; show searches, posts and a hard dollar cap and wait for a yes; pull about 1,000 posts; keep current-year posts only, drop ads and repeats; score views + likes + comments; rank on the avatar's own top 50; the owner picks the formats before any writing.
items.why: A hand-made seed list once skipped the avatar's biggest world.

items.title: No automatic paid scraping: every paid pull runs on a person's go, every pull has a spend floor and cap, and…
items.text: No automatic paid scraping: every paid pull runs on a person's go, every pull has a spend floor and cap, and publishing anything public is a person's act, never a schedule.
items.why: Unattended buttons can empty a month's budget in an afternoon.
items.when: Scheduling any paid data pull or public export.

items.title: Pick swipes for creator briefs from proven sources only, never organic viral posts: competitor ads already…
items.text: Pick swipes for creator briefs from proven sources only, never organic viral posts: competitor ads already running 30+ days ranked on estimated spend, days live and duplicates, and shop-platform videos ranked on sales then views; never pad the list; proven winning formats move to the front, formats to avoid to the back; picks wait for the owner's yes.
items.why: A creator brief should start from a swipe with proof of selling, not just reach.

items.title: Pick the next organic post to tear down per feed as the best untouched entertainment post ranked by sent…
items.text: Pick the next organic post to tear down per feed as the best untouched entertainment post ranked by sent rate, then punch past following, then views.
items.why: Share rate and reach beyond the creator's audience signal a transferable format.

items.title: Group competitor ads into copy blocks by identical headline plus primary text; a block says what copy they…
items.text: Group competitor ads into copy blocks by identical headline plus primary text; a block says what copy they have locked, not an angle, and an angle is read off the frame, not the copy.
items.why: In our own account one copy block held a $41,870 ad and a $99 ad; the difference was the picture.

items.title: Rank competitor copy blocks by variant replication (how many near-identical variants they run), not by…
items.text: Rank competitor copy blocks by variant replication (how many near-identical variants they run), not by creative volume; replication shows what they are betting on, not what converts.
items.why: Nobody clones a loser, but a brand can clone a loser for a week before killing it.

items.title: Read a competitor ad's funnel stage from its headline (top: education, mechanism, problem; mid: proof, story,…
items.text: Read a competitor ad's funnel stage from its headline (top: education, mechanism, problem; mid: proof, story, result; bottom: offer, scarcity, guarantee), using the body only as a fallback.
items.why: Nearly every direct-response body mentions a guarantee; the hook carries the awareness level.

items.title: Hold dated or seasonal promos out of the evergreen ranking and report them separately.
items.text: Hold dated or seasonal promos out of the evergreen ranking and report them separately.
items.why: A 10-day sale carried 20% of one brand's variant weight; it is real but not an evergreen angle.

items.title: When briefing from competitor swipes: rank on replication, then read the stage (a bottom-funnel block at the…
items.text: When briefing from competitor swipes: rank on replication, then read the stage (a bottom-funnel block at the top is a volume play, not an angle); treat near-identical headlines as one family; verify the landing page yourself.
items.why: You are copying what a competitor committed to, which is a better start than guessing but still not proof.

items.title: Cluster competitor ads before paying for per-ad detail: one paid detail pull per copy block, not per ad.
items.text: Cluster competitor ads before paying for per-ad detail: one paid detail pull per copy block, not per ad.
items.why: 18 credits instead of 830 for the same landing-page coverage.

items.title: In a competitor teardown, the judgment sections (structural findings; what to take and what to beat) are…
items.text: In a competitor teardown, the judgment sections (structural findings; what to take and what to beat) are written by a person, never a machine; everything else is countable from the data.
items.why: Once a machine drafts the judgment you can no longer tell what was observed.

items.title: Type a landing page structurally: quiz step markers or quiz host means quiz; five or more numbered items…
items.text: Type a landing page structurally: quiz step markers or quiz host means quiz; five or more numbered items means listicle; cart language means product page; over 4,000 characters of prose with none of these means advertorial.
items.why: Structure, not appearance, decides page type reliably.

items.title: Describe our own ads, competitor ads and organic posts in one shared vocabulary; our own ads are the only…
items.text: Describe our own ads, competitor ads and organic posts in one shared vocabulary; our own ads are the only lane with an outcome and make the other two comparable.
items.why: Same words across lanes let swipes be judged against what actually earned.

items.title: To see which competitor bets are sustained or killed, sweep the same advertiser weekly and diff; a single…
items.text: To see which competitor bets are sustained or killed, sweep the same advertiser weekly and diff; a single sweep cannot show duration or kills.
items.why: Replication sustained over time is a far better proxy than a snapshot.

items.title: Do not rank brands on reported reach alone; a third-party reach figure can read zero for a brand with active…
items.text: Do not rank brands on reported reach alone; a third-party reach figure can read zero for a brand with active ads.
items.why: Reach data from ad-intelligence tools is unreliable on its own.

items.title: A machine may send to an outside audience or commit spend only on a person's go: typed by that person under…
