items.text: In a meme format, keep the source's framing, camera move, beat and sound, and protect the decisive action.
items.why: The meme works because its form is recognised.

items.title: In a micro-drama, open wide to set positions, tighten sizes as stakes rise, push in at the turn with silence,…
items.text: In a micro-drama, open wide to set positions, tighten sizes as stakes rise, push in at the turn with silence, cut hook-conflict-turn-payoff, and protect wardrobe and positions across sizes.
items.why: Escalating sizes carry rising stakes.

items.title: In a comedy skit, keep the camera simple so the performance plays, cut to the reaction, let jokes land on…
items.text: In a comedy skit, keep the camera simple so the performance plays, cut to the reaction, let jokes land on room tone, and protect timing.
items.why: Timing is what makes the joke.

items.title: Fill every line of the shot brief for every shot (shot size/angle/lens, who bound to reference, one action,…
items.text: Fill every line of the shot brief for every shot (shot size/angle/lens, who bound to reference, one action, camera move, set bound to reference and time, light, palette, sound, exact line or none, the shared style line, length in seconds); a blank line means the model picks for you.
items.why: Anything left unsaid is decided by the model, not by us.

items.title: Write each generation prompt as if the model has seen nothing else, and change only one thing per retry.
items.text: Write each generation prompt as if the model has seen nothing else, and change only one thing per retry.
items.why: Single-variable retries show what fixed or broke the shot.

items.title: Treat the creative as the targeting: Andromeda groups ads that look or feel alike as variations of one…
items.text: Treat the creative as the targeting: Andromeda groups ads that look or feel alike as variations of one creative, so give the algorithm one clean place to learn and a steady supply of genuinely different creatives.
items.why: Meta retrieves and ranks ads by each ad's creative fingerprint, not by audience settings.

items.title: Run each offer in its own Advantage+ sales campaign with the budget on the campaign, and link every ad in it…
items.text: Run each offer in its own Advantage+ sales campaign with the budget on the campaign, and link every ad in it to that offer's one page.
items.why: Advantage+ sales campaigns average 20% lower cost per result, and one page keeps learning in one place.

items.title: Make each ad set one {avatar} plus one angle, so each angle's learning and spend read on their own while the…
items.text: Make each ad set one {avatar} plus one angle, so each angle's learning and spend read on their own while the creative carries the match under broad Advantage+ Audience targeting.
items.why: Only a few angles will hit, and each must be readable on its own.

items.title: Keep 6 to 10 live creatives per ad set and never more than 50.
items.text: Keep 6 to 10 live creatives per ad set and never more than 50.
items.why: Meta favours fewer ads with more assets.

items.title: Optimise for purchase value, with the pixel and Conversions API sending Purchase with value.
items.text: Optimise for purchase value, with the pixel and Conversions API sending Purchase with value.
items.why: Value optimisation is Meta's own guidance for sales.

items.title: Every new creative must be 3+ moves from the nearest live creative across persona, angle, awareness, format,…
items.text: Every new creative must be 3+ moves from the nearest live creative across persona, angle, awareness, format, face, setting and look; inside one ad set the avatar and angle are fixed, so the moves come from awareness, format, face, setting and look.
items.why: Meta treats look-alike ads as one creative; the 3-move threshold is ours, Meta publishes none.

items.title: Every new creative links to {brand}'s one offer page and carries the core message.
items.text: Every new creative links to {brand}'s one offer page and carries the core message.
items.why: One offer page keeps learning and results in one place.

items.title: Every 9:16 video carries music or voiceover, and key messages sit inside the 9:16 safe zone.
items.text: Every 9:16 video carries music or voiceover, and key messages sit inside the 9:16 safe zone.
items.why: Meta reports up to 13% more incremental conversions with sound.

items.title: Run {creator} content as partnership ads.
items.text: Run {creator} content as partnership ads.
items.why: Meta reports 19% lower acquisition cost for partnership ads.

items.title: Make each ad a flexible ad of up to 10 assets with different faces and settings; each ad set holds at least…
items.text: Make each ad a flexible ad of up to 10 assets with different faces and settings; each ad set holds at least one image, one video and one 9:16 video with audio, and at least 20% of its assets are 9:16 video with audio.
items.why: Meta reports 7-9% lower CPA from the format mix and vertical audio share.
items.when: Building Meta ads and ad sets.

items.title: Budget each campaign at about 7 × cost per purchase × the number of live ad sets per day (using break-even…
items.text: Budget each campaign at about 7 × cost per purchase × the number of live ad sets per day (using break-even CPA until real CPA exists), because each ad set needs about 50 results a week to exit learning; add ad sets only as budget allows.
items.why: Below that, ad sets stay learning-limited.

items.title: Run the week on a fixed loop: read results Monday, brief to the gaps Tuesday with every brief scored before…
items.text: Run the week on a fixed loop: read results Monday, brief to the gaps Tuesday with every brief scored before it is made, drop the week's new creatives into the ad set as one batch Thursday while removing what Meta marks creative limited or fatigued, judge each creative daily against break-even, and make no edits while learning.
items.why: The loop is built on Meta's learning phase and fatigue guidance.

items.title: Never build on unpublished Meta folklore: "entity ID", ">60% similarity score", "8-15+ ads per ad set" or…
items.text: Never build on unpublished Meta folklore: "entity ID", ">60% similarity score", "8-15+ ads per ad set" or "similar ads pay higher CPMs".
items.why: These are not Meta's published guidance, and Meta says fewer ads, more assets.

items.title: Run each section swap (a new hook, proof or offer staging) as its own asset inside the version's flexible ad,…
items.text: Run each section swap (a new hook, proof or offer staging) as its own asset inside the version's flexible ad, so Meta reports spend and purchases per asset and every section earns its own score.
items.why: Per-asset reporting grades each section on real results.
items.when: Testing hooks, proof and offer variants on Meta.

items.title: Default every ad to maxed creative dials: intensity, absurdity, specificity, dramatisation and stopping power…
items.text: Default every ad to maxed creative dials: intensity, absurdity, specificity, dramatisation and stopping power at the top (4), swap depth at replacement (3) and ad-likeness at native (0), unless a preset or the brief says otherwise.
items.why: Maxed and hyper-specific is the house stance; the guards keep it on the claim.
items.when: Copy, video and image ads for any {brand}; setting target levels before writing or production.

items.title: Never ship a sterile ad: no preset, saved level or brief may set intensity below 3, absurdity below 3, humor…
items.text: Never ship a sterile ad: no preset, saved level or brief may set intensity below 3, absurdity below 3, humor below 2, dramatisation below 3, stopping power below 4 or parody marks below 2, at any awareness level, bottom funnel and offers included.
items.why: Sterile ads waste the money season; the floor holds under every preset.
items.when: Every ad in every medium and funnel stage.

items.title: Give a proof or offer ad its proof inside an absurd, dramatised picture, never a plain product shot or plain…
items.text: Give a proof or offer ad its proof inside an absurd, dramatised picture, never a plain product shot or plain sale graphic.
items.why: The never-sterile floor applies to bottom-funnel and offer ads too.
items.when: Product-aware and most-aware ads, offers, promotions.

items.title: Tie every absurd or swapped element to the problem, the result or the product; absurdity at 3 or 4 only works…
items.text: Tie every absurd or swapped element to the problem, the result or the product; absurdity at 3 or 4 only works when the relevance and legibility guards are met.
items.why: Unexpected and irrelevant is the one quadrant that hurts the message.
items.when: Any ad using absurdity, swaps or surreal elements.

items.title: Make the problem and what is ours readable inside one second, however loud the rest of the piece is.
items.text: Make the problem and what is ours readable inside one second, however loud the rest of the piece is.
items.why: Legibility is the guard that lets the loud dials run at the top.
items.when: Every ad, especially absurd or dense ones.

items.title: Give every violation or edgy moment its safety (distance, a character, obvious exaggeration); edge above 2…
items.text: Give every violation or edgy moment its safety (distance, a character, obvious exaggeration); edge above 2 needs humor or absurdity to make it benign.
items.why: Without the benign half the same picture reads as gross or offensive.
items.when: Ads that show the problem graphically, taboo-adjacent humour, embarrassing moments.

items.title: Exaggerate the premise and the emotion, never the medical or physical outcome.
items.text: Exaggerate the premise and the emotion, never the medical or physical outcome.
items.why: Exaggerated outcomes are where ad policy and believability break.
items.when: Dramatised ads, especially health, skin or body results.

items.title: Take every hyper-specific detail from the {avatar}'s own words or the {brand}'s own files; never invent one.
items.text: Take every hyper-specific detail from the {avatar}'s own words or the {brand}'s own files; never invent one.
items.why: An invented specific reads false; specifics are what keep absurd, dramatised pieces believable.
items.when: Writing copy, scripts, scenes and picture details.

items.title: The words on an ad must make sense to a stranger on one read, before any joke lands; keep a borrowed sentence…
items.text: The words on an ad must make sense to a stranger on one read, before any joke lands; keep a borrowed sentence shape only when our words still say something literally true and clear, and rewrite any line that needs the swipe to be understood.
items.why: A great picture with text that doesn't make sense fails; filling a swipe's sentence with our nouns is a word game.
items.when: Headlines, captions and on-screen text, especially on swiped formats.

items.title: Make the words and the picture say the same idea: a stranger reading the line then looking at the picture…
items.text: Make the words and the picture say the same idea: a stranger reading the line then looking at the picture must understand why that picture is there; a line about something the picture does not show fails.
items.why: A great picture under a line that makes no sense is a wasted picture.
items.when: Static ads, video on-screen lines, any word-plus-picture creative.

items.title: Keep coherence between words and picture at the top (4) while keeping anchorage low (about 1): give one hint,…
items.text: Keep coherence between words and picture at the top (4) while keeping anchorage low (about 1): give one hint, never spell the picture out word for word.
items.why: A picture the viewer solves is remembered; spelling it out kills the joke, while 0 can leave a hard swap unread.

items.title: Turn any real brand mark, outfit or famous face a swipe carries into an absurd parody of itself (parody level…
items.text: Turn any real brand mark, outfit or famous face a swipe carries into an absurd parody of itself (parody level 3 by default, never below 2); never keep it as the real thing and never just blank it.
items.why: The parody makes it funny and culturally relevant; we make people laugh, never pass anything off.
items.when: Remaking swipes that contain logos, uniforms or celebrities.

items.title: Pick one primary emotion per beat, with at most one secondary; its strength is the intensity dial and its…
items.text: Pick one primary emotion per beat, with at most one secondary; its strength is the intensity dial and its direction the valence dial.
items.why: A beat carrying many emotions blurs; one emotion per beat keeps it readable.
items.when: Scripting beats in video, copy and image sequences.

items.title: Name the technique used to turn a dial up (techniques are switches: a piece uses one or it does not).
items.text: Name the technique used to turn a dial up (techniques are switches: a piece uses one or it does not).
items.why: Naming the move makes it repeatable and measurable across chains.

items.title: Run intensity at peak (4) by default, with the peak landing in the first three seconds of video; test 3…
items.text: Run intensity at peak (4) by default, with the peak landing in the first three seconds of video; test 3 against 4 because peak arousal with no relief reads as distress.
items.why: Activation is what makes people stop and share; a low-arousal ad is wallpaper.

items.title: Open a direct-response piece at the problem's worst (valence about -2) and close high; keep the negative…
items.text: Open a direct-response piece at the problem's worst (valence about -2) and close high; keep the negative feeling on the problem, never on the product.
items.why: The problem at its worst stops the right person; disgust sticks to whatever it touches.

items.title: Pair dramatisation at 3 or 4 with specificity and realism at 3 or more.
items.text: Pair dramatisation at 3 or 4 with specificity and realism at 3 or more.
items.why: Dramatisation without specifics reads as puffery.

items.title: Keep the world realistic (realism about 3: real rooms, real skin, phone grain, speech rhythm, never marketing…
items.text: Keep the world realistic (realism about 3: real rooms, real skin, phone grain, speech rhythm, never marketing tone) even when the event in it is absurd.
items.why: Lo-fi real makes the absurd land as something that happened and keeps it off AI slop.
items.when: Production look for video and images.

items.title: Make upper-funnel ads not look like ads at all (ad-likeness 0: a post a friend could have made); let bottom…
items.text: Make upper-funnel ads not look like ads at all (ad-likeness 0: a post a friend could have made); let bottom funnel set its own level, about 3 for product proof.
items.why: Low ad-likeness delays the 'this is an ad' discount.

items.title: Score the hook's stopping power and its link to us separately; a scroll stop on something unrelated to the…
items.text: Score the hook's stopping power and its link to us separately; a scroll stop on something unrelated to the product or problem is a wasted click.
items.why: Everything else is wasted if the scroll does not stop, but a stop with no intent buys bad clicks.

items.title: When swapping our product into a swipe, keep the swipe's pose, light, crowd and frame and make the swapped…
items.text: When swapping our product into a swipe, keep the swipe's pose, light, crowd and frame and make the swapped object rhyme in shape, pose, colour, size and light with what it replaced.
items.why: A swap that rhymes reads as the swipe first and ours a second later; a non-rhyming swap goes random.
items.when: Remaking swipes in image or video.

items.title: Keep the product true to itself and true to its size: get size rhyme or scale distortion by moving the…
items.text: Keep the product true to itself and true to its size: get size rhyme or scale distortion by moving the camera, the product's place, or distorting a prop, the problem or the world, never by resizing the product (unless the whole joke is one giant product, shown once).
items.why: One product, one size; a resized product breaks believability.
items.when: Image and video scenes with the product in frame.

items.title: Build scale distortion in a true-size 3D set and print it, never ask a picture model for a size in words.
items.text: Build scale distortion in a true-size 3D set and print it, never ask a picture model for a size in words.
items.why: A picture model cannot hold a size from words; the set gives real contact and shadow.
items.when: Image production with scale distortion or rhyme.

items.title: Prefer known pictures, formats and moments the viewer already recognises (borrowedness 4), picked from the…
items.text: Prefer known pictures, formats and moments the viewer already recognises (borrowedness 4), picked from the {avatar}'s own feed.
items.why: A picture they already know stops them; if they don't know the source the joke falls flat.
items.when: Choosing swipes, memes and formats to remake.

items.title: Keep frame density low (about 1: one thing to look at) and dress surfaces before adding props.
items.text: Keep frame density low (about 1: one thing to look at) and dress surfaces before adding props.
items.why: One thing to look at makes the swap land; dense frames hide the problem.

items.title: Keep the uncanny and image degradation light (about 1, never above 2), and keep the product itself clean.
items.text: Keep the uncanny and image degradation light (about 1, never above 2), and keep the product itself clean.
items.why: A little off stops the scroll; above 2 it looks generated, and degraded product pictures look cheap.

items.title: Keep irony light (about 1, never above 2) and cringe modest (about 2).
items.text: Keep irony light (about 1, never above 2) and cringe modest (about 2).
items.why: A wink keeps it native; deep irony loses the message and peak cringe makes the brand the joke.

items.title: Cast a low-status speaker (status about 3) to make the problem safe to laugh at, but avoid low status on a…
items.text: Cast a low-status speaker (status about 3) to make the problem safe to laugh at, but avoid low status on a proof beat.
items.why: A low-status speaker makes the problem safe; low status weakens proof.

items.title: Default video to handheld camera, fast cutting (about 3), candid eye contact (about 2) and a close shot scale…
items.text: Default video to handheld camera, fast cutting (about 3), candid eye contact (about 2) and a close shot scale (about 3).
items.why: Handheld and candid read native; fast cutting holds the feed; close shows the problem.

items.title: Write every clip beat by beat by the second with nonstop physical action (motion 4) set on the beat with…
items.text: Write every clip beat by beat by the second with nonstop physical action (motion 4) set on the beat with attitude (vibe 4), every move still serving the scene.
items.why: Nonstop action is the house default for every clip; motion with no story reads as noise.

items.title: Use celebrity, known-influencer lookalikes and cultural references from the {avatar}'s own researched world…
items.text: Use celebrity, known-influencer lookalikes and cultural references from the {avatar}'s own researched world (culture casting about 3), keeping each face slightly different from the real person.
items.why: Cultural references drive engagement while being funny and audience-aware; too close reads as the real person.
items.when: Casting and concept for any ad.

items.title: Dress promotional image ads in one concept from the {avatar}'s culture crossed with the moment (season or…
items.text: Dress promotional image ads in one concept from the {avatar}'s culture crossed with the moment (season or holiday): change what surfaces and props are made of, never the layout, camera or product placement; keep native posts at dressing 1.
items.why: Promotion image ads must stand out on feed and be themed; a dressed swipe that moves the layout is a different ad.

items.title: For a dressed promo ad, make the headline the concept talking with one spice device, never the sale's dates…
items.text: For a dressed promo ad, make the headline the concept talking with one spice device, never the sale's dates as a calendar, and print only the moment's own name on a real prop in the scene.
items.why: The concept carries the theme; dates-as-calendar is sterile.

items.title: Treat proven bar ads as moves to reach, never as ads to copy: a chain finds its own swipe's version of the…
items.text: Treat proven bar ads as moves to reach, never as ads to copy: a chain finds its own swipe's version of the move; copying one is a failure like a sterile ad.
items.why: The bar sets the level; copying it produces the same ad twice.
items.when: Using reference exemplars in creative chains.

items.title: Use the awareness preset to set dials: unaware is a post with no offer or call to action; problem-aware shows…
items.text: Use the awareness preset to set dials: unaware is a post with no offer or call to action; problem-aware shows and names the problem and reveals the cause; product proof carries proof, result and price inside an absurd picture.
items.why: Each awareness level needs a different mix of ad-likeness, valence and anchorage.
items.when: Setting a creative's target levels by awareness.

items.title: Test where the evidence is thin rather than treating it as law: absurdity 3 against 4, intensity 3 against 4,…
items.text: Test where the evidence is thin rather than treating it as law: absurdity 3 against 4, intensity 3 against 4, and UGC-against-polished realism are our own tests.
items.why: The moderate-incongruity sweet spot failed replication and the UGC evidence is thin.

items.title: Let the awareness level pick the story arc, map every beat of the arc to one doctrine section so the arc is…
items.text: Let the awareness level pick the story arc, map every beat of the arc to one doctrine section so the arc is the section plan, then close as the awareness level asks (offer, call to action, urgency only where true).
items.why: The arc IS the section plan; the close depends on awareness.
items.when: Scripting any ad or story-led piece.

items.title: Match arcs to awareness: unaware gets curiosity arcs (cold open, mystery box, kishotenketsu, escalation);…
items.text: Match arcs to awareness: unaware gets curiosity arcs (cold open, mystery box, kishotenketsu, escalation); problem-aware gets the fall (person in a hole, Icarus); solution-aware gets the failed fixes (Oedipus, epiphany bridge); product- and most-aware get the reveal (transformation, rags to riches).
items.why: Each awareness level needs a different shape to hold attention and move belief.

items.title: Use one arc per piece and nest devices inside it; a borrowed swipe keeps its arc unless the brief says why it…
items.text: Use one arc per piece and nest devices inside it; a borrowed swipe keeps its arc unless the brief says why it changes.
items.why: Two arcs in 30 s read as noise.

items.title: Name every story device used, and pay off every device that is set up.
items.text: Name every story device used, and pay off every device that is set up.
items.why: An unpaid setup leaves the viewer unsatisfied.

items.title: Deliver the claim inside the story, never as a break from it, and the claim must still be true.
items.text: Deliver the claim inside the story, never as a break from it, and the claim must still be true.
items.why: A viewer absorbed in a story argues back less; break the story to sell and the resistance comes back.

items.title: Give even an absurd piece one turn (a change); absurdity with no change is a meme, not an ad.
items.text: Give even an absurd piece one turn (a change); absurdity with no change is a meme, not an ad.
items.why: The turn is what connects the absurd to the sale.

items.title: End on the peak: design one peak and make the last 2 seconds the best feeling in the ad, with the offer…
items.text: End on the peak: design one peak and make the last 2 seconds the best feeling in the ad, with the offer riding on that feeling, never the offer alone.
items.why: People remember the most intense and the last moment, not the average.
items.when: Endings of video and story ads.

items.title: Join beats with 'but' and 'therefore', never 'and then'.
items.text: Join beats with 'but' and 'therefore', never 'and then'.
items.why: 'And then' feels like a list; causal beats feel like a story nobody scrolls away from.

items.title: Cast the viewer as the hero and the {brand} as the mentor who hands over the fix, never the hero.
items.text: Cast the viewer as the hero and the {brand} as the mentor who hands over the fix, never the hero.
items.why: The viewer must stay the hero for the story to be theirs.
items.when: Story ads using a guide or expert.

items.title: Make the villain the problem, the failed tool, the bad advice or the old way, never a real person, a named…
items.text: Make the villain the problem, the failed tool, the bad advice or the old way, never a real person, a named competitor or a group of people.
items.why: A shared enemy bonds the viewer, but naming real people or groups crosses the line.

items.title: Open two curiosity loops in the first 5 seconds and close the second one last; plant the product or clue in…
items.text: Open two curiosity loops in the first 5 seconds and close the second one last; plant the product or clue in the first 5 seconds so the ending feels earned.
items.why: An interrupted question stays in the mind until closed; a planted payoff feels earned, not sold.

items.title: Make the failed fix in a false-victory beat the competitor's category (the usual tool everyone already tried)…
items.text: Make the failed fix in a false-victory beat the competitor's category (the usual tool everyone already tried) and let it fail on screen; the product arrives only after the lowest point.
items.why: Showing failed solutions makes the real one land as the only one left.

items.title: Swing emotion once per 10 seconds (laughing to wincing, shame to pride) to keep arousal up.
items.text: Swing emotion once per 10 seconds (laughing to wincing, shame to pride) to keep arousal up.
items.why: Arousal drives sharing.

items.title: Use one exact specific detail per beat (the receipt, the timestamp, the cheap thing that failed), and mirror…
items.text: Use one exact specific detail per beat (the receipt, the timestamp, the cheap thing that failed), and mirror the viewer's situation using the {avatar}'s own research words verbatim.
items.why: Specific beats general every time; the viewer must think 'that's me'.

items.title: Make the lead's flaw funny, never contemptible, and give the lead an early likeable moment so the viewer is…
items.text: Make the lead's flaw funny, never contemptible, and give the lead an early likeable moment so the viewer is on their side.
items.why: The viewer must like the lead.

items.title: Refuse any persuasion trigger used without its truth: social proof with real numbers and customers only,…
items.text: Refuse any persuasion trigger used without its truth: social proof with real numbers and customers only, authority with no fake credential (an actor is a character), scarcity tied to a real moment or real stock, an anchor that is a real alternative at a real price, a reason that is true.
items.why: A trigger without its truth (a fake deadline, a fake crowd) is refused; the line is a guard, never a dial.
items.when: Every ad, offer and page using persuasion triggers.

items.title: Always give the mechanism, why it works, in one line.
items.text: Always give the mechanism, why it works, in one line.
items.why: A request with a reason gets more yeses, even a thin reason.

items.title: Sell who the viewer becomes, not the tool, and never shame who the viewer is now; aim shame at the problem,…
items.text: Sell who the viewer becomes, not the tool, and never shame who the viewer is now; aim shame at the problem, never the viewer.
items.why: People act to match who they think they are; viewer shame crosses the line.

items.title: Never use fear about a health problem the viewer does not have, and never promise a result the product does…
items.text: Never use fear about a health problem the viewer does not have, and never promise a result the product does not give.
items.why: Loss aversion and future pacing only work ethically within the truth.
items.when: Loss framing and future pacing in ads.

items.title: Push to the edge, never over: exaggeration everyone sees as a joke, taboo-adjacent humour, real public…
items.text: Push to the edge, never over: exaggeration everyone sees as a joke, taboo-adjacent humour, real public stories labelled as reported, real fears and embarrassment, lookalikes, uncomfortable truths about the category are allowed.
items.why: Going to the edge amplifies attention and dramatisation.

items.title: Never cross the edge line: no claim the product cannot back; no fake testimonial, review, crowd, expert or…
items.text: Never cross the edge line: no claim the product cannot back; no fake testimonial, review, crowd, expert or result presented as real; no fake deadline, stock or price; no real person named, impersonated or defamed; no mocking protected traits; no minors in anything risky; no real tragedy for laughs.
items.why: These break law, platform standards and trust.

items.title: Never fake membership in a real community or culture; speak as one of the audience's own only through their…
items.text: Never fake membership in a real community or culture; speak as one of the audience's own only through their real slang, world and references.
items.why: Unity persuades only when it is real.

items.title: Run every ad through the same flow: avatar and product, the idea (a working swipe or our own story),…
items.text: Run every ad through the same flow: avatar and product, the idea (a working swipe or our own story), awareness, arc, format and style, writing, brief review, audio first, cast/sets/scene pictures, hand-off, launch.
items.why: One flow keeps every ad comparable and gated.

items.title: Get the owner's sign-off at the fixed gates: idea, awareness, arc, brief review, audio, each cast/set/scene…
items.text: Get the owner's sign-off at the fixed gates: idea, awareness, arc, brief review, audio, each cast/set/scene picture, and the final launch click.
items.why: The owner checks each step before money is spent on the next.

items.title: Resolve who makes a video (AI, creator or founder) from the existing route and assignment before production;…
items.text: Resolve who makes a video (AI, creator or founder) from the existing route and assignment before production; if unknown and production depends on it, ask once, and never default to AI because the asset is video.
items.why: The maker route decides the whole production chain; a broad video type does not choose it.

items.title: Treat each stage as its own operation with its own authorization: inspect, plan, write, produce, package,…
items.text: Treat each stage as its own operation with its own authorization: inspect, plan, write, produce, package, upload and launch; an approved brief, a checklist tick, an inventory row or a reviewer comment does not authorize production, sending, spend or deployment.
items.why: Crossing stages without authority spends money or ships work nobody approved.

items.title: Make the brief the only seam into production: the teardown is the only input to writing, the brief is the…
items.text: Make the brief the only seam into production: the teardown is the only input to writing, the brief is the only thing that crosses to production, and finished copy is the only input to email design.
items.why: Single seams keep each stage's input explicit and checkable.

items.title: Never take an ad live from the production line: every finished ad is filed for approval and the go-live is…
items.text: Never take an ad live from the production line: every finished ad is filed for approval and the go-live is the owner's click; email is drafted and scheduled only through a person's explicit approval, never sent directly.
items.why: Going live and sending are the owner's calls.
items.when: Ad upload, email upload and launch.

items.title: Make each review change one recut or one image edit, a single change off the approved baseline.
items.text: Make each review change one recut or one image edit, a single change off the approved baseline.
items.why: One change per edit keeps cause and effect clear and preserves the baseline.
items.when: Ad review cycles for video and statics.

items.title: Feed results back into writing: audit what spent, bank the winners, hand the top ads to the hook stage, and…
items.text: Feed results back into writing: audit what spent, bank the winners, hand the top ads to the hook stage, and score results back to the prompts and borrowed winners that wrote each ad.
items.why: Results, not opinion, decide what the next creative borrows from.

items.title: Send recorded corrections upstream to the highest owning source (brand fact, definition, prompt, engine or…
items.text: Send recorded corrections upstream to the highest owning source (brand fact, definition, prompt, engine or skill), but do not rewrite shared definitions when a correction is only an item-specific choice.
items.why: Fixing the source makes the fix compound; item choices should not pollute shared rules.

items.title: Treat a variation of a proven winner (new format or hook) as a new cut that goes through the same checks as…
items.text: Treat a variation of a proven winner (new format or hook) as a new cut that goes through the same checks as any ad.
items.why: Variations carry the same risks as new ads.

items.title: Keep storefront promos, acquisition funnels and email as separate surfaces: a store go is not a funnel…
items.text: Keep storefront promos, acquisition funnels and email as separate surfaces: a store go is not a funnel deployment go, and a measurement check never deploys a funnel or changes an ad account.
items.why: Each surface has its own offers, gates and owners.

items.title: Name every file so spend joins back to the ad.
items.text: Name every file so spend joins back to the ad.
items.why: Without the join, results cannot be traced to the creative that earned them.
items.when: Naming before filing ads for approval.

items.title: A route map, prepared activation brief or inventory report is not an executed workflow; report the current…
items.text: A route map, prepared activation brief or inventory report is not an executed workflow; report the current station, the actual output, the held reason and the next action.
items.why: Plans are not results; reporting must state what is true.

items.title: Write email-flow and page copy from brand files and language-bank rows cited by row id, with a sources table;…
items.text: Write email-flow and page copy from brand files and language-bank rows cited by row id, with a sources table; drafts only, nothing scheduled, sent, built or published.
items.why: Cited language keeps copy traceable to real customer words.
items.when: Email flows and landing/product/upsell page copy.

items.title: Merge copies before ranking creatives: re-cuts of one script, the same ad sent to different landing pages,…
items.text: Merge copies before ranking creatives: re-cuts of one script, the same ad sent to different landing pages, renames, and ads that open on the same footage (hook band ignored) count as one creative.
items.why: Unmerged duplicates filled the top list with the same ad and distorted the ranking.
items.when: Ad account analysis, any creative ranking

items.title: Define the core creatives as the smallest set carrying 60% of purchases and break those down first; widen to…
items.text: Define the core creatives as the smallest set carrying 60% of purchases and break those down first; widen to 70% and 90% tiers only after.
items.why: The top-10% cut had a long tail of small sellers; the purchases are carried by a few creatives.
items.when: Ad account analysis, choosing what to tear down

items.title: For this year's video analysis keep only creatives with $2,500+ spend, ranked by purchases; for last year…
items.text: For this year's video analysis keep only creatives with $2,500+ spend, ranked by purchases; for last year keep the top 40 by purchases (video and image).
items.why: Real spend behind a creative is needed before its numbers mean anything.

items.title: Measure video attention as hook = 3-second views / impressions, hold = ThruPlays / 3-second views, watched to…
items.text: Measure video attention as hook = 3-second views / impressions, hold = ThruPlays / 3-second views, watched to end = 100% views / 3-second views.
items.why: One fixed formula makes videos comparable across ads and years.

items.title: Tag what is on screen by looking at each ad's picture, never from the ad name, and lead with the creative…
items.text: Tag what is on screen by looking at each ad's picture, never from the ad name, and lead with the creative (image or video); copy is read second, for messaging only.
items.why: Ad names lie about the visual, and the creative is what the owner cares about first.

items.title: Tag each top ad with the one message it leads with, from a fixed per-{brand} list whose names stay stable,…
items.text: Tag each top ad with the one message it leads with, from a fixed per-{brand} list whose names stay stable, and total ads, share of purchases and cost per purchase per message per year.
items.why: Core messages are what new formats must carry to land.

items.title: Show whole-store revenue (ad funnel, website, app, renewals) beside ad spend; treat pixel ROAS as…
items.text: Show whole-store revenue (ad funnel, website, app, renewals) beside ad spend; treat pixel ROAS as understating the store and ad-driven lift as unproven until shown.
items.why: The business doesn't run in a vacuum and most revenue can arrive outside the ad funnel.

items.title: Treat a gap in a data source as missing data, not as zero activity; source older numbers from the platform…
items.text: Treat a gap in a data source as missing data, not as zero activity; source older numbers from the platform rather than reading the gap as ads off.
items.why: Zero spend rows before a warehouse starts are missing data, not ads turned off.

items.title: An analysis page reports facts only; the owner decides what to prioritise, cut or scale.
items.text: An analysis page reports facts only; the owner decides what to prioritise, cut or scale.
items.why: Keeps the read separate from the call that is his.

items.title: Before trusting an analysis, reconcile its 7-day spend to within a few percent of the ad platform for the…
items.text: Before trusting an analysis, reconcile its 7-day spend to within a few percent of the ad platform for the same dates and spot-check that tags on the top 8 match the pictures.
items.why: A report that doesn't tie to the platform can't drive decisions.

items.title: After an account analysis, reset creative from the evidence: put the top 10% of creatives on one study board…
items.text: After an account analysis, reset creative from the evidence: put the top 10% of creatives on one study board sorted founder / creator / B-roll and cuts / statics, tear them down in purchase order (message, funnel position, positioning, copy style), then swipe the formats of a brand winning now with a similar {avatar} and inject our distilled message.
items.why: New ads should be built from what has actually sold plus what is winning now.
items.when: Creative reset after an account audit

items.title: In teardowns of past winners treat the founder's involvement as irrelevant: only what was executed counts,…
items.text: In teardowns of past winners treat the founder's involvement as irrelevant: only what was executed counts, and the {avatar} must not depend on the {founder}.
items.why: The system must scale without the founder in the ad.

items.title: Use cheaper models only where quality can't suffer; judgement work such as creative tagging stays on the top…
items.text: Use cheaper models only where quality can't suffer; judgement work such as creative tagging stays on the top model.
items.why: Cost savings must not degrade the read that drives decisions.

items.title: Borrow a persuasion mechanic, never the bet: the customer always receives what they paid for and no money is…
items.text: Borrow a persuasion mechanic, never the bet: the customer always receives what they paid for and no money is ever at risk on chance.
items.why: Each mechanic must serve the outcome the customer came for, not gamble with it.
items.when: Any offer, page, email or ad mechanic

items.title: Give each asset one lead conversion mechanic; a second may support it; more than two is a defect.
items.text: Give each asset one lead conversion mechanic; a second may support it; more than two is a defect.
items.why: One clear point gets the response.

items.title: Pick measured mechanics first (visible progress, head start, real scarcity, routine streak, triggered…
items.text: Pick measured mechanics first (visible progress, head start, real scarcity, routine streak, triggered message, risk reversal, top customers served first); run an unproven mechanic only as a test with a holdout, read on its metric, then promote or cut it on the numbers.
items.why: Evidence-backed mechanics move numbers; untested ones must earn their place.

items.title: Every conversion mechanic names the number it moves: cost per click, cost per conversion, order value, upsell…
items.text: Every conversion mechanic names the number it moves: cost per click, cost per conversion, order value, upsell take rate, subscription rate, repeat rate or email revenue.
items.why: Work that can't be tied to a number doesn't get done.

items.title: Every fact a mechanic shows (count, deadline, stock level, price, tier) comes from live data; if a fact is…
items.text: Every fact a mechanic shows (count, deadline, stock level, price, tier) comes from live data; if a fact is missing, drop the mechanic, never estimate it.
items.why: Fake counts and limits are both a legal risk and a broken promise.
items.when: Scarcity, deadlines, counts, tiers in any asset

items.title: Scarcity and deadlines must be real: name the true size of the run or live units left, state the real end…
items.text: Scarcity and deadlines must be real: name the true size of the run or live units left, state the real end date, show a countdown only when the offer truly ends at zero, and never reset it.
items.why: A timer alone showed no lift, and fake limits break consumer-protection rules.

items.title: Lead risk reversal with the guarantee as the reason to try, put it directly under the buy button, state…
items.text: Lead risk reversal with the guarantee as the reason to try, put it directly under the buy button, state exactly what comes back and how, and never use the word risk-free.
items.why: Money-back framing had the strongest effect among offers tested; risk-free is a flagged term.

items.title: Send direct messages on the customer's own moment (routine day, run-out date, tier change, viewed drop), not…
items.text: Send direct messages on the customer's own moment (routine day, run-out date, tier change, viewed drop), not the calendar, with one alert per real event and the customer setting the volume.
items.why: Direct messages drive spend, and relevance to the customer's moment is what makes them work.

items.title: Identify the top customer tier and serve it directly: lookalikes built from it, personal notes, first access…
items.text: Identify the top customer tier and serve it directly: lookalikes built from it, personal notes, first access and early allocation.
items.why: A small share of accounts produces most revenue.

items.title: Never tie a prize picked by chance to a purchase: everyone in the offer gets the same item, or free entry has…
items.text: Never tie a prize picked by chance to a purchase: everyone in the offer gets the same item, or free entry has equal chance; a chance promotion over $5,000 in prizes must be filed and bonded before it starts.
items.why: Prize plus chance plus consideration is an illegal lottery.

items.title: Any former price shown must be one regularly offered, and the shown price must be what is paid.
items.text: Any former price shown must be one regularly offered, and the shown price must be what is paid.
items.why: Reference-price rules bar fake markdowns and drip pricing.

items.title: Reviews and customer stories must be real, with paid or given connections disclosed and rewards never tied to…
items.text: Reviews and customer stories must be real, with paid or given connections disclosed and rewards never tied to sentiment; every result claim needs evidence, cosmetic wording and typical results disclosed.
items.why: Endorsement and claims rules apply to every asset.

items.title: State recurring terms before purchase with express consent and a simple way to stop, and message only…
items.text: State recurring terms before purchase with express consent and a simple way to stop, and message only customers who opted in to that channel, honoring stop.
items.why: Subscription and messaging consent laws apply.

items.title: On paid social and social shops avoid spins, wheels, raffles and sweepstakes, barred before-and-after…
items.text: On paid social and social shops avoid spins, wheels, raffles and sweepstakes, barred before-and-after comparisons, statements of physical inferiority and implied personal attributes; read the policies on launch day.
items.why: Platform ad and shop policies reject these.
items.when: Paid social and social commerce assets

items.title: Show value in plain terms: one number the viewer can check in their head, price per day and what is in the…
items.text: Show value in plain terms: one number the viewer can check in their head, price per day and what is in the box, and total, saving and what ships beside the button.
items.why: Unfamiliar notation hides what is on offer.

items.title: Run creative as one loop: take what works, tear down things that are working that we haven't made yet, inject…
items.text: Run creative as one loop: take what works, tear down things that are working that we haven't made yet, inject what works into them, and create new ideas from there.
items.why: Market evidence and winners, not taste, feed every new brief.

items.title: When swiping paid ads, filter to ads running at least 14 days, and also check the top creative of the last 30…
items.text: When swiping paid ads, filter to ads running at least 14 days, and also check the top creative of the last 30 days.
items.why: Fourteen days filters out new tests that haven't proven themselves.

items.title: Choose swipe references for the mechanism and market evidence they reveal, inside and outside the category,…
items.text: Choose swipe references for the mechanism and market evidence they reveal, inside and outside the category, across direct response, education, entertainment, community and brand content, naming each asset's job and intended distribution; demographic similarity alone is not a reason.
items.why: The mechanism is what transfers to our offer.

items.title: Adapt sale creatives by moving them to the most-aware stage while keeping their message and positioning.
items.text: Adapt sale creatives by moving them to the most-aware stage while keeping their message and positioning.
items.why: Sale ads work on the already-aware buyer.

items.title: Reuse an existing teardown that is substantially similar to a new swipe; redo one only when nothing close…
items.text: Reuse an existing teardown that is substantially similar to a new swipe; redo one only when nothing close exists, and map the combination frame by frame against both videos before writing.
items.why: Teardowns take time; the map prevents writing blind.

items.title: Use the {brand}'s real offer; a source ad never establishes facts about our product or dictates an original…
items.text: Use the {brand}'s real offer; a source ad never establishes facts about our product or dictates an original idea's execution.
items.why: Swipes give structure, not facts.

items.title: Every brief gets 5 unique variants: same message, different execution, all around one winner that is actually…
items.text: Every brief gets 5 unique variants: same message, different execution, all around one winner that is actually scaled.
items.why: That is how creative diversity and new formats turn up through a clear process.

items.title: Decide the writing line's gates and small creative calls by the winner, the piece's rulings and the decision…
items.text: Decide the writing line's gates and small creative calls by the winner, the piece's rulings and the decision framework, logging each in one line; the owner reviews finished briefs.
items.why: Questions along the way slow the owner; his time goes to finished work.

items.title: Compare human footage and AI executions on observed results for the format and market; never assume a…
items.text: Compare human footage and AI executions on observed results for the format and market; never assume a universal performance winner.
items.why: Results decide, not opinion.

items.title: Use video generation only where needed to amplify; build montages from owned raw UGC with old captions zoomed…
items.text: Use video generation only where needed to amplify; build montages from owned raw UGC with old captions zoomed or cut out and new ones on top; a format that is fully AI stays fully AI.
items.why: The AI process is not all AI, and overcomplicating a format hurts it.

items.title: When spoken words change, reconcile the picture and literal captions with them; a changed spoken line never…
items.text: When spoken words change, reconcile the picture and literal captions with them; a changed spoken line never approves a replacement proof or offer card, which stays traceable to its own evidence.
items.why: Picture must show what is said, and proof must stay sourced.

items.title: Build voiceover in natural same-speaker chunks, not one call per line, preserving the actual speaker routing.
items.text: Build voiceover in natural same-speaker chunks, not one call per line, preserving the actual speaker routing.
items.why: Line-by-line reads sound stitched; conversations are not one narrator.

items.title: Keep the real-footage control as cuts from actually captured words and actions; any newly written AI skit is…
items.text: Keep the real-footage control as cuts from actually captured words and actions; any newly written AI skit is a separately identified variant, and a clip's mouth must match before an edited sentence is assigned to it.
items.why: The control must stay a true read of real footage.

items.title: Every scene card states the exact words and speaker, first picture, action on the words, end picture,…
items.text: Every scene card states the exact words and speaker, first picture, action on the words, end picture, framing, sound, captions, proof layer, asset source and execution route.
items.why: A complete scene spec is what makes a brief producible without questions.

items.title: Keep technical failures (routing, schema, run recovery, IDs) with the agents; never return them to the owner…
items.text: Keep technical failures (routing, schema, run recovery, IDs) with the agents; never return them to the owner as creative decisions.
items.why: Creative choices must stay separate from service faults.

items.title: Review every static panel at its intended aspect ratio with its exact headline, body, CTA, product placement…
items.text: Review every static panel at its intended aspect ratio with its exact headline, body, CTA, product placement and proof layer before maker handoff.
items.why: Statics are judged as they will run.

items.title: Treat the current winning audience as evidence about one segment, not a boundary: segment by desired outcome,…
items.text: Treat the current winning audience as evidence about one segment, not a boundary: segment by desired outcome, problem, use context and awareness, and research other ages, skin tones and communities without assigning preferences from appearance.
items.why: Growth needs new segments while winners keep running.

items.title: Treat broad desires (confidence, attraction, clear skin, glow) as hypotheses whose local importance,…
items.text: Treat broad desires (confidence, attraction, clear skin, glow) as hypotheses whose local importance, vocabulary, proof and presentation need market evidence.
items.why: One audience's response is not proof that everyone shares it.

items.title: For new concept exploration set creativity and diversity controls to their highest settings and vary…
items.text: For new concept exploration set creativity and diversity controls to their highest settings and vary concepts, angles, formats, cast, settings, tone, visual treatment, hooks and channels; changing only a face, language or caption is not a new concept.
items.why: Breadth across the portfolio finds new winners; breadth does not require every piece to be loud.

items.title: Use a swipe to explain a mechanism (what earns attention, activates desire, builds belief, prompts action),…
items.text: Use a swipe to explain a mechanism (what earns attention, activates desire, builds belief, prompts action), separate observed performance from the hypothesis of why it worked, and build an original execution; exact replication is for commissioned remakes or controlled comparisons only.
items.why: Copying execution without the mechanism doesn't transfer.

items.title: Keep one desire and argument per asset while the portfolio explores many; run new hypotheses beside proven…
items.text: Keep one desire and argument per asset while the portfolio explores many; run new hypotheses beside proven controls, name the question each test answers, and keep winning work running while opening new markets.
items.why: Testing must not starve what already scales.

items.title: Count distinct concepts, useful variations, shipped content and results separately; treat capacity targets as…
items.text: Count distinct concepts, useful variations, shipped content and results separately; treat capacity targets as ambitions until throughput, cost, failure rate and distribution are measured.
items.why: Rendered files alone are not the outcome.

items.title: Audit market sales by shipping country with test, canceled and unpaid orders excluded, refunds shown…
items.text: Audit market sales by shipping country with test, canceled and unpaid orders excluded, refunds shown separately, new purchases split from renewals, never parcels for purchases and never ethnicity inferred from country; rank markets only once coverage and marketing exposure are explicit.
items.why: Low historical sales can reflect no marketing or restricted availability.

items.title: Localize language first across the whole buying journey (navigation, offer, proof, cart, checkout,…
items.text: Localize language first across the whole buying journey (navigation, offer, proof, cart, checkout, subscription terms, follow-ups) with local language review, then adapt content, cast, demos, settings and proof from market research.
items.why: A translated page is only an initial language version, not a local experience.

items.title: Pair every localized creative test with a matching destination, checking market status, catalog availability,…
items.text: Pair every localized creative test with a matching destination, checking market status, catalog availability, currency, price, delivery and working checkout separately.
items.why: Creative and journey must agree for a test to read.

items.title: Expand markets through bounded pilots compared to the relevant control: keep what works and expand, carrying…
items.text: Expand markets through bounded pilots compared to the relevant control: keep what works and expand, carrying market and language through creative identity, landing page and results.
items.why: Learning must return to the next idea.

items.title: Hold the evergreen traffic map under every moment: paid ads land on the funnel with the funnel's own offer,…
items.text: Hold the evergreen traffic map under every moment: paid ads land on the funnel with the funnel's own offer, email and SMS land on the storefront order, organic posts land on the quiz with no price, and new store visitors get the standing sign-up opt-in; a moment changes an offer line, never where traffic goes.
items.why: Stable destinations keep tracking and offers clean.
items.when: Holiday and promo planning, every channel

items.title: Keep the funnel offer and the store/email offer as separate lines: a funnel price never appears in email, SMS…
items.text: Keep the funnel offer and the store/email offer as separate lines: a funnel price never appears in email, SMS or the storefront, and a store bundle offer never runs on a funnel ad.
items.why: Funnel offers leak and confuse the price a customer sees.
items.when: Offers across funnel, store, email, SMS

items.title: Most calendar moments are content moments: never invent an offer; promos are founder-set, and the owner names…
items.text: Most calendar moments are content moments: never invent an offer; promos are founder-set, and the owner names each month's moment offers (or 'content') before the month's calendar triggers.
items.why: Promos are the owner's call and a monthly moment is not a sale.

items.title: Read the live page before repeating any record's claim about it; a mismatch between page and record is listed…
items.text: Read the live page before repeating any record's claim about it; a mismatch between page and record is listed as a gap, and neither side changes without the owner's word.
items.why: Records go stale before pages do.

items.title: Check every send's and asset's facts and customer language against its own {brand}; never carry facts or…
items.text: Check every send's and asset's facts and customer language against its own {brand}; never carry facts or customer rows across brands.
items.why: Brand facts bleed between brands.

items.title: Start a holiday moment's work when it is within 6 weeks, using the holiday cadence's lead days (a Black…
items.text: Start a holiday moment's work when it is within 6 weeks, using the holiday cadence's lead days (a Black Friday sale opens 7 days early) over older dates.
items.why: Assets and offers need lead time and the cadence file wins over old pages.

items.title: After every promo window, read orders and CPA per day against last year and write keep / change / drop for…
items.text: After every promo window, read orders and CPA per day against last year and write keep / change / drop for next year's same moment.
items.why: Each moment compounds when its result feeds next year.

items.title: Write a swipe against the banked winner closest to it in format (length, pace, tone, format, structure,…
items.text: Write a swipe against the banked winner closest to it in format (length, pace, tone, format, structure, hook), not one fixed winner.
items.why: The nearest winner transfers best into the swipe's shape.
items.when: Writing a new ad from a swipe

items.title: Write in one of two lanes chosen on purpose: winner plus swipe, or swipe only for a new {brand} or {offer}…
items.text: Write in one of two lanes chosen on purpose: winner plus swipe, or swipe only for a new {brand} or {offer} with no winners yet.
items.why: Without winners, the swipe alone carries the structure.

items.title: The owner picks the swipes; do not pick them for him, and run paid teardowns and writing only on his go.
items.text: The owner picks the swipes; do not pick them for him, and run paid teardowns and writing only on his go.
items.why: Swipe choice and spend are his calls.

items.title: A scene edited after approval loses its approval, and a prepared handoff is withdrawn if anything changes.
items.text: A scene edited after approval loses its approval, and a prepared handoff is withdrawn if anything changes.
items.why: Only what was approved may go to production.

items.title: No handoff, message or upload goes out without the owner's word that time.
items.text: No handoff, message or upload goes out without the owner's word that time.
items.why: Sending is his call, per action.

items.title: Count sign-ups from every source and cross-check against the SMS tool's counts; one list is never all…
items.text: Count sign-ups from every source and cross-check against the SMS tool's counts; one list is never all sign-ups.
items.why: Reading one list made a brand look like it had no sign-ups.

items.title: Split orders by their real source (funnel orders synced into the store, samples, refills), count customer…
items.text: Split orders by their real source (funnel orders synced into the store, samples, refills), count customer orders only, and count a mirrored order and its copy within 12 hours once.
items.why: Splitting by integration alone put most funnel orders on the store.

items.title: Set each flow's send times from the measured time-to-buy curve for its own trigger, store and funnel apart…
items.text: Set each flow's send times from the measured time-to-buy curve for its own trigger, store and funnel apart (median, 75th percentile, share of buyers by 10 min through 90 days).
items.why: Send timing should follow when buyers actually buy.

items.title: Measure a flow's lift with a 50/50 random split inside the flow; before/after months don't measure it and…
items.text: Measure a flow's lift with a 50/50 random split inside the flow; before/after months don't measure it and platform-credited revenue is only an upper bound.
items.why: Traffic volume and mix move too much between months.

items.title: Before comparing periods, check that a trigger's conversion is comparable; an event can change source between…
items.text: Before comparing periods, check that a trigger's conversion is comparable; an event can change source between periods.
items.why: A source change made one trigger's conversion fall from 86% to 17%.

items.title: A metric that drops to 0 while its source still has orders is a cut connection, not a real drop.
items.text: A metric that drops to 0 while its source still has orders is a cut connection, not a real drop.
items.why: Lost integrations silently zero metrics.

items.title: Open every pop-up's button link: the destination must carry the offer the pop-up promises.
items.text: Open every pop-up's button link: the destination must carry the offer the pop-up promises.
items.why: A pop-up can promise an offer the page doesn't have.

items.title: A chat lane or sidebar group is not the maker route, and a lane map or prepared brief never activates…
items.text: A chat lane or sidebar group is not the maker route, and a lane map or prepared brief never activates generation, spend, sending or deployment.
items.why: Each operation stops at its own boundary.

items.title: Before spending on generation, record a preflight and run a dry run of the actual request; compare resolved…
items.text: Before spending on generation, record a preflight and run a dry run of the actual request; compare resolved model, resolution, references and stages with the rules and brief, never substituting remembered defaults or another run's settings.
items.why: The request must match the rules before money is spent.

items.title: Every image or video, personal and experimental work included, goes through the established production entry…
items.text: Every image or video, personal and experimental work included, goes through the established production entry point; direct vendor calls and scratch scripts are not routes around it, and a missing door is work to repair, not permission to bypass.
items.why: One process keeps every check in force.

items.title: When a production route fails, diagnose the concrete failure and keep every required stage and check; never…
items.text: When a production route fails, diagnose the concrete failure and keep every required stage and check; never claim a missing check passed.
items.why: Skipped checks ship faults.

items.title: Before every video-scene generation, show the complete resolved setup (every input in order with previews,…
items.text: Before every video-scene generation, show the complete resolved setup (every input in order with previews, the full exact prompt, beats, camera, model, duration, resolution, seed) and keep approved scene, cast, wardrobe, motion and settings unless the owner asks for a change or a documented failure needs a targeted repair.
items.why: What is reviewed must be exactly what is sent, and approved parts must not drift.

items.title: On a generation timeout, reconcile the existing job before submitting again, and freeze each take's request,…
items.text: On a generation timeout, reconcile the existing job before submitting again, and freeze each take's request, media and job ID; proposed changes go in a separate next-take setup, never overwriting history.
items.why: Duplicate submissions waste money and lost history breaks learning.

items.title: Handle every email thread so the reply is complete the first time: read every message and attachment, list…
items.text: Handle every email thread so the reply is complete the first time: read every message and attachment, list what was asked and what the next step needs, answer every question, attach every requested file, ask every open question in the same email, and when there is a deadline ask for a date that beats it.
items.why: Back-and-forth costs time; gaps found up front close the thread.
items.when: Any correspondence handled for the owner

items.title: Fill answers from existing records first and check hard dates (weekends, holidays, expiry) and…
items.text: Fill answers from existing records first and check hard dates (weekends, holidays, expiry) and contradictions; ask the owner once, naming exactly what is missing, who has it and the shortest way to get it, with choices.
items.why: Don't ask what a file or search can answer.

items.title: Keep personal documents, identity numbers and contact details private and local; reference identity numbers…
items.text: Keep personal documents, identity numbers and contact details private and local; reference identity numbers by the document that holds them, never copy them into shared records.
items.why: Personal data must not reach team surfaces.

items.title: Keep current checkout offers and existing customer contracts as separate scopes: 'every subscription offer'…
items.text: Keep current checkout offers and existing customer contracts as separate scopes: 'every subscription offer' means every current checkout offer, never permission to rewrite active, paused or historical contracts.
items.why: A checkout request was once misread as permission to change historical contracts.

items.title: Grade subscription evidence as configured, checkout-observed or order-proven; a correct price, an active…
items.text: Grade subscription evidence as configured, checkout-observed or order-proven; a correct price, an active flow, a page claim or a discount is not proof of the checkout or refill result.
items.why: Configuration and real outcomes diverge.

items.title: Refill wording names the actual refill contents without renaming the initial product, and billing units and…
items.text: Refill wording names the actual refill contents without renaming the initial product, and billing units and pack quantities are preserved, never converted to make labels look consistent.
items.why: Ambiguous refill text misleads buyers about what recurs.

items.title: Never place a test order, charge, notify customers or publish just to prove an audit; mark the…
items.text: Never place a test order, charge, notify customers or publish just to prove an audit; mark the next-real-order check as unproven.
items.why: Audits must not touch customers or money.

items.title: Before a live store write, save the before-state and a restoration path; read back an uncertain write before…
items.text: Before a live store write, save the before-state and a restoration path; read back an uncertain write before retrying; after a review rejection, never split the rejected scope into smaller writes.
items.why: Live changes must be reversible and within approval.

items.title: Each video version gets a custom cover worth running traffic to: the strongest frame of that version's own…
items.text: Each video version gets a custom cover worth running traffic to: the strongest frame of that version's own video blended with a concept from the covers its {avatar} sees on Explore, pushed.
items.why: A plain frame with words reads flat.

items.title: Give each version's cover a different moment (face mid-reaction, the problem close, hands on it), take the…
items.text: Give each version's cover a different moment (face mid-reaction, the problem close, hands on it), take the swipe cover's move not its picture, push one thing about five times past real so the hook line reads literally, and use the version's headline in the swipe's type.
items.why: Covers must be distinct and stop the scroll at phone size.

items.title: Make covers only through the image production process: no type layer, split or hand compositing afterward, a…
items.text: Make covers only through the image production process: no type layer, split or hand compositing afterward, a fault is fixed in the tool, and covers are final before approval.
items.why: Covers without a production record are refused at the approval gate.

items.title: Check every cover: each face against its cast sheet, nothing on a face or lips, words exact, product true to…
items.text: Check every cover: each face against its cast sheet, nothing on a face or lips, words exact, product true to its kit, every cover a different picture that reads at phone size.
items.why: Covers are what the viewer sees first.

items.title: Make an AI video scene as one continuous take: write the staging and every line with its speaker, make cast…
items.text: Make an AI video scene as one continuous take: write the staging and every line with its speaker, make cast sheets, the first frame and each person's own voice, preview the motion and get approval before any paid print, and state the take's cost.
items.why: The one process that worked so far.

items.title: Check every printed take for the right people, every line in order, a real product and no text; a miss is…
items.text: Check every printed take for the right people, every line in order, a real product and no text; a miss is reprinted, never patched.
items.why: Patching hides faults that recur.

items.title: Never use a swipe's footage directly as the motion reference; track poses only, and the motion video must…
items.text: Never use a swipe's footage directly as the motion reference; track poses only, and the motion video must show our action.
items.why: Swipe footage leaks its people and edits into the take.

items.title: Hand outside partners direction only: nothing from personal context, logs, legal or other work, and never…
items.text: Hand outside partners direction only: nothing from personal context, logs, legal or other work, and never keys.
items.why: Partners need the instruction, not the owner's private record.

items.title: Every partner message carries the partner's one page link, opening on what's new, then the pieces to open,…
items.text: Every partner message carries the partner's one page link, opening on what's new, then the pieces to open, then the next step; never send a prompt on its own.
items.why: A prompt sent without a link left the partner asking for one.

items.title: Each partner stays in their own lane: their own repo, their own AI tools and keys; no company tools on a…
items.text: Each partner stays in their own lane: their own repo, their own AI tools and keys; no company tools on a partner's private work unless agreed.
items.why: Keeps partner work and company resources separate.

items.title: Route work to a function (video editor, designer, funnel, offer), never to a named person; a roster says who…
items.text: Route work to a function (video editor, designer, funnel, offer), never to a named person; a roster says who fills each role now.
items.why: Roles outlast the people who fill them.

items.title: Group open work by the business task it serves, not by lane: two pieces that end in the same output, page or…
items.text: Group open work by the business task it serves, not by lane: two pieces that end in the same output, page or repo belong under one main; before closing any, carry forward items waiting on the owner's word, a live change, spend or a send.
items.why: Merged mains cut overlap without dropping pending decisions.

items.title: In research reports, groups are filters, not rankings: report what was found, where and when, flag loose name…
items.text: In research reports, groups are filters, not rankings: report what was found, where and when, flag loose name matches, and make no 'best leads' calls.
items.why: Name joins can be two different companies; ranking claims outrun the evidence.

items.title: A data source returning 0 signals or a fetch error means the source changed or blocked the scan; fix it…
items.text: A data source returning 0 signals or a fetch error means the source changed or blocked the scan; fix it before publishing.
items.why: A silent zero reads as a real finding.

items.title: On official applications, never infer legal declarations, religion, nationality, history or contacts from…
items.text: On official applications, never infer legal declarations, religion, nationality, history or contacts from defaults; leave final truth declarations, submission and payment to the owner, and never present an unsuccessful attempt as complete.
items.why: Declarations and payment are legally his.
items.when: Official forms done for the owner

items.title: Before making any asset, look for it: an exact-key hit is reused; a hit on every must-match tag (for a…
items.text: Before making any asset, look for it: an exact-key hit is reused; a hit on every must-match tag (for a person: role, sex, age band, ethnicity) is reused or varied; a new item beside a tag hit needs a written reason; a miss is made once through the one route for that kind.
items.why: The same thing was being made many times under different names.
items.when: Before making, buying or generating any reusable asset

items.title: Never resend a rejected recipe: change a setting and name the change; every rejection carries its reason in…
items.text: Never resend a rejected recipe: change a setting and name the change; every rejection carries its reason in words, and 'something else' counts as no reason.
items.why: Repeating a rejected recipe wastes money and teaches nothing.

items.title: Order reusable assets by results: exact key first, then tag hits with results by lowest cost per purchase…
items.text: Order reusable assets by results: exact key first, then tag hits with results by lowest cost per purchase then lowest cost per click, then tag hits with no results newest first; use count never orders them, and numbers count only above the owner's volume bar.
items.why: Results, not popularity, decide what gets reused.

items.title: Name a reusable person by role and demographic, never by the ad they were made for.
items.text: Name a reusable person by role and demographic, never by the ad they were made for.
items.why: Per-ad names hide reusable cast.

items.title: An improvement lands once, in its one home, and reaches every run from there: a ruling that changes a tool…
items.text: An improvement lands once, in its one home, and reaches every run from there: a ruling that changes a tool also lands as the tool fix, a better asset supersedes and retires the old one, and a replaced rule is deleted from its old file.
items.why: Fixes that live in copies drift and don't compound.
items.when: Any rule, prompt, tool or asset change

items.title: Originals are never deleted after a copy.
items.text: Originals are never deleted after a copy.
items.why: Copies drift; the original is the fallback.

items.title: Lock {avatar}, angle and format before cutting anything, and check every later pick (creator, AI shot,…
items.text: Lock {avatar}, angle and format before cutting anything, and check every later pick (creator, AI shot, supporting character, proof, music) against those three.
items.why: Many faces and wrong-avatar proof broke earlier cuts.

items.title: Swipes are the baseline: every swipe shot becomes one of our shots in the swipe's order, and only the owner…
items.text: Swipes are the baseline: every swipe shot becomes one of our shots in the swipe's order, and only the owner leaves one out.
items.why: Unless told otherwise, the swipe's proven structure is leveraged.

items.title: Each shot keeps its swipe shot's share of the scene; no minimum shot length or shot-per-line rule is…
items.text: Each shot keeps its swipe shot's share of the scene; no minimum shot length or shot-per-line rule is hard-coded.
items.why: Replaces the 1.5 s minimum of 7 Nov; hard-coded lengths created problems and lost the swipe's rhythm.

items.title: Judge every shot against its swipe shot on the pictures; a weak or missing copy fails, and is filled from…
items.text: Judge every shot against its swipe shot on the pictures; a weak or missing copy fails, and is filled from owned footage first, then an AI shot from the swipe's frame and the face master, then a creator shoot when the product is in the shot.
items.why: A clip at the right length is not a copy.

items.title: The product is never AI-drawn as the hero: product actions are real footage and any product on screen comes…
items.text: The product is never AI-drawn as the hero: product actions are real footage and any product on screen comes from real photos or the product kit.
items.why: Drawn products look fake and misrepresent the product.

items.title: The brief names a shot for every line, and a talking selfie never stands in for a named shot.
items.text: The brief names a shot for every line, and a talking selfie never stands in for a named shot.
items.why: It's still an ad: the planned scene types sell.

items.title: Proof and supporting characters match the {avatar}: bad skin is followed by that same person clear, and…
items.text: Proof and supporting characters match the {avatar}: bad skin is followed by that same person clear, and before/afters come from the same avatar.
items.why: Wrong-avatar proof breaks belief.

items.title: Use one demographic (gender, ethnicity, age band) for the whole edit, hands-only shots included; the…
items.text: Use one demographic (gender, ethnicity, age band) for the whole edit, hands-only shots included; the {founder}'s footage is not the {avatar}.
items.why: Mixed ages and ethnicities broke the avatar match.

items.title: Every claim and everything the narration names (offer item, product, ingredient, body part, action) gets a…
items.text: Every claim and everything the narration names (offer item, product, ingredient, body part, action) gets a shot depicting it, taken from owned footage when it exists.
items.why: Narration over unrelated footage wastes the line.

items.title: Vary the cut: no clip section used twice, no clip more than twice, shot types change, and key action moments…
items.text: Vary the cut: no clip section used twice, no clip more than twice, shot types change, and key action moments are cut from several clips of one demographic rather than one clip played in order.
