items.text: Prioritise control levers over volume in AI video: match generated shots to real footage (the swipe's look, real B-roll, real product) and control angle, camera, performance, props and continuity per shot; scale automation only after the system is proven end to end.
items.why: Mixing real and generated footage until indistinguishable is where realism lives.

items.title: Once scripts are ruled ready for production, fix only what stops the run (props, gates) and never rewrite…
items.text: Once scripts are ruled ready for production, fix only what stops the run (props, gates) and never rewrite script words off a reviewer's or teammate's flags; where a review conflicts with the owner's rulings, the rulings win.
items.why: Speed beats rework; the scripts were already fine.

items.title: Never use whole frames from other creators' videos (their faces or words) as props; flag them for remake.
items.text: Never use whole frames from other creators' videos (their faces or words) as props; flag them for remake.
items.why: Other creators' frames carry their likeness and words into our ads.

items.title: Run ads in two lanes only: a seasonal promotion lane for the sale window and an evergreen middle- and…
items.text: Run ads in two lanes only: a seasonal promotion lane for the sale window and an evergreen middle- and bottom-funnel lane; cut offers that add no leverage, and state price only as 'starting at' the lowest price.
items.why: Simpler strategy; the multi-buy offer did not provide leverage.
items.when: Paid ad strategy and offer framing

items.title: Point every ad and email only at the current funnel; a link to a retired funnel is a bug to repoint, and old…
items.text: Point every ad and email only at the current funnel; a link to a retired funnel is a bug to repoint, and old ads on it get paused.
items.why: The old funnel double-fires pixel events, and a page picker ranking by live-ad count kept choosing it.

items.title: End organic assets on the brand's quiz ('find your method'), never on a price or a product to buy.
items.text: End organic assets on the brand's quiz ('find your method'), never on a price or a product to buy.
items.why: Organic traffic is sent to the quiz, which does the selling.

items.title: Use one design system for the website, landing and offer pages and emails, built on the brand's real…
items.text: Use one design system for the website, landing and offer pages and emails, built on the brand's real typefaces and tokens; ads and funnel creative are exempt because they are for attention only.
items.why: Surfaces drifting apart was the problem; every experience someone lands on must be dialed in.
items.when: Site, landing pages and email design

items.title: In emails, use real product photos and cut-outs over 3D renders wherever the renders are not…
items.text: In emails, use real product photos and cut-outs over 3D renders wherever the renders are not production-perfect, and take embellishments from the brand's real studio set.
items.why: Real photos are production-ready where the 3D models are not.

items.title: Before any brief goes to production, check that the product named in it matches the run's product; a mismatch…
items.text: Before any brief goes to production, check that the product named in it matches the run's product; a mismatch is a stop.
items.why: An ad came out written around the wrong product after the owner named another.

items.title: Find the deeper desire under the problem (e.g.
items.text: Find the deeper desire under the problem (e.g. attraction, looking younger) and show it at the mirror beat and the payoff, while never claiming the product does more than it does.
items.why: The problem is the lock; the desire is the prize and hits harder than the problem alone.

items.title: Carry over a swipe's structure, never its problem: every brief must be about {brand}'s problem, so read each…
items.text: Carry over a swipe's structure, never its problem: every brief must be about {brand}'s problem, so read each brief's title paragraph and problem beat before calling it ready.
items.why: The teardown chain carries the swipe's problem forward unless told otherwise, and a brief about the wrong problem is useless.

items.title: Show no reviews block on checkout pages.
items.text: Show no reviews block on checkout pages.
items.why: The owner ruled it should not be there.

items.title: Keep front-end offers simple: sell the hero product alone and push volume, and never ask for a subscription…
items.text: Keep front-end offers simple: sell the hero product alone and push volume, and never ask for a subscription on the front end.
items.why: Over-engineered offers do not beat a simple device sale with volume.

items.title: Quote savings in dollar amounts, not percentages, and make the landing page, checkout and cart state the same…
items.text: Quote savings in dollar amounts, not percentages, and make the landing page, checkout and cart state the same price and saving.
items.why: Percentages and mismatched figures break congruence through the funnel.

items.title: Never show a discount, saving, promo, review or order that is not real on a funnel or store page; strip…
items.text: Never show a discount, saving, promo, review or order that is not real on a funnel or store page; strip template leftovers like phantom promo banners, fake reviews and sample orders.
items.why: A page claiming a phantom discount or fake proof misleads customers.

items.title: Keep one offer and price index across every sales platform and track each product's contribution against ad…
items.text: Keep one offer and price index across every sales platform and track each product's contribution against ad spend.
items.why: Standardised offers and pricing let contribution be read against spend.

items.title: Use only the brand's own colours in branded static ads, never a paid swipe's colours (native statics from…
items.text: Use only the brand's own colours in branded static ads, never a paid swipe's colours (native statics from organic swipes keep the swipe's colours).
items.why: Off-brand colour reads as not our brand at all.

items.title: Match the product to the ad's look: a photographic ad uses the real product photo as reference; a stylised ad…
items.text: Match the product to the ad's look: a photographic ad uses the real product photo as reference; a stylised ad draws the product in the ad's own style from the real photo; a generic render matching neither is slop.
items.why: A product matching neither the photo nor the ad's style looks fake.

items.title: Put no long dashes in on-image copy, and make sure every person and body in the picture makes sense for the…
items.text: Put no long dashes in on-image copy, and make sure every person and body in the picture makes sense for the ad.
items.why: Dashes do not look human-typed, and a mismatched body confuses.

items.title: Make static ads from static swipes and organic statics from organic photo posts, not video covers; never…
items.text: Make static ads from static swipes and organic statics from organic photo posts, not video covers; never repeat an image within a batch, and keep Black Friday and Cyber Monday as separate sets.
items.why: Format must match its swipe source; repeats and blended sale moments waste review.

items.title: Put no CTA, quiz mention or offer in ultra-upper-funnel native ads; they should not feel like an ad at all.
items.text: Put no CTA, quiz mention or offer in ultra-upper-funnel native ads; they should not feel like an ad at all.
items.why: Upper-funnel native creative works by not reading as an ad.

items.title: Swap the picture by visual rhyme: keep the swipe's picture (pose, light, crowd, framing) and turn its…
items.text: Swap the picture by visual rhyme: keep the swipe's picture (pose, light, crowd, framing) and turn its meaning-carrying objects into the problem and the product.
items.why: This is the creativity and style of marketing the owner was looking for.
items.when: Image ads from meme or photo swipes

items.title: Never make sterile creative, including bottom-funnel and offer ads; make the words and picture one idea, and…
items.text: Never make sterile creative, including bottom-funnel and offer ads; make the words and picture one idea, and never mad-lib the swipe's sentence with our nouns.
items.why: The top ads were deep with all those creative elements; text that does not match a great image fails.

items.title: Fix on-ad wording with a compositor over a clean plate, never by asking the image model to re-letter.
items.text: Fix on-ad wording with a compositor over a clean plate, never by asking the image model to re-letter.
items.why: Models re-lettering text drift and trip safety filters on close-up skin.

items.title: Once a brand is past the sub-avatar stage and onboarding broader buyers, make the storefront product-first:…
items.text: Once a brand is past the sub-avatar stage and onboarding broader buyers, make the storefront product-first: lead with the core set, offer the hero product and the replenishment set as options, and drop avatar-specific copy.
items.why: The website speaks to the solution and product for a wider audience.
items.when: Store home, collection and product pages

items.title: Never crop pictures out of AI mockups for real pages: use the product library first, crop so the problem is…
items.text: Never crop pictures out of AI mockups for real pages: use the product library first, crop so the problem is visible (never eyes-only), cover every product in the set, and generate only true gaps.
items.why: Real assets beat mockup crops on live pages.

items.title: Add an audience lane instead of pivoting the brand: one brand and catalogue, separate audience lanes (e.g.
items.text: Add an audience lane instead of pivoting the brand: one brand and catalogue, separate audience lanes (e.g. older buyers on Meta, younger on TikTok) that never share an asset.
items.why: Sell to the parents on Facebook while the young buyer buys directly on TikTok, like a kids' line, not a new company.
items.when: Brand expansion to a new audience

items.title: Store customer language as raw verbatim data first (one row per quote with source and signal), owned per core…
items.text: Store customer language as raw verbatim data first (one row per quote with source and signal), owned per core avatar with no combined files; summaries are derived, dated analysis on top.
items.why: Card-authored copy is not data, and combined files blur avatars.

items.title: Treat avatars derived from competitors as test avatars only until our own evidence backs them.
items.text: Treat avatars derived from competitors as test avatars only until our own evidence backs them.
items.why: Competitor-derived avatars have no evidence from our customers.

items.title: In AI demo ads, show the product working as a dramatization: application over a visible problem, wipe, and…
items.text: In AI demo ads, show the product working as a dramatization: application over a visible problem, wipe, and the problem gone instantly, with no marks in any later scene; keep the swipe's hook and never lighten the base skin tone.
items.why: The ad's job is to demonstrate; real proof (before/afters, the study) lives on the landing page.

items.title: Put no 'results may vary' or similar small print on demo ads, and do not treat a 'looks staged' viewer note…
items.text: Put no 'results may vary' or similar small print on demo ads, and do not treat a 'looks staged' viewer note on a dramatized demo as a fault.
items.why: Dramatization is the format; proof sits on the landing page.

items.title: A new problem means a new core avatar even when the demographic is the same; never run it under an existing…
items.text: A new problem means a new core avatar even when the demographic is the same; never run it under an existing avatar whose profile and language are about a different problem.
items.why: The existing avatar's language and sub-avatars describe a different desire.
items.when: Avatar assignment for new problem batches

items.title: Use comment sections only where the commenters are the avatar; when a platform's crowd skews younger than…
items.text: Use comment sections only where the commenters are the avatar; when a platform's crowd skews younger than her, use it for formats and competitors only, not for her language.
items.why: Comments from the wrong age group are not the avatar's voice.

items.title: A hook is a line plus a scroll stopper: a first-frame visual event that shows and tells the same thing at…
items.text: A hook is a line plus a scroll stopper: a first-frame visual event that shows and tells the same thing at once, not a camera setup.
items.why: Showing and telling together is what stops the scroll.

items.title: One brief, one discrete problem: hooks name it in the avatar's dominant word, and off-problem research seams…
items.text: One brief, one discrete problem: hooks name it in the avatar's dominant word, and off-problem research seams become variation notes, never hooks.
items.why: Mixing problems in one brief dilutes the message.

items.title: Ship every hook to test instead of picking one, and write one body any hook can head; the market decides and…
items.text: Ship every hook to test instead of picking one, and write one body any hook can head; the market decides and the human gate is QA only.
items.why: The market picks winners, not reviewers.

items.title: Make hook variations real swings, each entering on a different moment, behaviour or verbatim line, never word…
items.text: Make hook variations real swings, each entering on a different moment, behaviour or verbatim line, never word swaps.
items.why: Word swaps do not test anything new.

items.title: The avatar is ours: from a swipe in another category, the structure transfers and the subject does not, and…
items.text: The avatar is ours: from a swipe in another category, the structure transfers and the subject does not, and the source's audience never vetoes our avatar.
items.why: Cross-category swipes are the normal case.

items.title: Read the funnel entry level off the swipe (what it explains versus takes for granted), never choose it…
items.text: Read the funnel entry level off the swipe (what it explains versus takes for granted), never choose it because a research bank is fuller; treat thin language as no defect.
items.why: The swipe's assumptions set our entry point; language fills in over time.

items.title: Keep each avatar's and sub-avatar's affinity and content profile separate, never blended.
items.text: Keep each avatar's and sub-avatar's affinity and content profile separate, never blended.
items.why: Blended profiles lose what makes each avatar respond.

items.title: Treat teardown interpretations as options that widen choices, not single binding verdicts.
items.text: Treat teardown interpretations as options that widen choices, not single binding verdicts.
items.why: Collapsing a reading into one answer works against later stages' choices.

items.title: At the edit stage, cover clip faults with punch-ins, close-ups, B-roll and patched words; remake a clip only…
items.text: At the edit stage, cover clip faults with punch-ins, close-ups, B-roll and patched words; remake a clip only when no edit move can hide the fault.
items.why: Remakes cost money and time and most faults are fixable in the cut.

items.title: After the first text-to-image pass, make every image fix image-to-image off the last approved render,…
items.text: After the first text-to-image pass, make every image fix image-to-image off the last approved render, changing only what was asked.
items.why: Fresh generations re-roll faces, type, palette and layout so the ad drifts instead of converging.

items.title: Make every mid-shot overlay or effect its own element and composite it in the edit timed to its line; acting…
items.text: Make every mid-shot overlay or effect its own element and composite it in the edit timed to its line; acting inside a shot is timed beats in the clip prompt.
items.why: A clip asked to act and run a graphic does one badly, and one effect serves every hook version.
items.when: AI video with effects or animations

items.title: Swap the world as well as the argument when adapting an email: an email that would read the same with its…
items.text: Swap the world as well as the argument when adapting an email: an email that would read the same with its moment deleted has failed.
items.why: Only swapping the argument produced a football email with nothing about football.
items.when: Email copy adapted from source emails

items.title: The calendar decides and the copy obeys: a send with no offer gets no invented price or gift, and an angle…
items.text: The calendar decides and the copy obeys: a send with no offer gets no invented price or gift, and an angle tied to a dead moment is replaced.
items.why: Sends invented prices and ran a holiday deal three weeks after the holiday.

items.title: Make at most one send per day; versions of one send for different avatars may share the date.
items.text: Make at most one send per day; versions of one send for different avatars may share the date.
items.why: Two different sends on one day was ruled out.

items.title: Research the live week behind every email (checkable facts, the one odd thing, two or three baits the reader…
items.text: Research the live week behind every email (checkable facts, the one odd thing, two or three baits the reader can answer without buying, who may be named, a do-not-claim list).
items.why: Emails that bait the audience on what is happening that week engage; this runs for every email.

items.title: Name only customers the brand has already named publicly, with the source on file.
items.text: Name only customers the brand has already named publicly, with the source on file.
items.why: Naming customers without public precedent risks false claims.
items.when: Email and ad copy mentioning customers or athletes

items.title: Leave email design to the brand's existing templates and the designer; the email machine maps the month and…
items.text: Leave email design to the brand's existing templates and the designer; the email machine maps the month and writes the copy injected into a reference email's framework.
items.why: Machine-made email design was rejected as poor; the value is the calendar and the copy.

items.title: Work email one component at a time: copy first, then pictures, and push nothing into the email platform, not…
items.text: Work email one component at a time: copy first, then pictures, and push nothing into the email platform, not even drafts, until both are signed off.
items.why: A test pushed a draft with a wrong price straight into the live account.

items.title: Route email final wording and scheduling to the copy owner and picture or design improvements to the…
items.text: Route email final wording and scheduling to the copy owner and picture or design improvements to the {designer}.
items.why: Clear roles stop designers being handed copy and scheduling.

items.title: Design each email like a landing page: one type scale, a picture right after its headline (never a picture…
items.text: Design each email like a landing page: one type scale, a picture right after its headline (never a picture above its headline or a badge as the opener), and lead with a person whose story is the email's job.
items.why: Sloppy assets or type read as cheap and waste the send.

items.title: Use no face or proof asset twice in a week of emails, check every crop shows what its label names, and pair a…
items.text: Use no face or proof asset twice in a week of emails, check every crop shows what its label names, and pair a customer's words only with his own face.
items.why: Repeated customers and mismatched crops broke trust in the week's emails.

items.title: Treat the simulated viewer check as the consumer's voice: fix every 'not for me' or 'looks fake' by rewriting…
items.text: Treat the simulated viewer check as the consumer's voice: fix every 'not for me' or 'looks fake' by rewriting or re-picking the avatar the product fits, never wave it through; pass only mechanical holds.
items.why: The goal is video real consumers watch and act on, not output that clears gates.
items.when: AI viewer checks on video ads

items.title: Bias swipe picks, hooks and tests toward entertainment-first content someone would watch for its own sake;…
items.text: Bias swipe picks, hooks and tests toward entertainment-first content someone would watch for its own sake; treat sterile expert-consult content as the weaker bet unless it is itself watchable.
items.why: Song ads got about 38 s watch time at very low CPC while entertaining AI and organic formats are printing.

items.title: Let the production team run the image chain end to end while the owner only approves or sends back; a…
items.text: Let the production team run the image chain end to end while the owner only approves or sends back; a send-back note is the remake spec, and improvements go into the chain, not extra owner steps.
items.why: The owner will not sit in the production loop.

items.title: Run every finished creative set through the same copy process before filing, and assign each ad set an avatar…
items.text: Run every finished creative set through the same copy process before filing, and assign each ad set an avatar plus an angle taken from the brand's angle list, never coined (offer creative uses the offer angle).
items.why: Hand-written copy and coined angles broke the ad-set construction.
items.when: Filing ads for the ad account

items.title: Every chain run completes every pass and reports collisions as flags with citations; only a human kills a…
items.text: Every chain run completes every pass and reports collisions as flags with citations; only a human kills a run, and outputs state the rule and options in neutral language with no moralizing.
items.why: Killing a run substitutes the machine's judgment for the owner's decision rights.

items.title: Stop and report only when something is broken, never when the process works as designed (e.g.
items.text: Stop and report only when something is broken, never when the process works as designed (e.g. adapting a body-skin swipe to a face product).
items.why: Re-litigating the workflow's design at run time is overreach; the process is product-, problem- and body-part-agnostic.

items.title: Line up every person in every start picture against that person's banked master and remake any drift before a…
items.text: Line up every person in every start picture against that person's banked master and remake any drift before a single clip is made; a close-up references that person's master first, never a swipe frame with another face.
items.why: A wrong face caught after clips wastes the clips and trust.

items.title: Turn every review note into a brand-free lesson in the chain's lessons register (verbatim words, source, the…
items.text: Turn every review note into a brand-free lesson in the chain's lessons register (verbatim words, source, the rule for any brand, where it is enforced) and make the code or prompt obey it in the same change; never keep per-ad notes.
items.why: A note kept for one ad teaches the system nothing.

items.title: Send a video to review only as a finished edit: every element the swipe carries on it, no word cut off, no…
items.text: Send a video to review only as a finished edit: every element the swipe carries on it, no word cut off, no choppy jumps, with the swipe beside it for comparison.
items.why: Drafts with cut-off words and missing cards wasted review.

items.title: Measure AI video by first-take pass rate and failure reasons, not price per video; still give every paid…
items.text: Measure AI video by first-take pass rate and failure reasons, not price per video; still give every paid round a total and a stop point.
items.why: Cost falls as a result of consistency; per-video price targets aim at the wrong thing.

items.title: When one thing fails, patch only that thing: a cheap model locates the exact item, a deep model rewrites only…
items.text: When one thing fails, patch only that thing: a cheap model locates the exact item, a deep model rewrites only it, and only steps that read the changed part re-run.
items.why: Full rewrites burn time and money and invalidate everything downstream.

items.title: Check every picture at full zoom and fix every visible flaw before it goes to review; never hand a reviewer a…
items.text: Check every picture at full zoom and fix every visible flaw before it goes to review; never hand a reviewer a known defect.
items.why: Asking a reviewer to judge a flaw you already saw wastes his look.

items.title: Count and report by offer, merging product records that are the same offer into one row.
items.text: Count and report by offer, merging product records that are the same offer into one row.
items.why: Splitting one offer makes it look like two and muddies the numbers.

items.title: Take the hero product's true shape, size and physics from the store's turntable video and spec sheet…
items.text: Take the hero product's true shape, size and physics from the store's turntable video and spec sheet (measured, never guessed from one photo), and state size in numbers in prompts relative to the hand and face.
items.why: Single-photo references drew the product as the wrong object and far too small or too big.
items.when: Any picture or clip featuring the product

items.title: Never let the product be drawn: replace any generated product with a real cut-out at the best-fitting angle,…
items.text: Never let the product be drawn: replace any generated product with a real cut-out at the best-fitting angle, held the way real creators hold it, and use the brand's studio renders for product-only cards.
items.why: Redrawn products came out as slop when real footage and cut-outs exist.
items.when: Video stills and ad pictures with the product

items.title: In peak season, focus on video and static ad volume and park restructuring or refactors of live production…
items.text: In peak season, focus on video and static ad volume and park restructuring or refactors of live production systems until after.
items.why: Q4 volume comes first and the team is being trained on video and static.

items.title: Run each chosen format as its own batch with its own dollar cap.
items.text: Run each chosen format as its own batch with its own dollar cap.
items.why: Cheap volume ahead of competitors at low usage.

items.title: Run every ad type on its own format playbook over the shared chain, and match a new swipe to the nearest…
items.text: Run every ad type on its own format playbook over the shared chain, and match a new swipe to the nearest proven format as a variant before ever creating a new format family.
items.why: Each format needs specialised settings, but minting new formats all the time does not scale.

items.title: After every run, fold the run's fixes (known failures, cost) back into that format's playbook automatically;…
items.text: After every run, fold the run's fixes (known failures, cost) back into that format's playbook automatically; nobody hand-builds format workflows.
items.why: Specialised workflows must build and improve themselves from incoming videos to scale without slop.

items.title: Writing starts only on formats the owner picks from the ranked research.
items.text: Writing starts only on formats the owner picks from the ranked research.
items.why: Picks gate what gets written.

items.title: Keep avatar, sub-avatar, angle and format separate: an avatar is who, a sub-avatar a narrower who, an angle…
items.text: Keep avatar, sub-avatar, angle and format separate: an avatar is who, a sub-avatar a narrower who, an angle one claim a customer could agree or disagree with, a format how the ad is built; the same claim for a narrower person is a sub-avatar, in a different container a format, and the same mechanic with different footage a variant.
items.why: All four feel like an idea for an ad, and minting a variant as a new entry splits reporting on one claim.

items.title: Tear swipes down frame by frame (every frame at 8 per second), crop each person, place and prop from its…
items.text: Tear swipes down frame by frame (every frame at 8 per second), crop each person, place and prop from its frames, and use the real swipe frames, sharp and unblurred, as generation references.
items.why: Programming hundreds of videos a day needs real frames as references, not described elements.

items.title: Source missing props, places and people from other swipes in the library, never stock.
items.text: Source missing props, places and people from other swipes in the library, never stock.
items.why: The swipe library already holds real video frames.

items.title: Treat each shot's 3D setup (camera, posed stand-in, true-size props and product, motion) as its control…
items.text: Treat each shot's 3D setup (camera, posed stand-in, true-size props and product, motion) as its control layer, never reuse a print from another camera angle, and compare every picture side by side with its swipe frame before calling it done.
items.why: A room plate alone leaves framing, hands and product to the model, causing crop misses and misspelled packaging.

items.title: Optimise funnels page by page from real drop-off, time on page, quiz-screen drop-off, recordings and heatmaps…
items.text: Optimise funnels page by page from real drop-off, time on page, quiz-screen drop-off, recordings and heatmaps before scaling the next ad batch.
items.why: Real-time page data shows where the funnel leaks.

items.title: Make the early-console game look in code alone (low-res textures, simple lighting, shaped low-poly models),…
items.text: Make the early-console game look in code alone (low-res textures, simple lighting, shaped low-poly models), with no generated images or clips unless asked.
items.why: The look is code by nature and generated routes add cost and steps.

items.title: Fill every variable on the picture sheet (or mark it not applicable with a reason) before any generation, use…
items.text: Fill every variable on the picture sheet (or mark it not applicable with a reason) before any generation, use only input pictures with an approved record, and make start and end frames from one locked sheet with one declared change.
items.why: A blank or inconsistent variable is where slop starts, and it compounds through later pictures and the video.
items.when: Image generation for stills and video frames

items.title: Start every generated picture of a person from the current banked cast master and look sheet as references,…
items.text: Start every generated picture of a person from the current banked cast master and look sheet as references, never text-only and never a retired master; a role the cast covers never gets a new face, and photoreal jobs use only photoreal masters.
items.why: Text-only generation produced random new faces, and a cartoon master appeared on a photoreal page.

items.title: Run every paid generation at the lowest setting (e.g.
items.text: Run every paid generation at the lowest setting (e.g. 480p) and upscale the keeper locally; start from motion control on the original footage so the frame quality matches the swipe, never more polished than the original.
items.why: Credits are the cost line, and the swipe's phone-quality look is what reads as organic.

items.title: Check an offer is actually sold in the running funnels before writing it into an ad; the offer bank alone is…
items.text: Check an offer is actually sold in the running funnels before writing it into an ad; the offer bank alone is not proof.
items.why: An ad carried a bundle the brand does not sell.

items.title: When one ad format beats everything, double down: build a dedicated chain for that format and pipe variations…
items.text: When one ad format beats everything, double down: build a dedicated chain for that format and pipe variations through every similar swipe for new products.
items.why: The top advertorial outsold everything else, so its format should be multiplied.

items.title: Keep short talking reels natural: about 9-11 shots, per-clip voice, pacing at breathing speed and light…
items.text: Keep short talking reels natural: about 9-11 shots, per-clip voice, pacing at breathing speed and light direction; over-cutting, punch-ins at every pause and over-directed acting make them robotic.
items.why: The first, simplest reel felt best; mechanical edits made later ones robotic.

items.title: Check every still and clip against the brief, define each prop once at real size with a master picture, carry…
items.text: Check every still and clip against the brief, define each prop once at real size with a master picture, carry the shot's action in every clip prompt, and give the payoff its own close shot.
items.why: Small mistakes make the work look amateur.

items.title: Send content questions (what is made, whether it works) to the owner and everything else (files, queue, next…
items.text: Send content questions (what is made, whether it works) to the owner and everything else (files, queue, next brief, time, credits, access) to the operations lead.
items.why: Keeps the owner on content decisions only.

items.title: Never send a brief to designers, editors or creators that the owner has not checked.
items.text: Never send a brief to designers, editors or creators that the owner has not checked.
items.why: A picture built on a brief he never saw is spend on something he may throw out.

items.title: Review picture-ad copy on the image, swipe beside our words, before producing; when the owner rewrites the…
items.text: Review picture-ad copy on the image, swipe beside our words, before producing; when the owner rewrites the words, name what changed (rhythm, the swipe's shape, spice, specificity, offer line) and turn it into a brand-agnostic copy rule.
items.why: The machine copy was not landing and must learn the owner's way instead of him fixing it each time.
items.when: Image ad headline and copy writing

items.title: A stand-in for any chain stage runs the stage's declared model and reads the whole prompt; never downgrade…
items.text: A stand-in for any chain stage runs the stage's declared model and reads the whole prompt; never downgrade the model or skim to save usage.
items.why: The hyper-detailed prompts carry the quality; a cheaper model or skimmed prompt broke a brief.

items.title: Build recurring sets, products and props once as 3D models, compose scenes in 3D (camera, depth, placement,…
items.text: Build recurring sets, products and props once as 3D models, compose scenes in 3D (camera, depth, placement, product shape and use), render that as the reference, and let generation dress it.
items.why: Reusable elements give more depth control and persuasion for fewer credits.
items.when: Repeated scenes and elements in AI production

items.title: Pass teardown structure holds automatically when the answer is 'do what the swipe does'; turn only flaggable…
items.text: Pass teardown structure holds automatically when the answer is 'do what the swipe does'; turn only flaggable items (a real person's face or name, team, league or brand marks, copyrighted music) into original stand-ins playing the same role, and never invent facts.
items.why: The method is take a swipe and adapt it; re-approving the swipe's own structure wastes time.

items.title: A hook version is the control with only the opening scene's picture swapped: same audio, same length, the…
items.text: A hook version is the control with only the opening scene's picture swapped: same audio, same length, the song or voice starting on the same beat, never a pre-roll in front.
items.why: A pre-roll delays the punch and makes every version a different edit.

items.title: Put no price or offer in ad headlines.
items.text: Put no price or offer in ad headlines.
items.why: Owner ruling for headline copy.

items.title: When a caller has already decided the concept (a video brief, an email, a product shot), image production…
items.text: When a caller has already decided the concept (a video brief, an email, a product shot), image production executes its spec (base image, swaps tied to banked pictures, what stays, the words) and never invents a new concept.
items.why: Injecting a fresh ad concept overwrote decisions the caller had already made.
items.when: Image production for video frames, emails and product pictures

items.title: Split the work 10/80/10: the owner sets direction, the system does about 80% (executing the fix once a…
items.text: Split the work 10/80/10: the owner sets direction, the system does about 80% (executing the fix once a finding is defined), and the owner reviews the last 10% before anything goes live.
items.why: The owner cannot afford to re-instruct each step; components and skills exist to run the middle.
items.when: Any finding, audit or review cycle

items.title: Fix what is broken before running any test, and show every finding marked on the real page with a mock of the…
items.text: Fix what is broken before running any test, and show every finding marked on the real page with a mock of the proposed change.
items.why: Tests on a broken page measure the break; words alone do not land with a visual decision-maker.

items.title: Judge a swipe by its format and its market, never by what product it sells; never cut a swipe or brief for…
items.text: Judge a swipe by its format and its market, never by what product it sells; never cut a swipe or brief for selling a different product, and read the brief itself before judging it.
items.why: A swipe selling another product to the same customer is still the right format.

items.title: Keep copy the owner wrote deliberately unless he asks for a change, and build any icon, illustration or…
items.text: Keep copy the owner wrote deliberately unless he asks for a change, and build any icon, illustration or visual from the brand's own cards and design assets, never a newly invented style.
items.why: His wording and visual language are decisions, not drafts; off-brand styles cost a review cycle.
items.when: Pages, offer boxes and brand visuals

items.title: Keep the customer's problem clearly visible on screen until the product fixes it: draw it into the start and…
items.text: Keep the customer's problem clearly visible on screen until the product fixes it: draw it into the start and end pictures big enough to read on a phone, and show a clean result only at the payoff.
items.why: The problem is the reason the ad exists, and generation models smooth skin by default.

items.title: Treat a swipe's motion as the asset: the teardown reads motion, physics, cut rhythm, sound sync and what…
items.text: Treat a swipe's motion as the asset: the teardown reads motion, physics, cut rhythm, sound sync and what holds retention per shot, and generation uses one picture per continuous stretch with a dense frame-by-frame description of the movement, adding a new picture only at a real cut.
items.why: Turning a moving swipe into animated stills throws away exactly what made it work.

items.title: Drop removed and set-aside items from every count, list and report; killed means gone.
items.text: Drop removed and set-aside items from every count, list and report; killed means gone.
items.why: Counting dead items inflated open work (690 shown versus 325 real).

items.title: When a prompt rule is being ignored, restructure it as a labelled slot or a string-level test instead of…
items.text: When a prompt rule is being ignored, restructure it as a labelled slot or a string-level test instead of restating it harder; stop fabrication with a validator that checks citations against the files.
items.why: Prose rules compete with every other sentence while labelled slots can be self-checked.

items.title: Layer automation so only hits reach the owner: chains, an autopilot that turns one swipe into finished ads in…
items.text: Layer automation so only hits reach the owner: chains, an autopilot that turns one swipe into finished ads in every look, an operator that fixes failing steps and re-runs, and an orchestrator that turns the owner's sentences into queued work; keep the hard walls (no live send to the ad account or customers without a person).
items.why: Every stop that waits for the owner caps volume.

items.title: Give every product picture its true size and a label in the prompt (front, back, in hand), and make people…
items.text: Give every product picture its true size and a label in the prompt (front, back, in hand), and make people lookalikes of the swipe's people, except a famous face, which gets a different face of the same type.
items.why: Unlabelled references produced wrong product sides, and the swipe's people are part of the joke.

items.title: Make variations of a finished ad locally from its own footage first (about three cold-open hook versions from…
items.text: Make variations of a finished ad locally from its own footage first (about three cold-open hook versions from its strongest moments plus a clean thumbnail per version) before any paid restyle, and state count times credits for any paid batch before running it.
items.why: Most version-making is editing, which costs nothing locally; paid restyle batches burn real money.

items.title: Plan the marketing calendar as its own station that feeds ads as well as email; a reviewer's edits outrank…
items.text: Plan the marketing calendar as its own station that feeds ads as well as email; a reviewer's edits outrank the plan and the swiped source, a re-plan never overwrites human approvals, and a cut slot is never produced.
items.why: The calendar is relevant to ads too, and a reviewer's work must never silently disappear.

items.title: For generated product shots, supply a clean full-product image plus a real store photo and name the product's…
items.text: For generated product shots, supply a clean full-product image plus a real store photo and name the product's real parts in the prompt; a partial photo makes the model invent the rest.
items.why: Given only a partial photo, the model invented a part the product does not have.

items.title: Read the swipe's visual style at teardown and lock it at the top of every element, frame and clip prompt with…
items.text: Read the swipe's visual style at teardown and lock it at the top of every element, frame and clip prompt with a real swipe frame as the guide; anything made in the wrong style is restyled image-to-image keeping identity, wardrobe, skin marks and real age.
items.why: Style is half of why the swipe stops the scroll; the same story in a different look is a different ad.
items.when: Teardown and generation for stylised swipes

items.title: Maximise absurdity and movement in every video: direct clips beat by beat by the second, fast from frame one,…
items.text: Maximise absurdity and movement in every video: direct clips beat by beat by the second, fast from frame one, with big reactions, absurd escalation, a moving camera and people constantly in motion; never a slow push-in or a held pose.
items.why: A calm-paced clip wastes the seconds; the target is music-video density.

items.title: Protect ad account health when uploading volume: never raise or skip the upload pace, and send heavy videos…
items.text: Protect ad account health when uploading volume: never raise or skip the upload pace, and send heavy videos as compressed copies while the master stays untouched.
items.why: Nothing should look like spamming the ad account.
items.when: Uploading ads to the ad account

items.title: Pick the model per agent by its job: the cheapest for transcription and listing, a mid model for applying…
items.text: Pick the model per agent by its job: the cheapest for transcription and listing, a mid model for applying stated rules and verification, the top model only for design decisions and expensive adversarial checks.
items.why: Running the top model everywhere multiplies cost on work that is mostly file reading.

items.title: Run every AI clip's movement through the motion chain (real footage, tracking, motion read, 3D rehearsal,…
items.text: Run every AI clip's movement through the motion chain (real footage, tracking, motion read, 3D rehearsal, approved preview, take, match check) before spending credits, send tracked takes with no written shot sizes, and have an independent frame-by-frame check confirm the preview first.
items.why: Hand-keyed rehearsals and written shot sizes produced fake motion and odd zooms, and automated checks passed real faults.

items.title: Hold landing page messaging to the market's exact words and structures with cultural awareness, never…
items.text: Hold landing page messaging to the market's exact words and structures with cultural awareness, never paraphrased into brand voice.
items.why: The landing page is the centre of acquisition, where a prospect decides whether to deal with the brand at all.

items.title: Settle any call our own data or an existing ruling answers (e.g.
items.text: Settle any call our own data or an existing ruling answers (e.g. the most-viewed swipe sets the setting) instead of asking.
items.why: Most small questions are already solved by data or by rulings in the chain.

items.title: Build organic research feeds around whose scroll it is, one per sub-avatar, and sort posts into entertainment…
items.text: Build organic research feeds around whose scroll it is, one per sub-avatar, and sort posts into entertainment (first), educational and selling lanes; never search a problem as the ask.
items.why: Entertainment catches people at the unaware stage before they search; organic formats get ripped and merged with direct-response copy.

items.title: Voice narrated ads with a storytelling voice model that reads the script continuously, not line by line, and…
items.text: Voice narrated ads with a storytelling voice model that reads the script continuously, not line by line, and audition voices before using a new one.
items.why: Line-by-line reads came out flat and staccato and did not sound like a real narrator.

items.title: Make native statics match the swipe's granularity and quality (camera, grain, compression) and keep an…
items.text: Make native statics match the swipe's granularity and quality (camera, grain, compression) and keep an organic swipe's own colours; never make them cleaner or glossier than the real post, and add a product only when the swipe has a slot for one.
items.why: These are native ads; polish and off-swipe products break the native read.
items.when: Native statics from organic or meme swipes

items.title: Take every angle, format, avatar and ad name from the assigned bank or classifier; never coin a new one.
items.text: Take every angle, format, avatar and ad name from the assigned bank or classifier; never coin a new one. If nothing fits, raise the gap instead of inventing a name.
items.why: A coined name silently forks the vocabulary so page and ad reports can never be joined to show which angle earned.
items.when: Naming angles, formats, avatars, pages and ads

items.title: Never send a generic email: every email carries a concept borrowed from the reader's own culture (a format, a…
items.text: Never send a generic email: every email carries a concept borrowed from the reader's own culture (a format, a moment palette, products shown as made pictures, rotating proof), and the subject names the concept; an email with no concept is held at final check.
items.why: Generic emails are invisible, and creativity has to come from the process by default rather than being prompted each time.

items.title: Keep every load-bearing element of a swipe and swap it for ours; nothing is dropped.
items.text: Keep every load-bearing element of a swipe and swap it for ours; nothing is dropped. A hold on a load-bearing element clears only when a ruling explicitly names that element and what it becomes.
items.why: The load-bearing elements are why the swipe works; a silent drop breaks the ad.
items.when: Swipe teardown into script and brief

items.title: Make the creative calls (hook, twist) up front, then run everything after through the chain's stages and…
items.text: Make the creative calls (hook, twist) up front, then run everything after through the chain's stages and checks with no shortcuts.
items.why: Creativity at the start plus structure through the run keeps quality high and consistent.

items.title: Use a viral swipe whole as the hook with the {hero product} placed inside it, then bolt on a separate selling…
items.text: Use a viral swipe whole as the hook with the {hero product} placed inside it, then bolt on a separate selling video in the same vibe; never write a bridge or pitch into the swipe itself.
items.why: The swipe holds attention as it is; the bolted-on video does the selling.
items.when: Hook-led video ads built from organic swipes

items.title: Build ad bodies from proven winners: take the bones of what has worked and update the language to the…
items.text: Build ad bodies from proven winners: take the bones of what has worked and update the language to the {avatar}; never write bodies outside the variation chain.
items.why: Proven structures sell; freshly written bodies were rejected as weak.
items.when: Writing the selling body of a video ad

items.title: Put no length cap on the selling pitch; it runs as long as it needs.
items.text: Put no length cap on the selling pitch; it runs as long as it needs.
items.why: The pitch has to finish the argument; an arbitrary cap cuts proof and close.
items.when: Selling half of a video ad

items.title: In AI swaps give each shot one job: swap people and product in separate passes, and a swap replaces, never…
items.text: In AI swaps give each shot one job: swap people and product in separate passes, and a swap replaces, never adds (an empty hand stays empty). Check every swapped face against the cast master and every product against the packshot before cutting.
items.why: Combined passes drift identity and products; wrong faces and logo-less products are caught on sight.
items.when: Swapping our cast or product into swipe footage

items.title: Open every song ad on the verse: the story's punch line is the first sung line, on beat one, with no…
items.text: Open every song ad on the verse: the story's punch line is the first sung line, on beat one, with no instrumental intro and no chorus first.
items.why: The opening line is what holds the scroll; an intro or chorus first delays the story.

items.title: Never use the same clip twice in one ad, chorus included; fill gaps with real hands-and-product B-roll from…
items.text: Never use the same clip twice in one ad, chorus included; fill gaps with real hands-and-product B-roll from owned footage.
items.why: Repeated clips read as cheap and the owner checks cuts frame by frame.

items.title: Pick a song's genre and voice from the {avatar}'s own music and era; for an older woman, a male heartthrob…
items.text: Pick a song's genre and voice from the {avatar}'s own music and era; for an older woman, a male heartthrob voice from her youth can sing about her.
items.why: The song has to sound like what she grew up loving, not a lane foreign to her.

items.title: Before leaning on any {avatar} detail, confirm it has a real customer source; keep positioning and benefits…
items.text: Before leaning on any {avatar} detail, confirm it has a real customer source; keep positioning and benefits constant but make lived experiences fresh each run so no single line repeats in every piece.
items.why: An unsourced line from the first avatar sheet leaked into every chain and became repetitive and weird.
items.when: Writing scripts, hooks, concepts from avatar files

items.title: The owner makes every business, marketing, brand-risk and ad-policy call; do not add compliance, trademark or…
items.text: The owner makes every business, marketing, brand-risk and ad-policy call; do not add compliance, trademark or 'the platform will flag it' commentary unless asked.
items.why: Risk calls on ads, brands and wardrobe are the owner's, and unrequested warnings slow the work.

items.title: Put no on-screen disclaimers or small print on video ads ('Results vary', 'Terms apply', 'Real customer');…
items.text: Put no on-screen disclaimers or small print on video ads ('Results vary', 'Terms apply', 'Real customer'); say the guarantee in the words on file only when the script calls for it.
items.why: The owner ruled small print out of every video ad.

items.title: Never name a format, style or structure after a gender or kind of person ('remedy', not 'grandma's remedy');…
items.text: Never name a format, style or structure after a gender or kind of person ('remedy', not 'grandma's remedy'); the cast belongs in the cast layer.
items.why: A format is a reusable shape; a gendered name ties it to one cast and blocks reuse across brands and avatars.

items.title: Hunt formats that get millions of views, don't look like ads and teach the viewer something, made with no…
items.text: Hunt formats that get millions of views, don't look like ads and teach the viewer something, made with no humans and no paid video generation (script, storyboard, narrative and code only); rank by views and whether it can be made that way.
items.why: These formats get huge reach for little cost, while paid image and song rounds cost too much and took too long.
items.when: Sourcing organic formats for content brands

items.title: Keep email sends targeted to engaged segments; never blast churned, unengaged or every segment at once unless…
items.text: Keep email sends targeted to engaged segments; never blast churned, unengaged or every segment at once unless the owner names an emergency liquidation.
items.why: Blasting dead lists is spam and hurts deliverability; a list nobody opens is not an audience.

items.title: Men never kiss or hug men, and nobody kisses themselves or a mirror, in any ad; a man and woman kiss only…
items.text: Men never kiss or hug men, and nobody kisses themselves or a mirror, in any ad; a man and woman kiss only when the storyboard says so. Read every clip at 1.5 frames per second or finer before final.
items.why: Generators invent contact from loose motion prompts, and the owner will not run it; coarse checks miss a one-second kiss.

items.title: Before any paid generation round, state clips x price and a stop total; prove the look on one or two clips…
items.text: Before any paid generation round, state clips x price and a stop total; prove the look on one or two clips before sending the rest, and stop the moment the owner objects to spend.
items.why: Spend ran ahead of a locked look and burned two full films on a result that was still wrong.
items.when: Any paid image, clip, voice or song round

items.title: Never generate a product or rated item into a person's frames or cast sheet; frames show the person clean and…
items.text: Never generate a product or rated item into a person's frames or cast sheet; frames show the person clean and the item goes on as a cut-out layer in the edit.
items.why: A baked-in item can only be painted over afterwards, and the patch never holds on a moving person.

items.title: Build the offer box subscription-first: routine first with one-time purchase as a quiet line, no time inside…
items.text: Build the offer box subscription-first: routine first with one-time purchase as a quiet line, no time inside a tier (cadence under the button), say 'refills' not 'subscription', read every price from the store, make 'Buy 2 get 1' claims only when the numbers derive it, and preselect the biggest saving as 'Most popular'.
items.why: These rules make the subscription the default choice while keeping every claim true.

items.title: Check subscription discounts across pack sizes before designing tiers: a flat-amount discount inverts the…
items.text: Check subscription discounts across pack sizes before designing tiers: a flat-amount discount inverts the ladder (cheapest per unit becomes the smallest pack), so switch to percentage or rebuild the tiers.
items.why: Flat money off is a big percentage on a single and a small one on a multi-pack, so 'Most popular' stops being the best value.

items.title: Before calling a format right for an older {avatar}, read top comments for stated ages, grandkids and…
items.text: Before calling a format right for an older {avatar}, read top comments for stated ages, grandkids and growing-up years, and start from her saved childhood and holiday research; use lookalikes, never real characters.
items.why: Format and topic guesses fail; nostalgia lists and holiday specials drew older commenters while plausible topics did not.

items.title: Queue one brief per brand per day to each production creator until they are fluent with the AI system; no…
items.text: Queue one brief per brand per day to each production creator until they are fluent with the AI system; no bigger queue or batch until the owner says so, and capture how each works to improve the workflow.
items.why: Quality and fluency come before volume, and watching their workflow is how the creative process improves.
items.when: Onboarding designers and editors onto the AI production system

items.title: Every edit step names its model and moves to a newer, better model of the same kind when one ships; resizing…
items.text: Every edit step names its model and moves to a newer, better model of the same kind when one ships; resizing is not picture-making and uses whichever outpaint model resizes best.
items.why: The model decides what the work looks like, and resizing doesn't touch the image's contents.
items.when: Choosing models for image edits and resizes

items.title: Every picture ad, any batch size, runs the one current image process (swipe saved, teardown and writing,…
items.text: Every picture ad, any batch size, runs the one current image process (swipe saved, teardown and writing, review, production chain); never a side path or one-off script that makes pictures. If no door exists, build the door first, then use it.
items.why: Repeated output needs one path; side scripts produced leaked notes, inconsistent products and weird text.
items.when: All image production, including cast sheets, set prints and video start pictures

items.title: Make a picture ad look exactly like the swipe, then apply our finesse: type styled like the swipe's, no…
items.text: Make a picture ad look exactly like the swipe, then apply our finesse: type styled like the swipe's, no malformed limbs, the product only when the swipe has one, and words that fit what the picture shows.
items.why: The swipe's look is what works; deviations read as fake.

items.title: Turn every correction the owner gives into a check in the chain, not a note; a failed quality gate is a…
items.text: Turn every correction the owner gives into a check in the chain, not a note; a failed quality gate is a rerun, never a reformat of the output.
items.why: Production should run without him repeating himself, and reformatting hides the failure.

items.title: Group script lines by set-up (same setting, same people) and by what the person does: one start picture per…
items.text: Group script lines by set-up (same setting, same people) and by what the person does: one start picture per group, with close-ups and reactions as camera moves on that picture; make a new picture only when the person does something significantly different.
items.why: A picture per line lets faces, looks and grades drift and multiplies spend and checks.
items.when: Making start pictures for video ads

items.title: Make demonstration shots as AI scenes with our cast, using our own real footage from the same setting only as…
items.text: Make demonstration shots as AI scenes with our cast, using our own real footage from the same setting only as the movement reference.
items.why: Real footage gives believable motion while AI keeps the cast consistent.

items.title: Make each start picture once, never three versions; the reviewer checks the one picture and sends it back if…
items.text: Make each start picture once, never three versions; the reviewer checks the one picture and sends it back if wrong.
items.why: Three versions tripled picture spend and the checks on each cost nearly as much again for little gain.

items.title: Show pictures and clips without a swipe-look filter or grade.
items.text: Show pictures and clips without a swipe-look filter or grade.
items.why: The added filter made the execution look off and inconsistent.

items.title: A single product shown more than once must be the identical object every time (same height, width, label,…
items.text: A single product shown more than once must be the identical object every time (same height, width, label, scale), sourced from its 3D model or real packshot; never let a generator re-imagine or add a second one.
items.why: Two sizes of one product read as two products or AI slop and kill trust in the real thing.
items.when: Any shot where the product appears more than once

items.title: One source video gets one teardown record; look it up before any teardown, brief or asset is made and reuse…
items.text: One source video gets one teardown record; look it up before any teardown, brief or asset is made and reuse the record rather than starting new work. Every brief carries its angle and why, not just an avatar.
items.why: Repeat teardowns of the same video wasted tokens, and briefs need depth of intent.
items.when: Before tearing down or briefing any swipe

items.title: All video runs one process: a variation, opening, remake or new ad runs the same chain, checks and steps;…
items.text: All video runs one process: a variation, opening, remake or new ad runs the same chain, checks and steps; anything a variation needs comes from the main chain, never a copy.
items.why: A side path silently lost voice speed, tone and timed actions and made the opening slow.

items.title: Every ad-account change (pause, budget, launch) happens only on the owner's direct trigger for that specific…
items.text: Every ad-account change (pause, budget, launch) happens only on the owner's direct trigger for that specific action; never chain one off a queue, schedule or agent.
items.why: Ad-account actions spend or stop real money.

items.title: Pass every pre-final gate automatically on the chain's best work within existing rulings; never bring a…
items.text: Pass every pre-final gate automatically on the chain's best work within existing rulings; never bring a mid-chain hold to the owner. The owner's one creative stop is the finished ad, and that approval releases hook versions and thumbnails.
items.why: Step sign-offs stalled the chain; he wants to judge the final ad, not edit.

items.title: Run organic as authority-figure content: openly AI authority characters per brand on their own accounts,…
items.text: Run organic as authority-figure content: openly AI authority characters per brand on their own accounts, posting free, helpful reels daily at volume (about seven a week), tracking every reel and breeding winners.
items.why: The goal is organic impressions at volume at very low cost.

items.title: Treat a viral organic swipe as the hook of an ad, not the whole piece: keep the full ad arc (placement,…
items.text: Treat a viral organic swipe as the hook of an ad, not the whole piece: keep the full ad arc (placement, expansion, proof, close) and never cap length or remove sections in a run ruling; only the owner makes a piece organic-only.
items.why: A one-joke, no-offer cap left good content with no ad arc and no expansion.

items.title: For an original idea (not a swipe), round it out with position, customer language, research and offers, set…
items.text: For an original idea (not a swipe), round it out with position, customer language, research and offers, set the awareness stage first, get a format-free concept brief approved, then pick formats (format, style, medium kept as separate fields) and run it into each chain's writing step as a grid across formats and awareness stages.
items.why: Remaking swipes is easy; a fleshed-out unique brief lets any ad in any format run with high confidence.
items.when: Turning the owner's own ideas into ads

items.title: Never write a landing page freehand: rebuild the base page from a winning swipe matched on avatar and…
items.text: Never write a landing page freehand: rebuild the base page from a winning swipe matched on avatar and category first, then make one variation per sub-avatar off that base, with every stage's prompt and output visible so fixes go into the prompt, not the output.
items.why: Hand-varying a live page skipped the proven structure and left nothing to tighten.

items.title: On landing pages, never invent proof: star rows, badges and reviewer slots render nothing when there is no…
items.text: On landing pages, never invent proof: star rows, badges and reviewer slots render nothing when there is no real figure, and the guarantee badge is typeset from the page's own guarantee line; never generate the product's printed label (use the brand's photograph).
items.why: Template blocks render invented proof when empty and generators redraw labels wrong.

items.title: Paint a page's buttons and accents with the brand's live button colour, and never call a page done until it…
items.text: Paint a page's buttons and accents with the brand's live button colour, and never call a page done until it has been checked as built, in full-page screenshots at phone and desktop widths, not from measurements alone.
items.why: The wrong token produced off-brand buttons that only showed on the built page.

items.title: Paid ads end on the proven winners' own CTA wording sending the viewer straight to the offer page (not a…
items.text: Paid ads end on the proven winners' own CTA wording sending the viewer straight to the offer page (not a quiz), with no price said; ad bodies come from proven assets and every script gets the spice pass before review.
items.why: The proven scripts' CTA is what converted, and unspiced scripts read choppy; replaces the earlier quiz destination.

items.title: Run every independent ad and stage in parallel, never queued behind another; serialize only when one step…
items.text: Run every independent ad and stage in parallel, never queued behind another; serialize only when one step truly needs another's output, and don't let cost limit throughput.
items.why: Nine-figure scale needs a system that makes thousands of ads a day; a peer makes about 3,000.

items.title: Build AI ad concepts from the {avatar}'s researched worlds first: name the world he actually watches, cast an…
items.text: Build AI ad concepts from the {avatar}'s researched worlds first: name the world he actually watches, cast an obvious parody lookalike of a known figure from it (never the real person), aim the bit at the problem, then add two lines of words; make cultural lookalike casting the default.
items.why: The concept only lands when it is relevant entertainment for that avatar; generic celebrity bits miss.
items.when: AI ad concepts, statics and video

items.title: For evergreen problem-aware statics, open on the problem she feels year-round, leave the season out of the…
items.text: For evergreen problem-aware statics, open on the problem she feels year-round, leave the season out of the headline, lead with the payoff customers feel and keep side benefits (scent) as side notes in customer language only.
items.why: Body care still sells on felt problems in cooler months; non-customer words don't land.

items.title: When widening a {hero product} into adjacent problems, you may mention related conditions but never claim the…
items.text: When widening a {hero product} into adjacent problems, you may mention related conditions but never claim the product cures or treats them.
items.why: Scaling to wider problems lowers CPA and widens age range without making medical claims.
items.when: Expanding angles to related skin conditions

items.title: State ship-by and arrival dates only from measured real order data (cutoff time, transit percentiles), and…
items.text: State ship-by and arrival dates only from measured real order data (cutoff time, transit percentiles), and re-measure before changing them or claiming faster shipping anywhere.
items.why: The owner wants proper likely ship-by dates, not guesses.
items.when: Checkout, receipt and landing page shipping claims

items.title: Pull swipes only from advertisers in the {brand}'s own audience lane (women's brands for a women's brand,…
items.text: Pull swipes only from advertisers in the {brand}'s own audience lane (women's brands for a women's brand, men's for men's); check the advertiser yourself rather than trusting a 'shared' pool label.
items.why: A swipe carries its audience's look and voice; a wrong-lane swipe breaks the ad before writing starts.

items.title: Source the brand position from the live store first, then the funnel copy, then older brand files; never take…
items.text: Source the brand position from the live store first, then the funnel copy, then older brand files; never take an angle (such as clean-only or a label attack) that the product's own label contradicts.
items.why: Old position files were written before the full picture, and a claim the label contradicts is false.

items.title: The brand's authority figure must embody the result: her own appearance is the product proof, so the problem…
items.text: The brand's authority figure must embody the result: her own appearance is the product proof, so the problem is shown on the models or the viewer, never on the authority.
items.why: A spotted, weathered authority undercuts the proof that sells the product.

items.title: A cast member is one reference headshot (plus emotional states) for face and body only; outfits and…
items.text: A cast member is one reference headshot (plus emotional states) for face and body only; outfits and accessories are separate face-free banked elements picked visibly per video, with the face injected onto the body.
items.why: Baking person, outfit and accessories into one look forces whole remakes and hides wardrobe decisions, and one headshot keeps the face identical frame by frame.
items.when: Casting and wardrobe for AI video and images

items.title: Every picture ad starts by building the swipe's scene as a 3D set at true sizes (product from its own…
items.text: Every picture ad starts by building the swipe's scene as a 3D set at true sizes (product from its own true-size build, the swipe's camera and light), printing it with a fresh product casting sheet, swapping the swipe's moment props for ours, then setting words on top; use a custom set per brief, never skip it.
items.why: Depth, sizes and light programmed in 3D look real; pasted or prompted versions looked stuck on, and per-brief sets proved far more consistent than reusable ones.

items.title: A static batch is six pictures: the approved concept picture plus exactly five one-change variations, each…
items.text: A static batch is six pictures: the approved concept picture plus exactly five one-change variations, each made as an edit of the approved picture through the same path; never remake a variation from the swipe.
items.why: Everything going through the same path keeps the output consistent.

items.title: Every generated picture in a video obeys five rules: the real product only, no words in the picture (text…
items.text: Every generated picture in a video obeys five rules: the real product only, no words in the picture (text goes on in the edit), only the brief's props, one person matching the cast master, and our set (none of the swipe's decor). Look at every picture before any clip is made, and fix failures at the source.
items.why: Early pictures showed a drawn product, the swipe's props and text, a different face and the swipe's decor.

items.title: Keep all purchases flowing through each brand's one ad pixel (store and funnel together); separate funnel,…
items.text: Keep all purchases flowing through each brand's one ad pixel (store and funnel together); separate funnel, store and blended results only in your own reporting views.
items.why: Segmenting the pixel risks the platform's learning, and ads lift total store sales too.

items.title: Name organic pages by the category the brand's mechanism sits in, in the words people search, with the…
items.text: Name organic pages by the category the brand's mechanism sits in, in the words people search, with the mechanism called out subtly; name personas as a plain first and last name (or Dr. + first name). Never clever or themed, never so generic it could be any brand.
items.why: A clever name reads as a brand front; a plain one reads like a page people already follow.
items.when: Naming organic pages, accounts and personas

items.title: Lean new creative toward solution-aware, product-aware and most-aware audiences once unaware and…
items.text: Lean new creative toward solution-aware, product-aware and most-aware audiences once unaware and problem-aware coverage is built out.
items.why: Enough unaware and problem-aware creative has been made for both brands.

items.title: Design production so it runs on any platform: inputs and outputs always land in the same places, every brief…
items.text: Design production so it runs on any platform: inputs and outputs always land in the same places, every brief carries one tool-agnostic run sheet (model, exact prompt, element ids, settings, output name, return place), and every workflow states its tools and edit manifest in plain files.
items.why: Producers work in other tools, and anything that only works inside one session is lost to them.

items.title: Keep proprietary ecommerce knowledge (frameworks, logic, research) separate from execution tools, and build…
items.text: Keep proprietary ecommerce knowledge (frameworks, logic, research) separate from execution tools, and build it to be metered: outsiders pay a usage fee to pull on the knowledge.
items.why: The knowledge is the scarce, defensible asset; execution tools are cheap to rent and copy.

items.title: Run topic research through the real concept process: one problem file per product and problem (her words,…
items.text: Run topic research through the real concept process: one problem file per product and problem (her words, what can and can't be said, where the product meets it, risks), then a concept brief for approval, then injection into a proven format; test new concepts only in proven, cheap formats.
items.why: Research belongs in the real system, and cheap proven formats keep tests affordable.
items.when: Problem and topic research for new concepts

items.title: Every product kit records how the product physically behaves (how it rests, what it can't do, how it is held,…
items.text: Every product kit records how the product physically behaves (how it rests, what it can't do, how it is held, how it is used) from the brand's own files and pictures, and no picture shows it doing what it physically can't.
items.why: A product shown doing the impossible is a wasted generation; reading the brand's files first cuts re-rolls.
items.when: Any picture or clip with the product

items.title: Cast products like people: one product casting sheet per product, and build any missing angle as a true-size…
items.text: Cast products like people: one product casting sheet per product, and build any missing angle as a true-size 3D model first, layering the real look on after; start from the product's existing 3D model and change it only where real frames prove it wrong.
items.why: Shortcuts without the true-size 3D build came out wrong, and matching sheets are the base for every ad.

items.title: Every product casting sheet uses one fixed layout: front, three-quarter, side, back, from below, from above,…
items.text: Every product casting sheet uses one fixed layout: front, three-quarter, side, back, from below, from above, then a how-it-works row; never lay a sheet out by hand.
items.why: The sheets are the base for producing ads, so they must match.

items.title: Take product grips and holds from real creator and UGC footage of the product in hand before writing a hold…
items.text: Take product grips and holds from real creator and UGC footage of the product in hand before writing a hold into a prompt; those frames guide the pose and are never placed in the ad.
items.why: An invented grip reads fake.
items.when: Any shot with the product in a hand

items.title: The image model draws the scene, people and hands but never invents the product: a resting product is the…
items.text: The image model draws the scene, people and hands but never invents the product: a resting product is the real render or photo pasted in place (held, never delivered, if it can't be laid on), and a product in use is drawn from its real photo as reference and checked against it.
items.why: Generated products drift in shape, grip and light and read as slop; pasting only fits a resting product.
items.when: Every static and video shot with the product

items.title: Recreate the swipe for our brand shot by shot, and re-act every beat that acts out the swipe's problem so it…
items.text: Recreate the swipe for our brand shot by shot, and re-act every beat that acts out the swipe's problem so it shows ours; no beat may carry a claim or problem that isn't the product's.
items.why: A swap keeps the swipe's actions, so the ad ended up about the wrong problem.

items.title: Spend what it takes on foundational product masters (3D builds, angles, photoreal passes) with no credit cap,…
items.text: Spend what it takes on foundational product masters (3D builds, angles, photoreal passes) with no credit cap, keeping only the right results; this does not lift caps on data pulls or ad spend.
items.why: Product masters are the base for all image, website and email work, so getting them right outranks spend.

items.title: Index every verified element once (product masters, cast, sets, swipes) and pull it directly into every new…
items.text: Index every verified element once (product masters, cast, sets, swipes) and pull it directly into every new asset instead of re-sourcing it.
items.why: Consistency across every asset and far less time and token waste as production scales.
items.when: Any asset that uses an existing element

items.title: A style restyle (puppet, plush, cartoon) changes characters and set only; the product is never restyled, and…
items.text: A style restyle (puppet, plush, cartoon) changes characters and set only; the product is never restyled, and its real texture photo goes in as a reference beside it.
items.why: Restyles bleed into the product and it must read as real in every look.

items.title: For every product shot in animated ads, send the real packshot plus a real in-use or in-hand photo with exact…
items.text: For every product shot in animated ads, send the real packshot plus a real in-use or in-hand photo with exact shape words and the real grip; clip it as a short rigid take with minimal camera movement (no turn-to-camera or rack focus), and check a frame strip before the cut.
items.why: A styled product board alone let the model redesign the product, and motion warped it further.
items.when: Animated and AI video product shots

items.title: Teardown and writing are shared across formats, but production takes a separate line per execution type…
