items.text: Teardown and writing are shared across formats, but production takes a separate line per execution type (movie, talking head, phone thread, cartoon, song); decide the line before production, build each scene as a whole continuous moment, and keep cutscenes distinct from B-roll.
items.why: Treating every video the same caused manual tweaks, inconsistency and overspend.

items.title: Once a script reaches production, treat it as locked: never reopen claims, length or story; production limits…
items.text: Once a script reaches production, treat it as locked: never reopen claims, length or story; production limits are one change per retake and three takes at most.
items.why: Writing and strategy are done by then, and reopening them slows production.

items.title: Pull social-proof numbers (orders, customers) from the live store count, round down when spoken, and note the…
items.text: Pull social-proof numbers (orders, customers) from the live store count, round down when spoken, and note the count's date; never copy a number from an old ad.
items.why: Old ads freeze a number that has since grown; the live count is bigger and true.
items.when: Scripts and copy with proof numbers

items.title: When testing a site or theme change on small traffic, lock a pre-change baseline (28 and 14 days), read mix…
items.text: When testing a site or theme change on small traffic, lock a pre-change baseline (28 and 14 days), read mix metrics like refill and multi-pack share after about a week, and don't read conversion rate until about five weeks; compare against last year's same-week drift for seasonality.
items.why: Conversion rate on small daily traffic swings too much to read early.

items.title: In production, never pick a cheaper model or cut a step to save cost; use the model and steps the format…
items.text: In production, never pick a cheaper model or cut a step to save cost; use the model and steps the format calls for and maximize quality, realism and volume (paid rounds still get a stated budget and stop point).
items.why: Work made on a cheaper model to save credits came out looking fake with terrible movement.
items.when: Choosing models and steps in production

items.title: For a small fix (one field, one line, one picture), change only that element and re-run only the check it…
items.text: For a small fix (one field, one line, one picture), change only that element and re-run only the check it touches; never re-run a whole stage, picture set or clip set.
items.why: Full re-runs burn time and tokens re-proving what already passed.

items.title: Every ad tested on a quiz is also tested on the offer page that sells the same product: one creative, two ads.
items.text: Every ad tested on a quiz is also tested on the offer page that sells the same product: one creative, two ads.
items.why: Sometimes the offer page just works better, and quiz-only testing hides that.
items.when: Paid ad launches pointing to a quiz

items.title: In strategy and ideation use only real data: every concept, angle or matrix row carries receipts (real posts…
items.text: In strategy and ideation use only real data: every concept, angle or matrix row carries receipts (real posts from avatar research, real comments, or a named founder insight), or it is cut; creativity dials go up only at execution.
items.why: Ideas invented from general knowledge miss; ideas grounded in research and customer language land.

items.title: Every generated picture (email, page, static) starts from a real-life reference (owned creator footage,…
items.text: Every generated picture (email, page, static) starts from a real-life reference (owned creator footage, customer before-afters, archive, store photos, product kit), then our version is generated on top; never a scene, face or product from text alone.
items.why: Pictures made from words alone come out generic and wrong.
items.when: Every picture slot in emails, pages and ads

items.title: Real customer before-afters and archive content are fully usable in ads without owner sign-off; group…
items.text: Real customer before-afters and archive content are fully usable in ads without owner sign-off; group before-afters by the problem they show.
items.why: Real proof is the strongest asset, and approval holds on it slowed the system.

items.title: Learn from AI-made swipes but never remake one; find a real similar post (mostly on TikTok or Instagram) and…
items.text: Learn from AI-made swipes but never remake one; find a real similar post (mostly on TikTok or Instagram) and swipe that instead.
items.why: Copying an AI picture stacks fake on fake and drops quality and realness.

items.title: For every picture with our people, generate the image, then run a skin-only realism pass against the cast…
items.text: For every picture with our people, generate the image, then run a skin-only realism pass against the cast headshot, then apply the medium's lens look (e.g. phone camera) last; scene depth comes from a 3D set printed per shot.
items.why: One generation carrying many references loses skin fidelity; realism and medium look are separate jobs.

items.title: Write research and customer language verbatim: exact quotes with who, where and when, checked against the…
items.text: Write research and customer language verbatim: exact quotes with who, where and when, checked against the source; where none exists write 'no verbatim yet', never a paraphrase dressed as a quote, and label our own drafts as ours.
items.why: Work built on paraphrase drifts from how the customer actually talks.

items.title: Pay for deeper research pulls (social and forum scrapes) freely without asking first; ad-intelligence…
items.text: Pay for deeper research pulls (social and forum scrapes) freely without asking first; ad-intelligence credit-plan pulls still need a plan.
items.why: Research pulls cost a few dollars and asking slowed the content engine.

items.title: When selling to men, lead with the mirror moment after a life reset (divorce, breakup, new chapter), not…
items.text: When selling to men, lead with the mirror moment after a life reset (divorce, breakup, new chapter), not physical pain or irritation; build rankings and angles around it.
items.why: Men shrug off pain; the mirror moment is the one emotional stage that sells to them.

items.title: Reuse existing live ad copy on new video ads for the same product (checking it carries no dated promo); don't…
items.text: Reuse existing live ad copy on new video ads for the same product (checking it carries no dated promo); don't write unique copy per ad for now.
items.why: The creative is the variable; per-ad copy costs time for no gain.

items.title: Run the ad line fully automatically: pass any gate an existing ruling or the swipe already decides, and bring…
items.text: Run the ad line fully automatically: pass any gate an existing ruling or the swipe already decides, and bring the owner only genuine new creative calls, spend beyond approval, and finished output; on his feedback, trace the fault to its source stage and fix it there.
items.why: He built the gates and rulings so the machine can run; stops that his rulings already answer waste his time.

items.title: Edit ads by running the editing chain end to end; when it gets something wrong, fix the chain so every ad…
items.text: Edit ads by running the editing chain end to end; when it gets something wrong, fix the chain so every ad gets it right and re-run, never hand-tweak one video.
items.why: The chain already encodes the edit rules; micro-edits don't compound.

items.title: Plan every scene as a set-up (one place and camera) with a clear start, what happens inside in words, and a…
items.text: Plan every scene as a set-up (one place and camera) with a clear start, what happens inside in words, and a clear stop; one start picture per scene, an end picture only when it ends somewhere new, and returning set-ups reuse their picture (about 3-4 scenes for a 22-second verse).
items.why: A picture per line or bar blew up spend for no reason.

items.title: Name two formats on every video ad: the script format (what it says, e.g.
items.text: Name two formats on every video ad: the script format (what it says, e.g. remedy) and the production format (how it is made, e.g. talking head); never mix them in one list.
items.why: One ad needs both choices, and one word for both confused the work.

items.title: Approve a month's email plan (every send in plain words, the owner's calls, triggers) before any email is…
items.text: Approve a month's email plan (every send in plain words, the owner's calls, triggers) before any email is written.
items.why: The plan is the decision surface; writing before it's approved wastes work.

items.title: Send email campaigns only to engaged segments with a recency window (180 days when reactivating a dormant…
items.text: Send email campaigns only to engaged segments with a recency window (180 days when reactivating a dormant list), never to whole lifecycle segments; churned and unengaged get their own win-back and sunset flows.
items.why: Whole lifecycle segments are mostly dormant, so sending to them is a mass send.

items.title: Never re-ask the owner about something already ruled: when records disagree, the latest ruling or the…
items.text: Never re-ask the owner about something already ruled: when records disagree, the latest ruling or the practice in current use wins; ask only about what was never decided.
items.why: Re-asking re-litigates his own decisions and costs him time.

items.title: Shoot scenes like a film: build the 3D world once, rig the cast once, then film every scene and variation…
items.text: Shoot scenes like a film: build the 3D world once, rig the cast once, then film every scene and variation with cameras instead of generating scenes one by one.
items.why: Set and cast are paid for once; each new scene is then only camera and animation.

items.title: Treat a borrowed show (fight night, cooking show, soap) as a format and inject the brand through six roles:…
items.text: Treat a borrowed show (fight night, cooking show, soap) as a format and inject the brand through six roles: hero (the customer), villain (the problem given a face), the move (the product as the big moment), the voice (who explains the mechanism), the replay (the mechanism zoom), the verdict (the offer); pick visual style separately.
items.why: A show is a whole kind of entertainment the sub-avatar watches, not just a look; a show with no replay can't carry a mechanism.

items.title: Build every sequence in two halves: first a punchy skit that names the problem early, one picture and new…
items.text: Build every sequence in two halves: first a punchy skit that names the problem early, one picture and new movement per joke, literal visual gags, nothing random; then from the moment the product slides in, straight direct response: what it is, how it works, demonstration, results.
items.why: That structure made a cut ten times punchier, and the second half is where direct response does its work.

items.title: Organic slideshows carry only the brand's own products plus its named clipping partner, each as an ordinary…
items.text: Organic slideshows carry only the brand's own products plus its named clipping partner, each as an ordinary tip; never a third brand.
items.why: The owner's final word set the pair to match the clipping campaign.

items.title: Prepare every organic post and paid upload up to the last button; nothing posts until the owner's own tap.
items.text: Prepare every organic post and paid upload up to the last button; nothing posts until the owner's own tap.
items.why: Posting is an external send and his call.

items.title: In song ads every scene is a moving clip; never plan held stills or pan-over stills to save money.
items.text: In song ads every scene is a moving clip; never plan held stills or pan-over stills to save money.
items.why: The format is a moving film and held stills read as cheap; cost comes from resolution and model, not clip count.

items.title: Stage song-ad pictures on the real cultural TV and internet moments each story echoes, frame-swiped with our…
items.text: Stage song-ad pictures on the real cultural TV and internet moments each story echoes, frame-swiped with our cast in our own style and with show and platform branding stripped.
items.why: The familiar setting keeps the audience watching; the style keeps it ours.

items.title: Song ads from a swipe keep every plot beat of the swipe's story; the punch line is sung in the first second,…
items.text: Song ads from a swipe keep every plot beat of the swipe's story; the punch line is sung in the first second, length follows the story (about 2:30-3:30), and flow comes from sizing sections to their lines (first word within 1 s, no gap over 2 s, dead air at most 5%), never from cutting story. Describe the avatar's favourite artists' sound rather than naming them.
items.why: The ridiculous story is why it works, and dead air or a slow opening loses the listener.

items.title: Run song ads for volume at lowest customer acquisition cost: keep the pipeline never idle (write songs…
items.text: Run song ads for volume at lowest customer acquisition cost: keep the pipeline never idle (write songs ahead), make each ad as enthralling as possible, and benchmark around $15-30 per finished ad.
items.why: Competitors print about 30 a week in this format; volume of enthralling ads at low cost wins the race.

items.title: Build every scene of an animated song ad in a 3D world, one by one, the same way every time (reuse a world…
items.text: Build every scene of an animated song ad in a 3D world, one by one, the same way every time (reuse a world first; never prompt a room), and make each shot show the literal lyric with a start and end picture per clip.
items.why: Depth and a consistent look come from the worlds; prompted rooms came out flat and mismatched.

items.title: Check every asset each time it is made or moves stage to stage against written criteria, and fix a miss at…
items.text: Check every asset each time it is made or moves stage to stage against written criteria, and fix a miss at its own step (not a full re-run, not a skip); finish every creative batch with a completeness check.
items.why: Work slipped between stages, got re-run or missed, and batches arrived short of the required count.

items.title: Make static ads from proven statics in the same audience lane's swipe libraries, run through the image…
items.text: Make static ads from proven statics in the same audience lane's swipe libraries, run through the image stages; never hand-write layouts or model one brand's set on another brand's work.
items.why: Hand-written directions borrowed from another brand's set skipped the proven process and the right audience's swipes.

items.title: Read live prices, variants, selling plans and theme from the store itself; never quote a repo copy or…
items.text: Read live prices, variants, selling plans and theme from the store itself; never quote a repo copy or generated offer bank as current, and say so when only a snapshot exists.
items.why: Snapshots age; the live store is the source of truth.
items.when: Any work quoting prices or offers

items.title: In every song-ad format, open on the story (the girl, the conflict, the most shocking detail in the first…
items.text: In every song-ad format, open on the story (the girl, the conflict, the most shocking detail in the first bar), then the problem, then failed solutions, then the turn, then the solution in one line; never open on the problem or the pitch.
items.why: The story is the watch time; the problem and product land only after the viewer is hooked on the drama.

items.title: The owner makes only the strategic calls (run it, offer, target, spend, CPA ceiling, creative lead);…
items.text: The owner makes only the strategic calls (run it, offer, target, spend, CPA ceiling, creative lead); assigning people, task lists, due dates and chasing belong to the project manager.
items.why: Project management work overwhelms the owner and pulls him off high-level initiatives.

items.title: Separate style from format with one test: if you swap it and the script, cast and beats all stay the same,…
items.text: Separate style from format with one test: if you swap it and the script, cast and beats all stay the same, it's a style; if the script or who carries it must change, it's a format. A persona is cast, not format.
items.why: Mixing styles, formats and cast in one list blocks reusing a format with a different style.
items.when: Classifying swipes and building creative banks

items.title: Describe every swipe by four layers: format, style, structure and how it's made (from scratch, cast swap,…
items.text: Describe every swipe by four layers: format, style, structure and how it's made (from scratch, cast swap, real footage); a format not in the bank waits for the owner's call.
items.why: Layering lets a format run with a different style or structure and lets the system learn each format.

items.title: Push creative dials high but keep the swipe's fidelity: keep its camera, setting, light, grain, skin and…
items.text: Push creative dials high but keep the swipe's fidelity: keep its camera, setting, light, grain, skin and type, and put one surreal idea inside that real scene treated as normal; compare side by side with the swipe before keeping.
items.why: The ad works because it passes as native in the feed; both too plain and too fake failed.

items.title: Every character swap sends the full casting sheet (master, turnaround, angles, details, look) and names the…
items.text: Every character swap sends the full casting sheet (master, turnaround, angles, details, look) and names the before or after state; one person carries the whole ad, clips play at normal speed, and any swap that kept the original person is dropped.
items.why: Swaps sent with only a face kept the source creator's body and sometimes face and read as a stranger.

items.title: Never brief into a channel lane the brand doesn't run; research runs in five domains (what she watches,…
items.text: Never brief into a channel lane the brand doesn't run; research runs in five domains (what she watches, competitor bets, forums in her words, long-form sources with each claim marked sayable or not, her life and cohort) plus a synthesis of agreements, contradictions and unanswered high-volume questions.
items.why: Lanes are declared per brand with reasons, and cross-domain synthesis finds what one source misses.

items.title: File nothing a research agent finds into a brand until the owner moves it, and aim research at the rooms…
items.text: File nothing a research agent finds into a brand until the owner moves it, and aim research at the rooms where the avatar actually talks, checking each one matches her body part and problem.
items.why: Agent-seeded rooms produced off-topic material, and unvetted findings pollute the brand files.

items.title: Find research rooms by searching the sub-avatar's own words rather than writing a list from assumptions,…
items.text: Find research rooms by searching the sub-avatar's own words rather than writing a list from assumptions, check every room and row against the avatar's demographics (age, gender, skin tone, region, language) and drop mismatches with a reason, and keep raw research raw.
items.why: Agent-seeded rooms came back off-topic, and a room that fits one brand's customer can be a mismatch for another's.

items.title: If a swipe already shows our own product, keep the real photo and change only the words; skip any rebuild.
items.text: If a swipe already shows our own product, keep the real photo and change only the words; skip any rebuild.
items.why: A real photo of our product beats any rebuild and costs nothing.
items.when: Static swipes that already feature our product

items.title: Before voicing an adapted script, read it top to bottom as one argument: the costly fix, the 'no X on earth'…
items.text: Before voicing an adapted script, read it top to bottom as one argument: the costly fix, the 'no X on earth' line and the close must be the same kind of thing, and prices match the offer file.
items.why: A slot-by-slot swap can pass every check and still switch category mid-argument.

items.title: A talking clip's only movement reference is the swipe's own creator from a clean stretch; keep clip…
items.text: A talking clip's only movement reference is the swipe's own creator from a clean stretch; keep clip references simple and show them per clip before spending.
items.why: The swipe creator's movement is exactly what is being copied; a bank person adds nothing.

items.title: For talking-head videos: one approved start picture for all talking scenes, scenes grouped into long takes up…
items.text: For talking-head videos: one approved start picture for all talking scenes, scenes grouped into long takes up to 15 seconds (never one short line in a short take), one clean movement reference, no extra face sheets, no overlay words in the direction, and the voice at the swipe's pace capped at a real talking speed.
items.why: This recipe was called perfect; short lines in long takes made the model invent words and an uncapped pace garbled the voice.

items.title: Generated voice takes its pacing and pause length from the swipe's own voice, never a generic default speed.
items.text: Generated voice takes its pacing and pause length from the swipe's own voice, never a generic default speed.
items.why: Audio sounded choppy because the read didn't move like the swipe.

items.title: Teammates may approve production, run priced paid remakes and schedule email; only the ad launch stays with…
items.text: Teammates may approve production, run priced paid remakes and schedule email; only the ad launch stays with the owner. Don't add new owner-only gates anywhere else.
items.why: Real people run the line now, and gating every step on the owner stalls volume.

items.title: Inject a brand by substitution, not rewrite: the source transcript is the template and only brand slots…
items.text: Inject a brand by substitution, not rewrite: the source transcript is the template and only brand slots change.
items.why: The swipe's script is what works; rewriting loses it.

items.title: Write hooks as a straight-swipe control plus five variations and let a human pick; in expansion, every added…
items.text: Write hooks as a straight-swipe control plus five variations and let a human pick; in expansion, every added move must name the baseline line already doing its job or stay out; stages layer and never cannibalize, and the close continues the story ('this is what I ended up doing').
items.why: A strong baseline may need one move or none; blanket insertions and model recommendations dilute what works.
items.when: Script hook, expansion and close stages

items.title: Keep two brief lanes separate: a creator brief only for formats torn from that creator's own posts (her…
items.text: Keep two brief lanes separate: a creator brief only for formats torn from that creator's own posts (her structures back to her), and a general brief from swipe research written to no one, then graded against the roster for fit.
items.why: A creator's own posts are proven for her, while swipe formats need matching to the right maker.

items.title: The creator reads one short page: the ask, lines to 'say however you'd say them', the one shot that can't be…
items.text: The creator reads one short page: the ask, lines to 'say however you'd say them', the one shot that can't be skipped, 5-8 beats, six ways to start, wardrobe and location only as needed, and a few pictures; the detailed spec stays internal.
items.why: Creators reading the full shot list didn't know what to do with it.

items.title: Build reusable 3D worlds per brand (the room is the core, sets go inside it when a job needs one, then the…
items.text: Build reusable 3D worlds per brand (the room is the core, sets go inside it when a job needs one, then the character), and reuse them for series and character swaps.
items.why: Reuse across series and swaps avoids burning credits on new rooms.

items.title: Run the system the most token-efficient way that gives the same outcome; script repeat work only when the…
items.text: Run the system the most token-efficient way that gives the same outcome; script repeat work only when the outcome holds, and keep the custom version where scripting lowers quality.
items.why: Long freehand runs cost far more and vary run to run; waste and inconsistency share a cause.

items.title: Training material shows real clicks on the real tools with one real example running through, works with the…
items.text: Training material shows real clicks on the real tools with one real example running through, works with the sound off (one idea per screen, burned-in captions), opens each module with a real lesson or story, and shows good and bad outputs side by side; scripts are approved before any animation.
items.why: It has to be clear for anyone regardless of language, with no rambling, focused on execution.

items.title: Pay creators affiliate-only at 5% of sales for the whole partnership, never a percentage of ad spend; count…
items.text: Pay creators affiliate-only at 5% of sales for the whole partnership, never a percentage of ad spend; count only deliveries through the creator platform, seed general briefs of proven formats, and run creator ads at about $10/day per brand.
items.why: Nobody can predict ROAS, so pay only on sales.

items.title: Swipe picks are ultra-viral only: sort by views and set a floor of at least 500K before fitting the topic; if…
items.text: Swipe picks are ultra-viral only: sort by views and set a floor of at least 500K before fitting the topic; if too few clear it, propose a wider pull with a dollar cap rather than padding with small videos.
items.why: Small videos chosen for topic fit aren't proven attention.

items.title: Before any remake, put the best existing takes into the edit and cover small flaws there; make one thing,…
items.text: Before any remake, put the best existing takes into the edit and cover small flaws there; make one thing, look, then the next, never batch-generate a whole video's clips before the first are seen, and use fewer frames.
items.why: A strict automatic judge plus re-rolls turned small flaws into a pile of paid regenerations.

items.title: Variation runs are a winners x formats grid: every top ad goes into every new format; keep one cut per winner…
items.text: Variation runs are a winners x formats grid: every top ad goes into every new format; keep one cut per winner when winners are essentially the same ad, drop formats that don't fit the avatar, run one offer per product, and let the owner pick the squares.
items.why: Volume at once beats one-by-one picking, while redundant winners and off-avatar formats waste runs.
items.when: Proven ad into new format variation cycles

items.title: Make hook-variation cuts and thumbnails last, only after the main control cut is settled; at the edit, cover…
items.text: Make hook-variation cuts and thumbnails last, only after the main control cut is settled; at the edit, cover faults with punch-ins, close-ups and B-roll and regenerate only what is absolutely necessary.
items.why: The main cut changes during review, and versions built on an unsettled cut get redone.

items.title: QA a page the way a customer arrives (real entry URL, real order reference, cache proven fresh) and check the…
items.text: QA a page the way a customer arrives (real entry URL, real order reference, cache proven fresh) and check the first seconds as well as the settled state; never verify by disabling whatever hides content.
items.why: Bypassing the real load states hid defects that only exist in them.

items.title: Make awareness variations as new hook heads on the same body (near free); make problem variations as new…
items.text: Make awareness variations as new hook heads on the same body (near free); make problem variations as new brief runs.
items.why: Hooks are cheap to vary while a new problem changes the whole argument.

items.title: A variation keeps the previous run's exact settings (voice speed and tone, pauses, silence, clip route and…
items.text: A variation keeps the previous run's exact settings (voice speed and tone, pauses, silence, clip route and resolution); word count may change, pace and feel may not, and openings need real movement and camera, never a locked still.
items.why: A side path silently lost voice speed and tone and made the opening slow.

items.title: A talking clip keeps its own sound: never lay a separate voice file over it or use another talking take as…
items.text: A talking clip keeps its own sound: never lay a separate voice file over it or use another talking take as B-roll (more than one frame of lip slip is held); cut dead air on the clip at pauses, place B-roll by the words it covers, and put the hook headline on frame one with no fade.
items.why: Laid-over voices drift out of sync and read fake.

items.title: Make the audio first: one full continuous voiceover read (never stitched line by line), dead air cut, then…
items.text: Make the audio first: one full continuous voiceover read (never stitched line by line), dead air cut, then music and effects, and build scenes on top of the approved audio.
items.why: Scenes timed to finished audio cut cleanly; line-by-line reads sound stitched.

items.title: The teardown labels every beat as A-roll or B-roll with what the audio says, what the caption says and the…
items.text: The teardown labels every beat as A-roll or B-roll with what the audio says, what the caption says and the sound under it, so each element can be generated separately.
items.why: B-roll was missing from past runs because it was never labelled.

items.title: A prompt change is always a new numbered prompt file; never edit a prompt in place.
items.text: A prompt change is always a new numbered prompt file; never edit a prompt in place.
items.why: Versioned prompts keep every output traceable to the prompt that made it.

items.title: Once a reel comes out clean, measure every stage's minutes and cut the biggest first (parallel runs,…
items.text: Once a reel comes out clean, measure every stage's minutes and cut the biggest first (parallel runs, overlapping stages, faster models only where quality is untouched), targeting the same quality and cost in about a third of the time.
items.why: Volume is the business goal; the slow line is acceptable only as the dial-in phase.

items.title: Turn every production finding into a gate the code enforces or a labelled prompt slot before resorting to a…
items.text: Turn every production finding into a gate the code enforces or a labelled prompt slot before resorting to a prose rule.
items.why: Prose rules failed twice on the same slop classes; labelled slots beat prose rules.

items.title: Transcribe every talking clip and compare it to its script line; it ships only at 85% match or better.
items.text: Transcribe every talking clip and compare it to its script line; it ships only at 85% match or better.
items.why: A model lip-synced perfectly to invented words, which only a transcript check caught.

items.title: Build every script on the awareness and sophistication framework: every swipe gets a doctrine read…
items.text: Build every script on the awareness and sophistication framework: every swipe gets a doctrine read (framework, sections, awareness entry and exit, desire, techniques) and is banked; never force depth onto hooks, and give no scene a fixed length (a scene plays out fully).
items.why: The awareness framework is the backbone of the whole system's copy.

items.title: Write copy to be spoken: one thought per breath, an ellipsis where a person pauses mid-thought, a lift where…
items.text: Write copy to be spoken: one thought per breath, an ellipsis where a person pauses mid-thought, a lift where the point lands; never chop it into short listed sentences.
items.why: Three short sentences read as a list, not a person.

items.title: A scene whose proof has no verifiable fact on file builds nothing and is flagged as a finding.
items.text: A scene whose proof has no verifiable fact on file builds nothing and is flagged as a finding.
items.why: Unverifiable proof can't be shown or said.

items.title: When a hosted model refuses or underperforms, look for the purpose-built model on the same host and read the…
items.text: When a hosted model refuses or underperforms, look for the purpose-built model on the same host and read the endpoint's schema before declaring it closed, and never let an older version of a model slip in on a hosted door.
items.why: A purpose-built model on the same host solved the refusal, and older versions quietly degrade output.

items.title: Treat creative as swapping on data: every axis (creator, format, angle, model, actor, headline) is a bank of…
items.text: Treat creative as swapping on data: every axis (creator, format, angle, model, actor, headline) is a bank of interchangeable assets, each run is one combination, and data decides the next.
items.why: Mixing and matching banked assets on results is how the system scales.

items.title: Every new AI character goes source, identity block, one canonical master, full board set, voice, and only…
items.text: Every new AI character goes source, identity block, one canonical master, full board set, voice, and only then is castable; every cast character links to a core or sub-avatar and looks and sounds like her, and the avatar's cast member is bound on every run.
items.why: A defined master and avatar link keep the same person consistent and on-target in every run.

items.title: Any teardown can route to creator, AI or founder production; the chain decides the route, and the founder…
items.text: Any teardown can route to creator, AI or founder production; the chain decides the route, and the founder route is the same script plus a founder-only 'why I made this' adjustment.
items.why: One record should feed every production route, and some formats will never be AI.

items.title: Make video feel real through emotional connection: emotion per shot, character and culture-specific gestures,…
items.text: Make video feel real through emotional connection: emotion per shot, character and culture-specific gestures, marks of a lived life in every picture, a sense beat, the swipe's own rhythm (fewer, longer shots), and strict continuity, finished with captions native to the platform.
items.why: The natural-feel reel beat every mechanical one; over-cutting and over-directed acting read as fake.

items.title: Run the viewer check once, make one direct fix from the rebuttal bank, and move on; never re-run panels in…
items.text: Run the viewer check once, make one direct fix from the rebuttal bank, and move on; never re-run panels in rounds or bring its failures to the owner as a blocker.
items.why: Re-check loops held briefs for several paid rounds and kept failing on the same things.
items.when: Viewer and persona checks on scripts

items.title: Generate talking clips with picture and voice together in one audio-driven frontier model, never re-voiced…
items.text: Generate talking clips with picture and voice together in one audio-driven frontier model, never re-voiced after; never drop resolution or takes to save money.
items.why: Re-voicing loosened lip sync and low-resolution takes melted hands and objects; replaces the cheap-takes-then-upscale rule.

items.title: A character's voice must match who they are (race, age, region): read each voice's labels and listen before…
items.text: A character's voice must match who they are (race, age, region): read each voice's labels and listen before voicing, and never reuse another run's voice blind.
items.why: The wrong voice breaks the ad on the first line.

items.title: When a swipe opens with no words, write its hook versions as scroll stoppers (picture, motion, caption,…
items.text: When a swipe opens with no words, write its hook versions as scroll stoppers (picture, motion, caption, sound), never spoken lines.
items.why: Spoken-hook logic is the wrong axis for a wordless opener.

items.title: Never fire a batch of paid generations on a loose instruction: build the workflow, test it on one brief, show…
items.text: Never fire a batch of paid generations on a loose instruction: build the workflow, test it on one brief, show it, and scale only on the owner's word.
items.why: A loose 'let's run that' launched 84 pictures he never scoped.

items.title: Set comedy skits inside worlds the market recognizes (the games they play, the shows they stay up with) and…
items.text: Set comedy skits inside worlds the market recognizes (the games they play, the shows they stay up with) and standardize the worlds, style, vibe, plot slots and elements so each new variation is one request with cost shown first, keeping a second-by-second swipe comparison as a standing step.
items.why: A skit in a recognized world worked, and volume from a machine beats hand craft.

items.title: Run creativity on a five-rung dial (swap, remix, transplant, story, auteur) with a floor that holds on every…
items.text: Run creativity on a five-rung dial (swap, remix, transplant, story, auteur) with a floor that holds on every rung: one problem, an awareness entry, desire, the mechanism inside, proof from files, and the brand's close; every opening line must stop the scroll.
items.why: Higher creativity must never drop the direct-response floor, and writers opened slow.

items.title: A new concept must differ by 3+ moves from past concepts and from the live ad library.
items.text: A new concept must differ by 3+ moves from past concepts and from the live ad library.
items.why: Near-duplicates waste test budget.

items.title: Always run the full writing line, spice and audit included; caps apply to paid generation (pictures, clips,…
items.text: Always run the full writing line, spice and audit included; caps apply to paid generation (pictures, clips, voice), never to writing.
items.why: Writing cut short to stay under a cap came out flat, with too few scenes and a choppy voice.

items.title: Count an ad's cost as production spend only (voice, pictures, generated video, credits); leave writing out of…
items.text: Count an ad's cost as production spend only (voice, pictures, generated video, credits); leave writing out of cost numbers and caps.
items.why: An ad is judged by what it takes to produce, not the writing runs.

items.title: Let performance pick the on-screen authority: double down on the authority figure whose ads win, speak to the…
items.text: Let performance pick the on-screen authority: double down on the authority figure whose ads win, speak to the core avatar vicariously through her, and report ad results by avatar and on-screen identity.
items.why: Avatar and identity performance should steer what gets made next.

items.title: Build younger avatars from real customer photos of people 20 and up, adapted into new faces; leave out anyone…
items.text: Build younger avatars from real customer photos of people 20 and up, adapted into new faces; leave out anyone on record under 20 and never invent faces from written notes.
items.why: Made-up faces from written notes miss the audience being sold to.

items.title: Mine competitors' ad libraries by spend
items.text: Open a competitor's ad library and sort their ads by impressions, highest first; the top ads are taking the spend, so swipe those. Spend is the proof an ad works, so you start from winners instead of guessing.
items.why: Spend is the proof an ad works, so you start from winners instead of guessing.
items.when: competitor research for paid social, before making new ads

items.title: Research avatar, pain and trending angles first
items.text: Before making any ad, write down which {avatar} you are talking to, the pain they feel, and which angles are trending in your research, then build only from that. Skipping research gives ads that look right and don't sell.
items.why: Skipping research is how you end up with ads that look right and don't sell.
items.when: before any new ad or creative batch

items.title: Give each project its own context file
items.text: Keep a personal context file and a separate context file for each project (for example logistics vs. a database build) instead of one shared file. The AI treats the top file as your whole world, so mixed files make it drag in unrelated work.
items.why: Claude treats the top file as your whole world, so mixed files make it bring up unrelated work.
items.when: working with AI coding/assistant tools across several projects

items.title: Always plan before you build with AI
items.text: When asking AI to build something, start in plan mode and review the plan before it edits anything. Edit mode on a big task changes things you did not approve.
items.why: Edit mode on a big task changes things you did not approve.
items.when: any AI-assisted build or large change

items.title: Start a new product test with the landing page
items.text: Start a new product test with the landing page: put a competitor's page and your own side by side, finish the page first, then make the creatives, running research and copy steps in a fixed order each time. The page sets what the ad must promise, so ads made after it match it.
items.why: The page tells you what the ad must promise, so ads made after it match it.
items.when: launching a new product or offer test

items.title: Sort competitors into L1, L2 and L3
items.text: Label each competitor L1 (same product, same pain), L2 (same customer, different mechanism) or L3 (same category, different mechanism or {avatar}), and pull ideas from all three levels. It stops you only copying direct rivals and shows where new angles come from.
items.why: It stops you only copying direct rivals and shows you where new angles come from.

items.title: Read ad numbers as ranges, not exact figures
items.text: Read CPA and similar ad numbers as ranges, not exact cents; small gaps between tools are normal. Attribution windows shift the numbers, so chasing cents wastes time.
items.why: Attribution windows change the numbers, so chasing cents wastes time.
items.when: reviewing paid media results across tools

items.title: When numbers differ from Ads Manager, check spend first
items.text: If reach or frequency in your database does not match the ad platform, compare total spend for the same dates first; if spend matches, the gap is usually the attribution setting. Spend is the trustworthy number that tells you whether the data pull worked.
items.why: Spend is the number you can trust, so it tells you whether the pull worked.
items.when: reconciling ad data pulls against the ad platform

items.title: Plan every test around three lanes
items.text: Define every test by three lanes: {avatar}, angle and format, not by the messaging. Those three decide whether an ad gets spend, so they are what you track.
items.why: Those three things decide whether an ad gets spend, so they are what you need to track.

items.title: Track hit rate per avatar and angle
items.text: Count how many {avatar}s and angles you tested and how many took spend, and track avatar and angle hit rates, not only ad hit rate. In his experience about 80% of spend ends up on three to five avatars and three to five angles, so knowing which ones is the real learning.
items.why: Most spend ends up on a few avatars and angles, so knowing which ones is the real learning.
items.when: ongoing creative testing on paid social

items.title: Judge each test against your KPI
items.text: After launch, ask whether each test hit the KPI: if not, write down why; if yes, refine it and build a repeatable flow around it. Every test then has a clear next step.
items.why: This gives every test a clear next step.

items.title: Keep winners and learnings, not every ad
items.text: Store only ads that hit the KPI plus a short note on why losers failed, not every ad. Most ads won't work, and clutter hides the ones that did.
items.why: Most ads will not work, and clutter hides the ones that did.
items.when: building a creative database or learning bank

items.title: Read hook rate as three-second views over impressions
items.text: Calculate hook rate per video as three-second views divided by impressions, look at the range across your winners, and note where viewers drop off. A range from your own winners tells you what a good hook looks like for your account.
items.why: A range from winners tells you what a good hook looks like for your account.

items.title: Feed hook and drop-off data into the learning bank
items.text: Pull hook rate and drop-off for winning videos into a creative learning bank and use them when writing the next brief. It turns results into rules for new briefs.
items.why: It turns results into rules for the next brief.

items.title: Run tasks side by side, not in a chain
items.text: Find the steps in your process that don't depend on each other and run them at the same time instead of one after another. One long chain takes ages; parallel independent steps save hours.
items.why: One long chain of steps takes ages. Doing independent steps together saves hours.
items.when: any multi-step workflow or AI pipeline

items.title: Put a unique ID in every ad name
items.text: Give every ad a readable name ending in a short unique code, and keep scripts and creative notes in a separate sheet keyed to that code. The ad platform's data does not hold your creative details, so the code is how you join them.
items.why: Meta's data does not hold your creative details, so the code is how you join them.
items.when: naming ads for reporting and creative analysis

items.title: Map tasks, not functions, then rank them
items.text: List every small task in each department, rank them by impact, confidence and ease, and automate the top ones first. A task is the smallest unit of the business, so it is easier to automate than a whole function like media buying.
items.why: A task is the smallest unit of the business, so it is easier to automate than a big job like media buying.

items.title: Treat a data mismatch as an alert
items.text: When two systems should match 100%, treat any order that doesn't match as an alert and check those orders daily. A mismatch often means a double-fulfilled or wrong order.
items.why: A mismatch often means a double fulfilled or wrong order.

items.title: Feed winners back into a learning store
items.text: Connect ad results to your system so it knows which ads won, and save only winners with their {avatar} and angle so the next scripts learn from them. The next batch only improves if wins and losses are recorded.
items.why: The next batch gets better only if wins and losses are recorded.
items.when: AI-assisted creative production with a feedback loop

items.title: Hire young clippers to find formats
items.text: Pay a few heavy TikTok users (teenagers) to hunt for new formats for {brand} and post them organically, then ask what keywords they search. They find formats you would miss, and their search habits can be automated later.
items.why: They find formats you would miss, and their search habits can be automated later.
items.when: organic format discovery on short-form video

items.title: Ask your format finders how they search
items.text: Ask whoever finds formats exactly which keywords they type into TikTok and write them down so an agent can scrape the same way. You can only automate a search you understand first.
items.why: You can only automate a search you understand first.

items.title: Watch a competitor ad climb the rankings
items.text: Record a competitor's ad library several times a day and note which ad moves up the order; a fast climb means it is taking spend, so study its {avatar} and angle. One ad in a batch usually carries the winner, and rank speed shows it early.
items.why: One ad in a batch usually carries the winner, and rank speed shows it early.

items.title: Skip the photographer for packshots
items.text: Generate {hero product} packshots with an AI image tool instead of booking a photographer. It is faster and cheaper.
items.why: It is faster and cheaper.
items.when: product imagery for ads and pages

items.title: Put an advertorial before the page
items.text: When you launch an offer page, also build a presale advertorial that sits ahead of it. The advertorial warms people before the offer page.
items.why: The advertorial warms people before the offer page.

items.title: Rebuild a winner from its parts
items.text: Break a winning ad into characters, scenes, elements and transcript, drop new sub-{avatar} details into that same framework, and generate the new scenes. The winning structure is kept and only the person changes.
items.why: The structure that won is kept, and only the person changes.
items.when: making variations of a proven ad

items.title: Pay clippers per view
items.text: Pay organic {creator}s (clippers) a small fee per view threshold, for example per 2,000 views. Cost stays tied to reach, so you only pay for videos that get seen and the test stays cheap.
items.why: You only pay for videos that get seen, so the test stays cheap.

items.title: Send organic traffic to the site and watch Meta CPA
items.text: Send TikTok viewers to the website and check whether your Meta CPA drops as more warm people arrive. In one case Meta CPA came down because of TikTok traffic, so organic reach on one platform can lower paid costs on another.
items.why: TikTok reach can lower paid costs on another platform.
items.when: running organic TikTok alongside Meta paid

items.title: Test a new avatar on organic first
items.text: Post content aimed at a new {avatar} (for example a younger customer) in new formats on organic and see whether views jump; if the old avatar's posts stall, drop them. Organic views show interest before you spend on ads.
items.why: Organic views show interest before you spend on ads.

items.title: Organic views also validate the market
items.text: Count what organic posts cost per view; a small budget buying huge reach is also market proof. In one case about $2,000 bought 2.7 million views, validating the idea for a fraction of an ad test.
items.why: It gives market proof for a fraction of an ad test.
items.when: validating an idea or avatar before paid spend

items.title: Animate a character from a winning format
items.text: Take the character from a format winning on Instagram, turn it into a character you can animate with AI, and reuse it across videos. The brand's best-performing format started this way.
items.why: Our best performing format started this way.
items.when: AI video production from proven organic formats

items.title: Send products to creators on Instagram
items.text: Have a content manager find real {creator}s in your customers' age group on Instagram and YouTube and send them products. They post back, which grows followers and gives real content.
items.why: They post back, which grows followers and gives real content.

items.title: Follow formats from TikTok to Instagram to Facebook
items.text: Look for formats on TikTok first and expect the same ones to reach Instagram and then Facebook, where you test them. Older customers are on every platform, so a format that wins early can be reused later.
items.why: Older customers are on every platform, so a format that wins early can be reused later.
items.when: format discovery for brands with older customers

items.title: Keep a human at the taste check
items.text: Have a person check every AI image and clip before it ships; never send AI output through on its own. Details like faces and body movement need a human eye at the taste level.
items.why: Details like faces and body movement need a human eye.

items.title: Teach the AI from the clips a reviewer approves
items.text: When a reviewer rejects an AI clip for a small detail (an earring, a movement), run the approved clip through an AI video analyzer and write rules so later generations avoid the issue. The AI can't see taste on its own, so you capture it as written rules.
items.why: The AI cannot see taste on its own, so you capture it as written rules.
items.when: AI video production with human review

items.title: Build a language skill from real source text
items.text: Collect real customer words from Reddit, TikTok videos and slideshows and build one shared language skill from them, updated per {avatar}. Copy sounds real when it uses the words people actually use.
items.why: Copy sounds real when it uses the words people actually use.

items.title: Use one copy skill across every format
items.text: Use one copywriting skill for email, static and video, fed by the same research. One shared voice avoids drift between formats.
items.why: One shared voice avoids drift between formats.

items.title: Change only the content first
items.text: When sales are weak, keep the page and {offer} the same and change only the videos as your first test. It isolates what content alone can do; in one case new AI videos were the only thing that drove views and sales.
items.why: It isolates what the content alone can do.

items.title: Build the funnel from your best creative
items.text: Build the funnel by turning your top videos straight into the page, without over-designing it. People already liked the content, so a page that matches it converts.
items.why: People already liked the content, so a page that matches it converts.
items.when: building landing pages after creative wins

items.title: Have AI break down every swiped video
items.text: Save a competitor video and ask AI to list its scenes, transcript, settings and elements, then reread the output until you understand why it works before recreating it. The breakdown is what you rebuild from.
items.why: The breakdown is what you rebuild from.

items.title: Turn a health organic video into an ad
items.text: Look at what the {avatar} watches organically in the category (in one case older women watching health and wellness videos) and rebuild that as an ad. In that case the new format outperformed the brand's old VSL ads.
items.why: The new format outperformed the brand's old VSL ads.

items.title: Research adjacent categories for formats
items.text: Search TikTok and YouTube for adjacent concepts to your product (for a tea: kidney tea, detox tea) and save and break down the formats people use. Related niches reveal formats before they reach yours.
items.why: Related niches reveal formats before they reach yours.

items.title: Pick the biggest category and build the machine there
items.text: Pick the biggest category your products serve and build the content machine around it first, adding other products afterward. One machine on a proven need beats several half-built ones.
items.why: One machine on a proven need beats several half-built ones.
items.when: multi-product brand deciding where to focus

items.title: Make mobile and tablet designs too
items.text: When handing over a desktop design, add mobile and tablet versions too. It builds better than responsive scaling alone.
items.why: It builds better than responsive scaling alone.

items.title: Write the funnel spec before building
items.text: Write the funnel spec (entry page, upsells, prices, coupons) as a file before anything is built. An agent without a spec puts things in the wrong place.
items.why: An agent without a spec puts things in the wrong place.

items.title: Check every pixel fires before the ads
items.text: Before running ads, click through the funnel with a debugger or pixel helper to confirm every event fires, and fix what doesn't. Pixel connection takes the most time and breaks quietly.
items.why: Connecting pixels takes the most time and breaks quietly.
items.when: before launching paid traffic to a funnel

items.title: Build the pre-sell and offer page after a breakout
items.text: Once one format breaks out, build a pre-sell page and then the offer page in a string behind it, without redoing the whole funnel. One proven format pulls the pages with it.
items.why: One proven format pulls the pages with it.
items.when: after a creative format breaks out

items.title: Keep the avatar, change how you speak to them
items.text: Keep the same {avatar}, write a fresh angle, and match the page to that angle. It is the cheapest way to get new ads.
items.why: It is the cheapest way to get new ads.

items.title: Put the questions into the top of the page
items.text: If shoppers have product questions, move a short FAQ accordion up into the top section of the page and order it by what they ask most. Answering questions fast got people to check out.
items.why: Answering questions fast got people to check out.
items.when: landing pages with frequent shopper questions

items.title: Cut the page down to core ingredients
items.text: Strip the page down to the core ingredients of {hero product} and what each one does, removing extra claims. People don't read, so fewer, clearer points land.
items.why: People do not read, so fewer, clearer points land.

items.title: Test a smaller bundle ladder
items.text: Test a smaller bundle ladder (one to three units instead of one to six) and check revenue per visitor and CPA. In one test fewer units dropped CPA a lot and satisfied customers.
items.why: Fewer units dropped CPA and satisfied customers.

items.title: Test a quick version of the page first
items.text: Deploy a fast version of the funnel page first, get a week of data, then have the designer build the real one. You learn whether the angle works before spending design time.
items.why: You learn whether the angle works before spending design time.

items.title: Vary pre-sell pages, keep one checkout
items.text: Send clicks to many pre-sell and landing pages that all feed the same checkout, so nothing is rewired per test. Checkout is the hard part, so you reuse it.
items.why: Checkout is the hard part, so you reuse it.

items.title: Analyze and document your own workflow
items.text: Write down how a task is done, review what worked, change it, and keep the notes in one place. A system only improves if it records what you did.
items.why: A system only improves if it records what you did.

items.title: Let the AI write the brief, then other tools make it
items.text: Have an AI writer produce a detailed brief per image or video, then send the image part to an image model and the video part to a video model. Each tool gets exact instructions in its own format.
items.why: Each tool gets exact instructions in its own format.

items.title: Never accept an AI merge without checking
items.text: Never accept an AI merge of records without asking why; two fulfillment packages can be a reship, not a duplicate. Auto-merging hides real problems.
items.why: Auto-merging hides real problems.
items.when: AI working on order or customer data

items.title: Funnels are built as Next Commerce campaigns from Figma
items.text: Go from the Figma design straight into a funnel campaign on your commerce platform using its published skills, so a finished design can publish without a rebuild. It removes the hand-off between design and a live funnel.
items.why: It removes the hand-off between design and a live funnel.
items.when: brands whose commerce platform builds funnels from designs

items.title: Keep hero images as a human taste call
items.text: Let a person choose and generate hero and lifestyle images; use AI for structure, tokens and CSS, not for the taste calls. Image choice is taste, not something AI does directly.
items.when: page and email design with AI

items.title: Turn past pages and emails into baseline wireframes
items.text: Convert past emails and landing pages into plain baseline wireframes; the designer picks sections she likes and the brand design tokens are applied on top. Finished pre-generated designs block the designer's creativity; a basic wireframe lets her take it from there.
items.why: Pre-generated finished designs block the designer's creativity; a basic wireframe lets her take it from there.
items.when: design workflows with AI and a human designer

items.title: Hand off between sessions with a handoff file
items.text: At the end of each session write a handoff file in the project folder so anyone can open it, get the summary and carry on without a meeting or recorded video. Questions get answered from the file.
items.why: Questions get answered from the file, so people skip the meeting.

items.title: Do not build 100 agents for e-commerce
items.text: Don't build 100 agents for e-commerce; most of the work is manual decision support, so build only the few tools you need, tailored to how the team works. Overbuilt agent setups add complexity without helping.
items.why: Overbuilt agent setups add complexity without helping the work.
items.when: planning AI tooling for a DTC team

items.title: Source the swipe first, format second
items.text: Before building a swipe workflow, decide where the link comes from (ad library, TikTok, Instagram); once you have a link, video, photo and page all look the same to the tools. The source is the hard part.
items.why: The source is the hard part; every format becomes one link on the back end.

items.title: Use Apify to pull TikTok videos and ad-library swipes
items.text: Don't hand-build a TikTok or ad-library downloader; use an off-the-shelf scraper service to pull links and download videos, then feed them into the chain. In one case it saved a teammate about a day.
items.why: It saves a teammate about a day of working out how to get a video into Claude.

items.title: Store raw daily data, not weekly exports
items.text: Pull the lowest-level data every day into one database and build views from it, instead of exporting a fixed weekly range each time. Every report can be rebuilt from raw data and nothing is locked into one dashboard.
items.why: Every report can be rebuilt from the raw data, and nothing is locked into one dashboard.

items.title: Keep skills separate from data and insight
items.text: Build many small skills and keep data and insight in separate layers, so one tool can serve many uses. If everything lives in one script, changing anything later is risky.
items.why: If everything lives in one script, changing anything later is risky.

items.title: Put the guardrails in the Claude files
items.text: Write basic safety rules into the AI project instruction files so non-technical teammates are covered without anyone managing them. Rules in a handbook go unread; rules in the files apply automatically.
items.why: Rules in a handbook go unread; rules in the files are applied automatically.

items.title: Sketch concepts by hand before using Claude
items.text: Sketch concepts and angles by hand first, then give the sketch to the AI to build on. Starting cold in the AI produces lots of output with no real direction.
items.why: Starting in Claude cold produces lots of output with no real direction behind it.
items.when: creative and strategy work with AI

items.title: Expect a tiny yield from creator outreach
items.text: Plan to message hundreds of {creator}s and expect a small share to agree; in one round 304 were contacted and 38 got product. Only a few become real partners, so outreach volume must be high.
items.why: Only a few of those become real partners, so volume of outreach has to be high.

items.title: Write each creator's brief to fit how she talks
items.text: Open the {creator}'s page, rank her videos by organic performance, and write the brief to match how she speaks and what she talks about, not one script for everyone. A video fails when it doesn't match how that creator delivers her own message.
items.why: A video fails when it does not match how that creator delivers her own message.

items.title: Aim for 10 creators a month and learn them
items.text: Find about 10 {creator}s to work with each month, learn their content style, and write briefs just for them. Winners come from briefs built around one person's style.
items.why: Winners come from briefs built around one person's style.

items.title: Run a weak organic video as an ad anyway
items.text: Even if a {creator}'s first organic post gets only about 1,000 views, put the video into the ad account to see if it takes spend. Organic views don't predict ad performance.
items.why: Organic views do not predict how it performs as an ad.

items.title: Judge by blended efficiency, not one platform
items.text: Judge marketing by the store's overall marketing efficiency ratio, not each platform's own reported return; keep feeding in assets and set spend by overall margin. A single platform can look weak while the whole store runs far better.
items.why: A single platform can look weak while the whole store runs far better.

items.title: Put many ads in and watch what gets spend
items.text: Load as many ads as possible into the account and watch which videos get spend, without worrying about ad volume or whether any one works. Spend is the signal of which content is a winner.
items.why: Spend is the signal of which content is a winner.
items.when: Meta-style paid social where the algorithm allocates spend

items.title: The customer and angles stay; formats change
items.text: Keep the same {avatar} and angles and refresh the format every few months; test in order sub-avatars, then angles, then formats. Formats are what wear out, and a newer one is always coming up behind.
items.why: A format that stops working has a newer one coming up behind it.

items.title: Save viral videos and run them through Gemini
items.text: Save and download videos that stand out in your market, have an AI video model analyze the character, scenes, script and transcript, then have an AI writer remake it for {brand}. It turns a viral organic format into a script and scene list for {hero product}.
items.why: It turns a viral organic format into a script and scene list for your product.

items.title: Plan angles around the season
items.text: Map when the core desire peaks in each market (for example summer in the US, then summer in Australia) and in the off season test a related desire (for self-tanners, even skin tone). You keep acquiring customers during slow periods.
items.why: You keep acquiring customers during slow periods.
items.when: seasonal products sold in several markets

items.title: Hand the AI your avatar and language with the breakdown
items.text: Give the AI the video breakdown, your {avatar} and your customer language, and tell it to rewrite the video for that avatar. The script comes out in your customer's voice.
items.why: The script comes out in your customer's voice.

items.title: Start AI people from a real photo
items.text: Start AI-generated people from a real photo (from Instagram or Pinterest) attached as a reference and change one thing, like what she holds, rather than generating from scratch. Starting from a real picture keeps the person looking real.
items.why: Starting from a real picture keeps the person looking real.

items.title: Break a video into frames before remaking it
items.text: Have AI separate every scene and frame of a swiped video, rework the frames for {brand}, generate each as an image to check, then build the video. You catch bad frames before paying for the whole video.
items.why: You catch bad frames before paying for the whole video.

items.title: Research a topic by searching it on TikTok
items.text: Search the plain topic on TikTok, then add the specific audience (for example 'bloating', then 'bloating women 40'), read what they say and save it into a research document. The document teaches the AI exactly how your customer talks.
items.why: The research document teaches the AI exactly how your customer talks.

items.title: Ask your top 100 customers for interviews
items.text: Export your top 100 customers by spend from your store, find who they are, get them on a call, and have AI pull their desires from the recording. Real customer words give angles you cannot guess.
items.why: Real customer words give you angles you cannot guess.
items.when: customer research for an existing brand

items.title: Low order value is fine if you are profitable
items.text: A pain-relief angle may sell only one pack and lower average order value; if it is profitable, keep it and run other angles alongside for volume. The painkiller buyer wants one fix, so volume and profit matter more than order size.
items.why: The painkiller buyer wants one fix, so volume and profit matter more than order size.

items.title: Test angles one at a time
items.text: Split angles that don't share a promise into separate tests, then scale the one that works. Mixing angles overcomplicates the ad and hides what works.
items.why: Mixing angles makes the ad overcomplicated and hides what works.

items.title: Look at profit, then reinvest
items.text: Judge the account on profit, not ROAS or revenue, and reinvest profit into scaling. In one case a marketer at 1.2 ROAS with high acquisition cost was losing money without noticing.
items.why: A marketer with 1.2 ROAS and high acquisition cost was losing money without noticing.

items.title: Let data set the avatar, not your guess
items.text: Fill out the {avatar} sheet from objective data before making creative, not from your guess. In one skincare example buyers were 45 to 65 and on Instagram, not 75 and offline.
items.why: Wrong avatar guesses waste every ad built on them.

items.title: An offer is price plus a transformation
items.text: Write the {offer} as product and price plus the transformation, tied to the {avatar}'s core desire. A price-only offer misses what the buyer actually wants.
items.why: A price-only offer misses what the buyer actually wants.

items.title: Split the core avatar into sub-avatars by problem
items.text: Under one core {avatar}, list sub-avatars by their specific problem (in one shaving example: ingrown hairs vs. razor bumps vs. dark marks after shaving). Each sub-avatar gets its own headline and angle, so one avatar yields many ads.
items.why: Each sub-avatar gets its own headline and angle, so one avatar yields many ads.

items.title: Run research in order and customer language last
items.text: Run research in order: {avatar} sheet, then brand resonance (product, mechanism, core desires), then the customer language sheet last. Each builds on the one before, and the language bank is what you inject into swipes.
items.why: Each sheet builds on the one before; the language bank is what you inject into swipes.

items.title: Pull ad comments in bulk for customer voice
items.text: Collect the comments under your top ads in bulk (by a VA or a scraper) into one CSV before trying to understand the customer. Real customer words are the raw material for avatars and hooks, and you can't read them one at a time.
items.why: Real customer words are the raw material for avatars and hooks; you cannot read them one at a time.

items.title: Start each session in the right folder
items.text: Pick the right project folder before starting an AI session; a chat started at the wrong level pulls in context you didn't expect. Wrong context gives wrong answers.
items.why: Wrong context gives wrong answers.

items.title: Keep the avatar fixed, track the format they watch
items.text: The core {avatar}'s desires, pain points and angles stay fixed; what changes is the format they watch, so research the current format instead of re-researching the avatar. Formats like slideshows appear and fade.
items.why: Re-researching the avatar wastes time; formats like slideshows appear and fade.

items.title: Test small, then pull back when CPA climbs
items.text: Start tests at $50 to $100 a day, scale hard when one ad breaks out, and cut spend when CPA starts to rise. In one case a brand hit $2k a day within a week and was pulled back to about $1,100 because CPA throttled.
items.why: Fast spend past what CPA allows loses the profit.

items.title: Do not copy competitor ads one-for-one
items.text: Study competitors' ads but don't rebuild them one-for-one; take the structure and inject your own message. A straight copy can convert early but won't scale.
items.why: A straight copy can convert early but does not scale.

items.title: Ship only one or two creatives a week until one hits
items.text: Ship only a few creative batches a week until one hits, find the core message, then hand the winner to {creator}s to scale. Quality and learning beat volume before there is a winner.
items.why: Quality and learning beat volume before there is a winner.
items.when: early-stage brand without a winning ad

items.title: One pod per brand
items.text: Give each brand its own small pod and push everything AI can do away from people. Fewer hand-offs and fewer people are needed per brand.
items.why: Fewer hand-offs and fewer people needed per brand.

items.title: Judge ads against break-even, not spend
items.text: Know the break-even return before looking at ad results. In one example break-even was 1.4 ROAS and the brand ran at 2.5 overall; spend alone says nothing about profit.
items.why: Spend alone says nothing about profit.

items.title: When CPA is bad, distill the message deeper
items.text: If CPA is far over target, stop relaunching old ads; write out how to stand out from what's already running and sharpen the message. The old message wasn't the one that broke through.
items.why: The old message was not the one that broke through.
items.when: paid social with CPA well over target

items.title: Prove one offer and one message on cold traffic first
items.text: Validate one core {offer} with one core message on cold traffic before building upsells and other products. Once the front end is profitable, the rest has something to stand on.
items.why: Once the front end is profitable, the rest has something to stand on.
items.when: new brand or new product launch

items.title: Make every data source joinable by an ID
items.text: When adding a new data source, first check which ID (order, avatar, ticket) lets you join it to the rest. Good data with no shared ID can't be connected to anything.
items.why: Good data with no shared ID cannot be connected to anything else.

items.title: Write listicle copy by breaking down another listicle
items.text: Write listicle copy by breaking down a competitor's listicle, injecting your own message and story, and basing it on your winning video. The structure is proven; the message is yours.
items.why: The structure is proven; the message is ours.

items.title: Use an AI mockup, then a designer for the final page
items.text: Generate the page mockup section by section with an AI tool, then hand it to the designer to build the real front end. AI gets the layout fast; the designer adds the finish.
items.why: AI gets the layout fast; the designer adds the finish.

items.title: Move one skill at a time into the shared system
items.text: Move one skill at a time into a shared system, starting with the single most useful one the {founder} already runs by hand, then build the context it needs. Doing one end to end shows what context and storage the next needs.
items.why: Doing one end to end shows what context and storage the next one needs.
items.when: moving personal AI workflows into team systems

items.title: Template the page once, then make sub-avatar versions
items.text: Build the core {avatar}'s page as a template, then have AI produce versions with a different headline or hero image per sub-avatar. Changing one slot is faster and safer than rebuilding.
items.why: Changing one slot is faster and safer than rebuilding.

items.title: Split email into concept, copy and research steps
items.text: Split email creation into separate research, concept and copy steps, driven by the marketing calendar and customer language. Each step is easy to check and automate.
items.why: Each step is easy to check and to automate.

items.title: Not every step needs an agent
items.text: Climb from manual to prompt to skill to agent only when needed; a skill or standing rule is usually simpler than an agent. Most infrastructure needs no AI, and agents add complexity.
items.why: Most infrastructure needs no AI, and agents add complexity.
items.when: deciding how to automate a step

items.title: Convert designs to Figma files so campaign setup can run
items.text: Get the designer's page designs into proper Figma design files so campaign-setup skills can read and deploy straight from them. The skills need a readable design file, not a screenshot.
items.why: The skills need a design file they can read, not a screenshot.

items.title: Turn designer Figma files into wireframes with Claude Design
items.text: Have the designer upload her Figma email files to an AI design tool to get wireframes, then paste in the copy and generate images. It speeds her up without needing coding tools or the repo.
items.why: It speeds the designer up without her needing Claude Code or the repo.
items.when: email design with a non-technical designer

items.title: Have AI pull Pinterest images for the designer
items.text: Have the email concept step scrape Pinterest for the theme and hand the designer about 10 matching images to build from. Designers use inspiration; this gives better inspiration faster without replacing their work.
items.why: Designers do use inspiration; this gives them better inspiration faster, without replacing their work.

items.title: Start with plain statics on the core desire
items.text: For a new brand, start with plain statics: image plus headline on the core desire, with the {avatar} visible. It's the fastest way to find out whether the core message works.
items.why: It is the fastest way to find out whether the core message works.

items.title: Email buyers and ask for a review
items.text: Email early customers directly and ask them to leave a review. It built the first hundreds of reviews without paying for an app.
items.why: It built the first hundreds of reviews without paying for an app.

items.title: Have a second check loop the work
items.text: Have one agent write the copy and a separate check test it against brand voice and approved words, looping until it passes. A separate check catches off-brand work before a person sees it.
items.why: A separate check catches off-brand work before a person sees it.

items.title: Use an AI check loop to make sales pages bug-free
items.text: Run an AI checklist loop on a new sales page to catch bugs (pixels firing, load speed, CTA working), not to make it pretty. Checklist items are mechanical, so AI is reliable at them.
items.why: The checklist items are mechanical, so AI is reliable at them.

items.title: Check that pixels fire and speed holds
items.text: In a page QC pass, check in the code that pixels fire and page load speed hasn't slipped. A page that looks fine can still lose tracking or speed.
items.why: A page that looks fine can still lose tracking or speed.
items.when: page QA before or after changes

items.title: Break down five swipes, inject language, review the transcript
items.text: Run each swipe (in one batch, five) through the video breakdown, inject customer language, and read the transcript to make sure it sounds clean before storyboarding. Reading the transcript catches bad lines before any pictures are made.
items.why: Reading the transcript catches bad lines before any pictures are made.

items.title: Try written instructions before building something smart
items.text: Before building an agent, try written instructions: a skill, a rule or a plain integration; don't create agents you might need someday. Generating an agent takes minutes, so there's no need to build early.
