items.why: Generating an agent takes minutes, so there is no need to build them early.

items.title: Describe the need, not today's tool
items.text: Write each task as what you are trying to achieve, with no tool named, and record separately how it's done today. If a tool is written in, the AI assumes the tool is settled.
items.why: If a tool is written in, Claude will assume the tool is settled.

items.title: Find the one mechanism that makes the product different
items.text: Sit down with the numbers and {offer} and name the one mechanism that makes {hero product} work (for a hair line, hair porosity), then aim ads at it. A clear mechanism is the angle that sets the product apart.
items.why: A clear mechanism is the angle that sets the product apart.

items.title: Write tasks as who needs what and why
items.text: Boil each workflow step down to who you are, what you need and why, plus a done-when line. It strips out tool bias and shows the real problem.
items.why: It strips out tool bias and shows the real problem to solve.

items.title: Solve the hardest step first
items.text: Out of all the steps, pick the hardest one and solve only that first; for video, it's turning a video into usable text. Storage and wiring are easy; analysis is where the time goes.
items.why: Storage and wiring are easy; the video analysis is where the time goes.

items.title: Build each step so any brand can use it
items.text: Build each step (like video breakdown) to be general, taking brand and format as inputs, so it serves any similar job. One step serves many uses.
items.why: One step serves many uses.

items.title: Pick a creator's top 10 posts by views
items.text: For each {creator}, pick their 10 most popular posts, measured by views, and download them for breakdown. A clear rule keeps the choice the same every time.
items.why: A clear rule keeps the choice the same each time.

items.title: Store the video first, then analyze
items.text: Download the video and store it (for example in a shared drive) before running AI analysis on it. It closes an unlisted gap and makes the analysis repeatable.
items.why: It was a gap nobody had listed, and it makes the analysis repeatable.

items.title: Tell Claude to gut-check you
items.text: Explicitly tell the AI to gut-check your plan; otherwise it assumes you want exactly what it proposes. Without a check it can run off in wrong directions.
items.why: It can run off in wrong directions without a check.

items.title: Add advisors to gut-check big decisions
items.text: Create separate technical, AI and business advisor agents, ask them the same hard question, and have your assistant summarize their memos. The AI agrees with you unless asked to challenge, and separate advisors give useful conflicting advice.
items.why: Claude only agrees with you unless you ask it to challenge you.
items.when: big decisions made with AI help

items.title: Use JSON for machines, Markdown for Claude
items.text: Use Markdown for context people edit, and add a JSON file only when automation needs to read it or store state. Extra JSON is wasted until an automation layer needs it.
items.why: Extra JSON files are wasted until an automation layer needs them.

items.title: Package the process as a helper for editors
items.text: Package your production process into an AI helper and give it to the {editor}s to use. In one case creative output rose and cost per purchase dropped from about $60 to $45.
items.why: The team stops rebuilding the process each time.
items.when: teams of editors producing AI creative

items.title: Give the AI creators a character guide
items.text: Write a character guide from what the {founder} approved and use it on every AI-generated video. It keeps the character consistent across videos.
items.why: It keeps the character consistent across all videos.

items.title: Break down content to its message and carrier
items.text: For any video, image or page, record what the message is, how it's conveyed, and who carries it, so it could be rebuilt in another language or format. The goal is a breakdown that transfers across formats.
items.why: The goal is a breakdown that transfers across formats.

items.title: Run an imperfect first prompt on many examples
items.text: Write a simple, clear extraction prompt and run it across many accounts and formats, then read the outputs and adjust, accepting the first prompt isn't perfect. The outputs show what the system needs.
items.why: The outputs show what the system needs.

items.title: The only input is an inspiration link
items.text: Make the only input to the production helper an inspiration link (for example a viral TikTok); it breaks it down and injects the {offer} and {hero product}, regardless of the swipe's original brand or avatar. {editor}s only need the link.
items.why: The editors only need the link; the system does the rest.

items.title: Write the copy after the creative
items.text: Pick the image or video first, reverse-engineer it, then write the ad copy to match the format. The most congruent copy follows the creative.
items.why: The most congruent copy follows the creative.

items.title: Keep making the first video and making variations as separate jobs
items.text: Treat making the first video and making variations after it as two separate workflows with their own steps. Mixed steps make it hard to fix either.
items.why: Mixed steps make it hard to fix either.

items.title: Keep one copy of the repo and clone it by command line
items.text: Keep one copy of each code repo, cloned by command line into one projects folder, never in two places by hand. Two copies drift apart and break paths.
items.why: Two copies drift apart and break paths.

items.title: Do not mix cloud and local Claude
items.text: Pick local or cloud AI sessions for a given piece of work and don't mix them; local context isn't visible to cloud sessions. The two don't share files.
items.why: The two do not share files.

items.title: Rebuild voice of customer from support tickets
items.text: Analyze customer support tickets and rebuild the voice of customer from them. Tickets are real customer words at scale.
items.why: Tickets are real customer words at scale.

items.title: Add a checklist step that checks the teardown output
items.text: After the master teardown prompt, add a checklist step that confirms every required part is present. It catches gaps before the next stage uses them.
items.why: It catches gaps before the next stage uses them.

items.title: Test the prompt on five more influencers by hand
items.text: When a teardown prompt looks good, run it by hand on five other {creator}s before automating anything. One account's good result may not carry over.
items.why: One account's good result may not carry over.

items.title: Break down generally, then inject the brand
items.text: Keep the teardown general (format, structure) and add brand injection as a later step. One general breakdown works for all brands.
items.why: One general breakdown works for all brands.

items.title: Give each skill one job
items.text: Give each skill one job; don't make the teardown also decide the format, make a separate step that only identifies format. A skill that does two things can't be tuned.
items.why: A skill that does two things cannot be tuned.

items.title: Prove each step before adding the next
items.text: Test each step until it's good enough before chaining the next. If a long chain gives slop, you can't tell which step failed.
items.why: If a long chain gives slop, you cannot tell which step failed.

items.title: Ask customers why they did or did not buy
items.text: Use feedback forms and post-purchase emails with plain questions: why were you interested, why didn't you buy, what question went unanswered. First-party answers beat guessing from comments.
items.why: First-party answers beat guessing from comments.

items.title: Check at the lowest level you can
items.text: When adding a check, state exactly what is being tested at the lowest level possible, not an agent that 'reviews' in general. A vague check doesn't tell you what to fix.
items.why: A vague check does not tell you what to fix.

items.title: Tune the creator brief to what is winning
items.text: Review weekly which formats are winning and adjust the clipper/{creator} brief to match. Briefs go stale as formats change.
items.why: Briefs go stale as formats change.

items.title: Copy what a winning brand is doing in the same category
items.text: Watch which formats a winning brand in your category runs (in one case handheld product videos with meme-style edits and slideshows) and copy those formats. Tested formats are lower risk.
items.why: Tested formats are lower risk.

items.title: Offer free product to people already posting
items.text: Find TikTok accounts that already post about {brand} or the category, offer free product, then send them the brief. It costs only product, and they already like the topic.
items.why: It costs only product, and they already like the topic.

items.title: Write one brief per format
items.text: Write a separate {creator} brief for each winning format (meme edit, slideshow, UGC). Each format needs different instructions.
items.why: Each format needs different instructions.

items.title: Pay on performance
items.text: Pay clippers and UGC {creator}s on performance. You only pay for results.
items.why: You only pay for results.

items.title: Do not buy followers or old accounts
items.text: Don't buy followers or repurposed accounts; recruit real pages instead. A page built on another niche converts poorly (car-page followers won't buy skincare) and can get banned.
items.why: A page built on another niche converts poorly and can get banned.

items.title: Give creators a way to track sales
items.text: Give each {creator} a TikTok Shop connection or an affiliate link for their bio so sales trace back to them. The closer you attribute revenue, the more you can keep spending.
items.why: The closer you attribute revenue, the more you can spend.

items.title: Recruit pages over 10K followers
items.text: Recruit {creator} pages with more than 10K followers. At that size it's easy for them to connect TikTok Shop.
items.why: It is easy for them to connect TikTok Shop.

items.title: Backfill recent data first
items.text: When backfilling historical ad data into a new table, start from the most recent days and work backward. Old data doesn't match the rest and isn't useful until recent months are in.
items.why: Old data does not match the rest and is not useful until the recent months are in.

items.title: Stop judging by plain ROAS when upsells are excluded
items.text: If post-purchase upsells aren't tracked in the ad platform, look at blended MER alongside ROAS instead of ROAS alone. Plain ROAS leaves out post-first-purchase revenue and makes the account look worse than it is.
items.why: Plain ROAS leaves out money made after the first purchase, so it makes the account look worse than it is.

items.title: One ad that worked is not a rule
items.text: Before copying a pattern the AI found in ad data (for example soft claims beating strong ones), check whether it came from one ad and whether it was already tried; if cheap, test it next to current ads rather than switching everything. One ad's result can be down to timing, spend or what ran alongside it.
items.why: One winning or losing ad can be down to timing, spend or other ads running alongside it.

items.title: Use AI funnel audits for broken-page checks, not taste
items.text: Use AI funnel audits to check whether the page is broken or key parts sit above the fold, with judging criteria you set first; don't act on its opinions about things like guarantee wording. The audit gives generic suggestions real customers don't care about.
items.why: The audit made generic suggestions that real customers do not care about.

items.title: Treat AI findings as patterns, not answers
items.text: When AI points out a pattern in your ad data, write it down as a hypothesis and check it against what you know before changing anything. The AI only sees numbers, not why a spike happened or what else changed that week.
items.why: The AI only sees numbers. It does not know why a spike happened or what else changed that week.

items.title: Automate email first
items.text: Start automation with email, where repeated manual work lives; ads still need someone thinking about each one. Emails can be programmed and scheduled; ads need fresh thinking.
items.why: Emails can be programmed and scheduled. Ads need fresh thinking each time.

items.title: Plan the season change before the peak ends
items.text: Build the marketing calendar early enough to plan the move from the current seasonal product push to the next one. A peak season turns against you as it ends, so the next push must be ready.
items.why: A peak season turns against you as it ends, so the next push has to be ready.

items.title: Define what a good breakdown looks like, then test on about 10 videos
items.text: Write down what a good breakdown output contains (scenes, scripts, characters, timestamps), then run about 10 different videos through the prompt and check consistency. Without a definition of good, you can't tell if a prompt change helped.
items.why: Without a clear definition of good, you cannot tell if a prompt change helped.

items.title: Automate the manual video-gathering chore
items.text: Automate non-creative chores first, like manually downloading 10 videos from each {creator}. They cost hours each time and creative work waits on them.
items.why: They cost a teammate hours each time and the creative work waits on them.

items.title: Keep brand context out of the breakdown step
items.text: Keep the first video breakdown brand-free and bring in brand details only at the replication step. A breakdown just states what's in the video; deciding how to remake it needs brand context.
items.why: A breakdown just states what is in the video. Deciding how to reverse-engineer it needs your brand's context first.

items.title: Always keep a link back to the original video
items.text: Save the video or a link to it next to every breakdown so you can get back to the source. A script alone loses context, such as the format, when comparing angles later.
items.why: A script alone loses context, such as which format it came from, when you compare two angles later.

items.title: Add a format check to the breakdown
items.text: Have the breakdown name the video's format, since deeper output changes with format, and don't rely on AI to tell AI-made from human-made video. In one test the AI missed that one of two videos was AI-made, and output variation came from format, not the prompt.
items.why: The AI missed that one of two test videos was AI-made. Variation in the output came from format, not from the prompt.

items.title: Build an objection bank from support tickets
items.text: Have AI read support tickets, list the top unique objections, group them, and keep the customer's own wording for each. You get a clean list of real reasons people hesitate, in their words, ready for copy.
items.why: The result is a clean list of the real reasons people hesitate, in their words, ready to use in copy.

items.title: Check new copy against the customer language bank
items.text: Once a customer language bank exists, run every draft brief or script against it to check nothing sounds like something customers would never say. It stops marketer-speak slipping into ads.
items.why: It stops marketer-speak from slipping into ads.

items.title: Split the video teardown into three prompts
items.text: Split the video teardown into three prompts: breakdown, element-level replication, and brand injection, instead of one prompt doing everything. One long prompt gave weaker briefs; splitting gave editor-ready output.
items.why: One long prompt gave weaker briefs. Splitting it gave the output needed before sending to an editor.

items.title: Put brand injection last
items.text: Do brand injection last: combine the replication sheet with {avatar} details, brand resonance, language bank and {hero product} details at the very end. The result sells in the customer's language with a subtle pitch, so ads don't feel like ads.
items.why: The result sells in the customer's language and the sales pitch stays subtle, which makes ads that do not feel like ads.

items.title: Study who your customer follows
items.text: Pick a real person who fits your {avatar}, look at which creators she follows and which of their videos stand out, and use those for format inspiration. It shows what your customer actually watches, not what you guess.
items.why: This shows what your customer actually watches, not what you guess.

items.title: Decide which slide introduces the product
items.text: When remaking a slideshow ad, deliberately decide which slide introduces the method or {hero product} instead of putting it in early. If the product comes in too early, it looks like an ad and people click off.
items.why: If the product comes in too early, the ad looks like an ad and people click off.

items.title: Keep post-purchase upsells out of what Meta sees
items.text: Don't report post-purchase upsell revenue back to Meta; ROAS will look weaker but you still collect the extra money. He believes Meta bids against the first-order price point, so ROAS looks lower while profit is higher.
items.why: He believes Meta bids against the first-order price point, so ROAS looks lower while profit is higher.

items.title: Ask customers what they want before building an offer
items.text: Before building an {offer}, email customers or run a short survey asking what else they'd want with the product. In one case a $1 sample in every box beat extra discounting, because customers don't know your unit economics.
items.why: People do not know your unit economics, so a cheap extra they ask for works better than guessing a bigger discount.

items.title: Do not pick ads by CPA alone
items.text: Don't pick ads by CPA alone; compare purchase volume too. An ad with a lower CPA but two purchases matters less than one with 127.
items.why: Low-volume ads can look cheap but do not move the business.

items.title: Scale a winner by moving it across awareness stages
items.text: Scale a winner by keeping its core message and format and remaking it for the next awareness stage down: more problem-aware, then unaware versions. Once a format works, scaling is changing the traffic temperature, not inventing something new.
items.why: Once a format works, scaling is changing the temperature of the traffic, not inventing something new.

items.title: Creative is the targeting now
items.text: Run everything broad and change the creative context to reach different people, instead of retargeting. He says the algorithm now reads the creative itself as the main targeting signal.
items.why: He says the algorithm now reads the creative itself as the main signal.

items.title: Test the same ad in each placement format
items.text: Make the same ad as video, slideshow, feed image and story image, then compare CPA by format. Each format reaches people who like it, and one can have clearly the lowest CPA (in one case IG-story-style images).
items.why: Different formats go to people who like that format, and one format can have clearly the lowest CPA.

items.title: Gifting is a lower-funnel angle
items.text: Don't use a gift {offer} as the top-of-funnel ad; for cold traffic, speak to desires beyond buying a gift. A gift angle reaches people already ready to buy.
items.why: A gift angle reaches people who are already ready to buy.

items.title: Use the customer's exact words
items.text: Take wording straight from customer interviews; in one case women said 'brown spots', not 'dark spots', and asked why the product smelled like curry. The words you use for {hero product} are often not the words customers use.
items.why: The words you use for your product are often not the words customers use.

items.title: Research problems before thinking about the product
items.text: When you need a new angle, ignore the product for a week and research the problems and experiences people describe (on Reddit, for example). Assumptions about your product's benefits often don't match how customers think.
items.why: Assumptions about your product's benefits often do not match how customers think.

items.title: Keep asking why to reach the core desire
items.text: For each reason a customer gives, keep asking why until you reach the underlying desire. Knowing the real reason people buy means you don't have to make anything up.
items.why: Knowing the real reason people buy means you do not have to make anything up.

items.title: Test one problem at a time
items.text: Test one problem or angle per ad, based on validated research, not several at once. It keeps the test readable.
items.why: It keeps the test readable.

items.title: Agree on prompt version names
items.text: Agree on how prompt versions are named (V3, V4...) so everyone tests the same prompt. Otherwise people test different prompts without knowing.
items.why: Otherwise people test different prompts without knowing.

items.title: Batch-test only after the prompt looks ready
items.text: Get a prompt to a ready-enough state before running it in batches. Mass runs on a weak prompt just multiply the problem.
items.why: Mass runs on a weak prompt just multiply the problem.

items.title: Review test outputs blind
items.text: When rating a prompt's outputs, don't know in advance which prompt produced which output. Blind review removes bias.
items.why: It removes bias.

items.title: Use thumbs up or down plus free text
items.text: For a new prompt, rate each output thumbs up or down and write what's wrong in your own words. The AI can then propose a fix from your note.
items.why: The AI can then propose a fix from your note.

items.title: Let the checks come from real use
items.text: Grow the QC checklist from the actual failures you meet while improving the prompt. It keeps the check relevant.
items.why: It keeps the check relevant.

items.title: Never keep a repo inside a synced drive
items.text: Keep media in the shared drive and code in a separate folder; never put a code repo inside a synced drive. Two syncs fight and break things.
items.why: Two syncs fight and break things.

items.title: Keep each stage independent
items.text: Make each pipeline stage independent: stage one (teardown) shouldn't depend on stage two, and each works on any content and is tuned on its own. You can fix one stage without breaking the others.
items.why: You can fix one stage without breaking the others.

items.title: Watch the swipe first to judge if it is a usable format
items.text: Watch the swipe a few times before reading the teardown and decide whether it even works as a format. If the swipe isn't a fit, teardown quality doesn't matter.
items.why: If the swipe isn't a fit, the teardown quality does not matter.

items.title: Make the teardown detailed enough to reuse
items.text: Make the teardown text detailed enough (props and other specifics) that later stages don't need to re-run video analysis. Re-analysis is slow and costly.
items.why: Re-analysis is slow and costly.

items.title: Review a set of outputs side by side
items.text: Review a batch of outputs side by side, not one per day. Your mood on a given day shifts your judgment.
items.why: Your mood on a given day shifts your judgment.

items.title: Search by competitor domain
items.text: In an ad-intelligence tool, run a URL search on a competitor's domain to see the campaigns they run. It shows exactly what they're running.
items.why: It shows exactly what they run.

items.title: Pick ads running 4 to 10 days
items.text: Filter competitor ads to those running 4 to 10 days to see campaigns past testing. Days one to three are A/B testing; ads kept past day four usually show promise.
items.why: Days one to three are A/B testing; ads kept past day 4 usually show promise.

items.title: Avoid saturated campaigns
items.text: Pick swipe campaigns that are fresh to the market but not yet saturated. Everyone else is already running the saturated ones.
items.why: Everyone else is already running saturated ones.

items.title: Check the new ads column to see who is scaling
items.text: In an ad-intelligence tool's domains view, use the new-ads count to see whether a competitor is scaling up or down. A rising count signals a winner; a falling one, a failing one.
items.why: A rising count signals a winner; a falling one signals a failing one.

items.title: Download a competitor's landing page
items.text: In the ad-intelligence tool, open a competitor ad, go to its landing pages tab and download the page. It gives the page structure to study and strip.
items.why: It gives the page structure to study and strip.

items.title: Start with the top-level filters
items.text: In ad-research tools, use the top-level filters first, then narrow with advanced filters. It removes noise before you refine.
items.why: It removes noise before you refine.

items.title: Stack filters, do not just type the keyword
items.text: In ad-research tools, set industry, vertical and country first, then add keyword rules (such as ads containing both words) rather than just typing a keyword. Plain keyword searches often return nothing and people give up.
items.why: Plain keyword searches often show nothing and people give up.

items.title: Track a page the tool is missing
items.text: If an ad-research tool is missing a good page, add it with the tracker feature so its campaigns get pulled in (in that tool, about an hour). It fills gaps in the data.
items.why: It fills gaps in the data.

items.title: Pull the latest before running a shared tool
items.text: Always update your copy of a shared workspace before running a shared tool, and if it refuses because of unsaved changes, paste the error to the AI and ask what's going on. An out-of-date copy makes tools fail in confusing ways.
items.why: The tool depends on your copy being current; an old copy makes it fail in confusing ways.
items.when: teams sharing AI tooling via a repo

items.title: A new stage has to be wired into the chain
items.text: When you add or insert a stage in a chain, push it and let the system wire it so it takes the previous stage's output; don't just test it by hand and assume it's chained. A stage only runs end to end if it's connected to the one before.
items.why: A stage only runs end to end if it is connected to the stage before it.

items.title: A new prompt version only runs once you approve it
items.text: Save each prompt change as a new version and formally approve it; until approved, the chain keeps running the old version. You can work on new prompts without breaking the live chain.
items.why: This lets you work on new prompts without breaking the live chain.

items.title: Paste confusing errors to Claude
items.text: When you hit an error you don't understand, paste it to the AI and ask what it means, or send it to the team's technical owner. AI reads command and error messages well.
items.why: Claude reads command and error messages well.

items.title: The video link means the social post link
items.text: When the video tool asks for 'the video link', paste the social post link (Instagram etc.), not a cloud-drive link; the tool downloads the video from the post itself.
items.why: The tool downloads the video itself from the post.

items.title: Feed the tool one specific product link
items.text: Give the chain one exact {hero product} link or image folder instead of letting the AI search the web for pictures. It will wander and grab random pictures if nothing says where product images live.
items.why: Claude will wander and grab random pictures if nothing tells it where the product images live.

items.title: Run end to end to find missing context
items.text: Run the whole chain end to end rather than prompting step by step, and treat each failure as a clue to missing context. Step-by-step prompting hides gaps; a full run exposes them.
items.why: Step by step prompting hides gaps; a full run exposes them.

items.title: Hardcode to unblock, and leave a to-do
items.text: If a blank product link or folder blocks a run, hardcode one specific link for now and have the AI log a to-do to make it dynamic later. Otherwise a forgotten hardcode can pull the wrong brand's products into a flow.
items.why: Otherwise a forgotten hardcode can pull the wrong brand's products into a flow.

items.title: Tell Claude when a stage needs a different model
items.text: If a stage must do something other than text (for example send frames to an image model and place the images), tell the AI explicitly that the stage is different. A chain built around text output breaks silently on image work.
items.why: The chain was built around text output, so image work breaks silently.
items.when: AI pipelines mixing text and image steps

items.title: Tell Claude exactly what you are trying to do
items.text: Tell the AI precisely what you're trying to do (what the stage should take in and which model to use) instead of asking why something doesn't work. A vague question sends it off in wild directions.
items.why: A vague question sends it off in wild directions.
items.when: debugging or building with AI assistants

items.title: Set up attribution before choosing the deal
items.text: Set up attribution before choosing the {creator} deal (percentage of sales, weekly payouts, no cap). The tracking determines which deal types are possible.
items.why: The tracking determines which deal type is possible.
items.when: launching a creator or affiliate program

items.title: Create swipes from the best creators
items.text: Once the best {creator}s are known, create swipes from their content to scale the program. Proven content makes better briefs.
items.why: Proven content makes better briefs.

items.title: Let creators link their page so ads run with no approvals
items.text: Have {creator}s connect their account in the creator program so ads can run through their page without asking approval each time. Whitelisting is confusing for creators; this avoids repeat approvals.
items.why: Whitelisting is confusing for creators; this avoids repeat approvals.

items.title: Use individual briefs while testing creators
items.text: While testing {creator}s, give each one an individual brief to see who performs best and how they deliver. You learn which creators work before standardizing.
items.why: You learn which creators perform before standardizing.

items.title: Invite only creators who want the brand
items.text: Invite directly only the {creator}s who replied, not a mass invite of everyone you messaged. You only want people who genuinely want to work with {brand}.
items.why: You only want people who really want to work with the brand.

items.title: AI ads wear out fast: make new concepts of the same winning message
items.text: Once you know your winning pain points and angles, put effort into more executions of the same message, not new messaging. AI creatives fade faster than normal ones, and ideation isn't the bottleneck.
items.why: AI creatives fade faster than normal ones, and ideation is not the bottleneck.
items.when: AI-generated ad creative after finding winners

items.title: Reuse a winning educational format
items.text: Take a proven format (for example 'three things I don't recommend to fix X, and the real fix') and redo it many times. A proven format plus a proven message is the cheapest way to more winners.
items.why: A proven format plus a proven message is the cheapest way to get more winners.

items.title: Break your language bank down by funnel stage
items.text: Keep a customer language bank broken down by funnel stage and pull from the matching part, for example non-customer sources like ad comments for cold ads. Cold audiences respond to language from people who aren't yet customers.
items.why: Cold audiences respond to language from people who are not yet customers.

items.title: Use creators' own comment language in their scripts
items.text: Scrape a {creator}'s top posts and the comments under them and use that language to write the creator's scripts. The script sounds like them and speaks to their audience.
items.why: The script sounds like it comes from them and speaks to their audience.

items.title: Make a burner account and seed its feed
items.text: Create a burner TikTok or Instagram account, seed it with formats you've saved, and let a tool watch the feed and surface similar new ones. It finds new concepts deeper in your niche that you wouldn't scroll to.
items.why: It finds net new concepts deeper in your niche that you would not scroll to.

items.title: Reverse engineer organic formats, then inject your brand
items.text: Take a working organic format, reverse-engineer it, inject {brand}'s insights, and refine the script by hand if needed. Agencies do exactly this; you can do it with prompts.
items.why: Agencies do exactly this; you can do it with prompts.

items.title: Swipe a competitor's whole funnel
items.text: Swipe a competitor's whole funnel: pull their ads by angle, count creatives per angle, and capture the landing page each angle goes to. It shows which angles get the most testing and where they send traffic.
items.why: It shows which angles get the most creative testing and where they send traffic.

items.title: Inject brand tokens into a swiped page
items.text: Save a swiped page's HTML and CSS, swap in your brand tokens, and write new copy from your own research database. You keep the structure that works and make it yours.
items.why: You keep the structure that works and make it yours.

items.title: Say it is a long process to keep subscribers
items.text: If {hero product} takes months to work, say so in the ads (for example 'a six-month process'). Customers who expect it to take time stay on the subscription longer.
items.why: Customers who expect it to take time stay on the subscription longer.

items.title: Test a new product on acquisition first
items.text: Launch a new product to acquisition first and only roll it out fully if the CPA is there. It stops you scaling a product that doesn't convert.
items.why: It stops you from scaling a product that does not convert.

items.title: Favor products with an instant visible effect
items.text: When choosing products and ads, favor a product that can show some instant visible effect on camera. It gives an immediate hook and easy content formats.
items.why: It gives you an immediate hook and easy content formats.

items.title: Brand page: UGC and promos; top-of-funnel on third-party pages
items.text: Keep the brand page for real UGC and promotional statics and videos, and run top-of-funnel story ads from third-party pages. It keeps the brand page credible while still testing wild hooks.
items.why: It keeps the brand page credible while still testing wild hooks.

items.title: Double down on a winning format with new avatars
items.text: Once you find the winning format, double and quadruple down on it with different {avatar}s and executions. The same storyline with different people keeps winning while individual ads fade.
items.why: Same storyline with different people keeps winning while individual ads fade.

items.title: Humans keep the taste; the system learns from feedback
items.text: Start with human review and keep telling the tool what looks good and what doesn't so it learns your taste, with a human still picking formats. AI doesn't know which format to pick unless taught why.
items.why: AI does not know which format to pick unless you teach it why.

items.title: Tell the system why you picked a format
items.text: When you add a format to the system, record why you picked it so the tool can sort formats the way you would. Reasons let it organize and later scout inspiration on its own.
items.why: Reasons are what let it organize and later scout inspiration on its own.

items.title: Reconcile your numbers to the store platform report
items.text: Reconcile your sheet against the commerce platform's report as the source of truth, and adjust for time-zone cutoffs when order counts are off by a few. A small mismatch is usually the date cutoff, not a formula error.
items.why: A mismatch of a few orders is usually the date cutoff, not a formula error.

items.title: Try a new analysis with an MCP and an artifact first
items.text: If no integration exists yet, connect through an MCP, build a quick artifact, and share it with the team if useful; build the full integration after. You find the right numbers faster than by meeting about ten metrics first.
items.why: You find the right numbers faster than by meeting about ten metrics first.

items.title: Write down one definition for each metric
items.text: Agree on named definitions for each metric (for example platform-tracked ROAS vs. blended ROAS) and use the same one everywhere. Two people computing ROAS differently get different numbers.
items.why: Two people computing ROAS differently will end up with different numbers.

items.title: Build metrics daily and add date ranges on top
items.text: Store each metric at the lowest reasonable unit (daily) and calculate 7- or 30-day views on top. Fixing a 7-day view up front loses single-day detail.
items.why: Fixing a 7-day view up front loses the single-day detail.

items.title: Watch the gap between real CPA and Meta CPA
items.text: Build the performance view to show the gap between real CPA from the store and the CPA the ad platform reports. It tells you whether spend is really breaking even.
items.why: It tells you whether your spend is really breaking even.

items.title: Test a new country with a quick weekly test
items.text: Test a new country by duplicating existing ads into it for about a week; if nothing happens, turn it off, otherwise do it properly, and tell the fulfillment partner when it starts. It's cheap validation for deciding where inventory goes.
items.why: It is cheap validation for deciding where inventory should go.

items.title: Run all copy through one language bank by funnel stage
items.text: Write video, email and static copy the same way: pick the funnel stage and have the system pull from the language bank for that stage. One process means every format uses the same research.
items.why: One process means copy for every format uses the same research.

items.title: Build the email calendar from the catalog of emails
items.text: Build the email calendar from brand insight and customer language using the catalog of emails you can actually send, then bring in designs and turn them into HTML. The calendar is built from real options by segment and funnel stage.
items.why: It makes sure the calendar is built from real options, by segment and funnel stage.

items.title: Prompts do not need to be perfect before you wire in the chain
items.text: Wire the chain and components into the system as soon as the overall approach feels right, and keep tuning prompts afterward. The chain and the prompts are separate, so prompts can improve any time.
items.why: The chain and the prompts are separate, so you can improve prompts any time.

items.title: Organic swipe tool that starts a teardown
items.text: Use a swipe tool that finds organic posts and automatically starts the teardown chain. It cuts the manual step between finding a swipe and breaking it down.
items.why: It cuts out the manual step between finding a swipe and breaking it down.

items.title: Get creator feedback on briefs, then run once more
items.text: Send the full briefs to {creator}s, collect their reactions, and feed that into one more run. Creators tell you what is unclear or hard to film.
items.why: Creators tell you what is unclear or hard to film.

items.title: Define one workflow at a time with a few steps
items.text: Pick the highest-priority workflow (such as an email campaign or funnel launch), write its five or so steps, and accept that some stay manual. Workflows get refined by actually shipping work.
items.why: Workflows get refined by actually getting work out.

items.title: Index the footage so editors can pull scenes
items.text: Index the shared footage drive so an {editor} can ask for a scene, get a bin of matching clips, and download them as one sequence. It removes searching through folders by hand.
items.why: It removes searching through folders by hand.
items.when: video teams with large footage libraries

items.title: Add a kill-or-keep step with a reason
items.text: For each concept and its variations, mark kill or keep and type what was wrong; the tool regenerates from the reason. A written reason gives the next generation something specific to fix.
items.why: A written reason gives the next generation something specific to fix.

items.title: Keep fast regeneration direct; use review for QC
items.text: Do quick generation rounds directly in the generation tool or AI assistant, and use a formal review step only when another person must check the finished asset. A tool layer around generation is always slower.
items.why: A tool layer around generation is always slower.

items.title: Review items one by one and save a verdict
items.text: Compare each asset to its reference, mark approved or rejected with a note, and save the verdict for the whole set. A structured review beats a chat message asking someone to take a look.
items.why: A structured review beats a Slack message asking someone to take a look.

items.title: Assign each reviewer a different check
items.text: Give each reviewer a specific check: one technical quality, another copy, and the {founder} the e-commerce details. Everyone knows what to look for.
items.why: Everyone knows what to look for.

items.title: Show the design beside the live page
items.text: When reviewing a built page, put the design reference side by side with the deployed page. The reviewer can compare directly.
items.why: The reviewer can compare directly.

items.title: Keep the editor's queue open
items.text: Keep a queue of work open for a self-starting {editor}. He runs through it without being directed.
items.why: He just runs through it without being directed.

items.title: Index the Drive for consistent product images
items.text: Index the asset drive so images are generated against the real {hero product}, with the slop removed. Ads came out consistent, especially in how the product looks.
items.why: Ads came out consistent, especially in how the product looks.

items.title: Keep creative files in a shared cloud drive the AI can read directly.
items.text: Keep creative files in a shared cloud drive the AI can read directly. It makes indexing and automation easier.
items.why: It makes indexing and automation easier.

items.title: Edit in the repo and share a preview link
items.text: Edit pages in the campaign repo, share the auto-generated preview link, keep iterating, then deploy to main. You see something close to the live page before it goes out.
items.why: You see something close to the real live page before it goes out.

items.title: Mark a design as ready for review before handoff
items.text: Mark clearly when a design is ready for review, and run a quick QC pass before it goes to the dev team. Placeholders and typos reached dev because nobody knew the design wasn't finished.
items.why: Placeholders and typos reached the dev team because nobody knew the design was not finished.

items.title: Duplicate a funnel by swapping the hero and assets
items.text: To make a funnel for another product, copy the existing one, swap the hero and other assets, and preview it. It's far faster than designing a new page.
items.why: It is far faster than designing a new page.

items.title: Ask for a checkout variation from a template
items.text: Ask the AI to duplicate a checkout template (for example a three-step checkout) to get a variation to test. It took about a minute.
items.why: It took about a minute.

items.title: Skip extra QC when the brand owner already reviewed
items.text: If the person who knows {brand} best has already reviewed a finished asset, publish it without extra QC. Another step only slows it down.
items.why: Another step only slows it down.

items.title: Run traffic to a new funnel as soon as it is ready
items.text: Send traffic to a new funnel as soon as it's ready, and test a single-quantity lander to see its effect on conversion. Early traffic gives early conversion data.
items.why: Early traffic gives early conversion data.

items.title: Build quick tools as artifacts before real infrastructure
items.text: Start a new sales or ops tool as a simple artifact fed by existing sheets; don't set up a database or full dashboard until it proves useful. A working tool in days beats a perfect backend in weeks, and the backend can be swapped later.
items.why: A working tool in days beats a perfect backend in weeks, and Claude can swap the backend later.

items.title: Map the human workflow before building the AI version
items.text: Write down who does each step today, then decide which steps AI takes over, telling the AI that humans are real steps, not just checkers. Left alone, AI hands every step to AI and the tool won't fit how the work runs.
items.why: Left alone, Claude hands every step to AI and treats people as an afterthought, so the tool does not fit how the work really runs.

items.title: Put a time estimate and owner on every step
items.text: Note the owner (including outside {editor}s) and time estimate for every workflow step, and send briefs to the slowest people first. Seeing a one-week editor step tells you which briefs to release first and avoids clashes.
items.why: Seeing a one-week editor step lets you decide which briefs to release first and avoid clashes with internal work.

items.title: Settle the offer alongside the design, not after it
items.text: Decide the {offer} and packages at the same time as the page spec, not after the page is built. Designing first and picking the offer later overcomplicates the page and adds rework.
items.why: Designing first and picking the offer later overcomplicates the page and adds rework.

items.title: Build offer pages from the vendor templates, skip Figma
items.text: For a new offer page, start from an existing direct-response template repo, edit it directly and review via the deploy preview link; only go back to Figma if the funnel is truly new. Templates cover most proven DR layouts (he estimates 90%), and a preview link is responsive while Figma isn't.
items.why: The templates already cover most proven direct response layouts, and a preview link is responsive while Figma is not.
items.when: building offer pages with a template library

items.title: Keep all store data in one table so answers match
items.text: Pull orders, 3PL and ad data into one table with fixed definitions, and have the AI and dashboards read only that table. Otherwise the AI reads raw sources fresh each time and can give different revenue numbers for the same question.
items.why: Without one table Claude reads the raw sources fresh each time and can give a different revenue number for the same question.

items.title: Define fulfillment cost once before joining data
items.text: Write one rule for fulfillment cost, order keys and SKU matching before merging data sources, and apply it in the combined table. Each system defines cost differently, and mismatched definitions caused made-up numbers early on.
items.why: Each system defines cost differently, and unmatched definitions caused made-up numbers early on.

items.title: Plan reorders with sold-out date, send-by date and order-by date
items.text: For each SKU, enter lead time and freight time, then compute the sold-out date at the current sales rate and the date the next production order must be placed. It turns a stock sheet into clear deadlines so you stop running out.
items.why: This turns a stock sheet into a clear deadline for each product so you stop running out.

items.title: Back-test your forecast against what happened
items.text: Once or twice a year, back-test past forecasts against actual sales to see how far off the method is before trusting it for peak season. Forecasts worsen further out, and checking shows how much cushion to plan.
items.why: Forecasts get worse the further out they go, and checking them shows how much cushion to plan.

items.title: Add a cash and accrual view for refunds
items.text: Keep a toggle between cash view (refund counted on refund day) and accrual view (refund tied to the original order), and use accrual when judging how an older campaign did. Cash view makes old campaigns look better because late refunds land in later weeks.
items.why: Cash view makes an old campaign look better than it was because late refunds land in later weeks.

items.title: Run one brand per session by pointing at that brand folder
items.text: Open each AI session on the folder of the one brand you're working on, and run two brands in two separate sessions. Separate context stops one brand's language leaking into another's copy.
items.why: Keeping brand context separate stops one brand language leaking into another brand copy.
items.when: operators running several brands with AI

items.title: Save context as small focused files, not one giant file
items.text: Save context as small focused files per job (for example one for copy language) rather than one huge brand file. The longer the context file, the less closely the AI follows it, and long chats compact and lose detail.
items.why: The longer the context file is, the less closely Claude follows it, and long chats compact and lose detail.

items.title: Use a cheaper model for checking and drafting
items.text: Use the strongest model to build, and cheaper models for QC and simple tasks where 90% of the result is enough. Cheaper models get about 90% of the result in about 10% of the time and cost.
items.why: Top models are slow and costly for simple jobs, and cheaper ones finish much faster.

items.title: Pull and push the shared files every day
items.text: Pull the latest shared files before starting and push your changes when finishing, every day, noting any conflicts. Ten days without syncing let small differences drift into big merge conflicts.
items.why: Ten days without syncing let small differences drift apart and caused big merge conflicts.

items.title: Subscriptions cost less than credits
items.text: When AI usage runs out, add a second normal subscription instead of buying extra credits or API usage. Credits cost many times more than the same work on a subscription.
items.why: Credits cost many times more than the same work on a subscription.

items.title: Keep team context in the shared repo, not account projects
items.text: Store team rules and context files in a shared repo so any AI account can read them from the same folder, not in account-bound projects. Account-tied projects lose everything when you switch accounts.
items.why: Cowork projects are tied to one account, so switching accounts loses everything.

items.title: Work in the shared workspace, not the funnel project
items.text: Do creative work in the shared workspace and only open the funnel project when an asset is ready to go into the live funnel. Most work is making assets, which only needs the drive and shared context.
items.why: Most work is making assets, which only needs Drive and the shared brain, not the funnel itself.
items.when: teams with separate creative and funnel repos

items.title: Ask Claude to simplify anything
items.text: When an AI assistant's prompt or explanation is too technical, tell it to simplify and drop the technical terms. You do not need to understand the machinery to use it.
items.why: You do not need to understand the machinery to use it.
items.when: working with AI tools as a non-technical operator

items.title: Drive holds pictures, the repo is the brain
items.text: Keep images and finished assets in shared file storage, and keep briefs, prompts and {brand} context in a central text repository, then point the AI at both. The AI needs the text for brand and product context and the storage for the real files.
items.why: Claude needs the repo for context on brand and product, and Drive for the real files.
items.when: setting up an AI-assisted creative system

items.title: Run a brief by its number
items.text: Give every brief an ID and tell the image tool to execute the brief by that ID; it pulls the brief, makes the images and variations, and checks them. The brief already holds the research, headlines and planned variations, so nothing is rebuilt from scratch.
items.why: The brief already holds the research, headlines and planned variations, so you do not rebuild it from scratch.
items.when: AI image production from a library of numbered briefs

items.title: Your job on a draft is to fix what looks off
items.text: On a machine-made draft, the human's job is to scan the variations, pick the best, and request edits where a product, logo, color or word looks wrong, then package and ship. The machine is fast, but a human eye catches the odd details.
items.why: The machine is fast but your eye catches weird products, bottle caps and wrong colors.
items.when: reviewing AI-generated image variations before shipping

items.title: Edit slop means the prompt is missing something
items.text: If image edits come out differently each time, the edit prompt is not naming the parts of the image. Use an edit prompt that names each element so the model changes only that one.
items.why: Naming each element lets the model change only that one.

items.title: Use the free model and run the chains
items.text: Do the heavy reading and planning with a free or cheap AI model working against your saved context and prompt chains, and pay credits only for the final generations. Most of the work does not need an expensive model.
items.why: Most of the work does not need a costly model.
items.when: AI-assisted creative production with paid generation credits

items.title: Pick the tool for the job
items.text: Use a fast scripted AI assistant for straight batch output, and a slower creative tool that checks quality as it goes when working image by image with creative judgment. Pick the tool for the job.
items.why: Higgsfield checks quality as it goes; Claude gives quick straight output.
items.when: choosing between AI tools for image production

items.title: Run several briefs at once in separate sessions
items.text: Run several briefs at once, one AI session per brief, then come back to review; tell each session where the context and brief live. Each generation takes a while, so waiting on one at a time wastes the day.
items.why: Each generation takes a while, so waiting on one at a time wastes the day.
items.when: AI production of video, image and copy work

items.title: Hero images need a dark side behind text
items.text: On a hero image, check that text and icons stay readable and slightly darken the side that sits behind the text. White text on a bright area is hard to read.
items.why: White text on a bright area is hard to read.
items.when: hero images on landing pages, ads or emails with text overlay

items.title: Tell Claude the exact Drive folder
items.text: When asking an AI for an asset, name the exact folder path (for example the {brand} identity folder) instead of letting it search. A specific path is found fast; a vague request takes a long time.
items.why: A specific path is found fast; a vague request takes a long time.
items.when: AI assistants pulling files from shared storage

items.title: Reuse one cast face across a whole shoot
items.text: Pick one cast member and have the system use that same face for an entire shoot, varying only the scenes and how the person holds the {hero product}. One face across the set keeps it consistent.
items.why: The same face across images keeps the set consistent.
items.when: AI-generated photo shoots and image ad sets

items.title: Stop a runaway revision loop
items.text: If an AI system keeps regenerating, stop it and tell it to deliver what it has; the system should cap revisions and pick the best. Endless retries burn time and credits without better results.
items.why: Endless retries burn time and credits without better results.
items.when: AI generation runs with automatic revision loops

items.title: Fix a wrong logo from the real file
items.text: When a generated image has a wrong logo, have the tool swap in the real logo file (a transparent-background PNG) using the reference image, rather than letting the model draw it. Model-drawn logos are often off.
items.why: Logos drawn by the model are often off; a real transparent file avoids the problem.
items.when: AI image generation with brand logos

items.title: A new session forgets, so re-point it
items.text: Each new AI chat starts blank, so at the start re-point it to the file storage connector and the context repository and name the brief. Otherwise it works without the brief packet.
items.why: Each session starts blank and must reopen the brief packet.
items.when: starting a new AI session on ongoing production work

items.title: Give each cast member an ID tied to an avatar
items.text: Give each generated person an ID linked to an {avatar}, so people, products, angles and headlines can be swapped without redoing the thinking. The system can then match the right person to the right message automatically.
items.why: The system can match the right person to the right message automatically.
items.when: AI-generated cast across many ad variations

items.title: Native ads should not look like ads
items.text: Native ads should not look like ads: make the picture feel like normal life, show the proof subtly (for example the visible problem on the person's skin), and let the copy tell a personal story that leads to it. People scroll past anything that looks like an ad.
items.why: People scroll past anything that looks like an ad.
items.when: native-style image ads on paid social

items.title: Good enough first, then refine
items.text: When replacing funnel images, start with the obvious ones and accept good enough, then refine once you see the process. Perfection on every image delays the page and hides what the process needs.
items.why: Perfection on every image delays the page and hides what the process needs.

items.title: Mix founder-led creative with other creators
items.text: Keep a {founder} story on the page and in some ads, but also run a clean mix of other creative types and {creator}s. The {brand} then keeps earning without depending on one person to make everything.
items.why: The brand then keeps earning without depending on one person to make everything.
items.when: founder-led brands building a creative mix

items.title: Use revenue per day as the scale signal
items.text: Use revenue per day as the scale signal: if a test reaches about $1,000 a day, push it toward $10,000 a day, where it is worth running. A clear daily target tells you when to stop testing and start scaling.
items.why: A clear daily target tells you when to stop testing and start scaling.
items.when: paid media, deciding when a test becomes a scale candidate

items.title: Check against existing files before adding a brand file
items.text: Before adding a new {brand} file to the shared system, check it against existing files early so you do not create a duplicate. Duplicates cause conflicts for quality-check tools that read brand files.
items.why: Duplicates cause conflicts later for QC tools that read brand files.
items.when: adding files to a shared brand knowledge base

items.title: Get it working first, clean up after
items.text: Build it, see if it fits, get it working, then review and clean up afterwards. Cleanup should not stop you getting a working result.
items.why: Cleanup should not stop you getting a working result.

items.title: Keep editing simple; non-marketers cannot judge good
items.text: Keep video edits simple as long as the clips and voiceover make sense, and do not chase every note from people who are not marketers. They do not know what a winning ad looks like, so their notes slow the queue without helping results.
items.why: They do not know what a winning ad looks like, so their notes slow the queue without helping results.
items.when: ad editing and review with non-marketer feedback

items.title: Some slop is fine in ads that sell
items.text: Expect some rough AI moments: reduce them in the production chain, but do not hold a good ad for small flaws. Some of the best-performing ads have rough spots and still work.
items.why: Some of the best performing ads have slop and still work.

items.title: Have a second person run a new tool
items.text: After building a tool, have a second person run it on their own machine before calling it ready. It may depend on setup only the builder has.
items.why: It works for the builder but may depend on setup only the builder has.
items.when: releasing internal tools to a team

items.title: Store characters and copy in the brand repo
items.text: Store each {brand}'s characters, images and copy in its own folder so any session can call a character on demand. The {editor} then no longer has to ask for headlines or character files by message.
items.why: The editor no longer asks for headlines or character files by message.
items.when: multi-brand creative production with recurring characters

items.title: Aim to cut cost per AI video to about 20 dollars
items.text: Aim to cut the cost of each finished AI video to about $20 by generating with the better clips first and fixing issues with prompts in one session. In one case videos had cost about $200 each, which cannot scale, and a good chain cut that sharply.
items.why: Videos that cost about 200 dollars each cannot scale, and a good chain cut that sharply.
items.when: AI video ad production at volume

items.title: Machine outputs wait for a human before becoming brand truth
items.text: Let machine runs write to a separate runs area, and have a person decide what gets promoted into the {brand}'s source-of-truth files. Otherwise the machine decides your source of truth.
items.why: Otherwise the machine decides your source of truth.
items.when: automated systems that produce brand knowledge

items.title: Source ideas from what people actually watch
items.text: Do not invent ads; source ideas from the social posts your {avatar} actually watches, then recreate them for the {brand}. Ideas already getting attention have a higher chance to work.
items.why: Ideas already getting attention have a higher chance to work.
items.when: creative ideation for paid and organic social

items.title: Swipe a viral organic video and inject your brand
items.text: Pick a viral or well-viewed organic video in your niche, run it through a teardown process, and merge your {brand} details into a clean brief draft. You get a proven structure without inventing the idea.
items.why: You get a proven structure without inventing the idea.
items.when: turning organic swipes into ad briefs

items.title: Turn repeated steps into a saved skill
items.text: If you do the same job often, such as downloading a brief, have the AI save it as a reusable skill so it runs on a single request. It removes the same manual steps from every new brief.
items.why: It removes the same manual steps from every new brief.
items.when: repeated manual steps in AI-assisted work

items.title: Build a shared queue anyone can execute
items.text: Put briefs into one shared queue so any {editor} or clipper can pick one up and run it. A shared queue lets more people produce without waiting on one person.
items.why: A shared queue lets more people produce without waiting on one person.
items.when: scaling creative production across a team

items.title: Look at the output in the run folder yourself
items.text: Open a machine run's output yourself and check it is what you expected, because the system tests the code, not your intent. The AI knows the technical steps but not how you plan to use the result.
items.why: The AI knows the technical steps but not how you plan to use it.

items.title: Every machine run starts from a brief
items.text: Every machine run starts from a finished brief: write or pick the brief first, then point the copy tool straight at it rather than making it hunt for a {creator} name. The tool only reads briefs, and the strategy work is what makes its output usable.
items.why: The tool only reads briefs; the strategy work is what makes its output usable.
items.when: running AI copy or creative tools

items.title: Tag the funnel version in the ad name
items.text: Put the new funnel's name in the ad name so results for the updated funnel can be read separately. Without a tag you cannot tell if a CPA change came from the new funnel; in one case the tag showed CPA down $20.
items.why: Without a tag you cannot tell if a CPA change came from the new funnel.
items.when: testing a new funnel behind existing ads

items.title: Ingredient name errors mean a new voiceover
items.text: Check that every ingredient name is spoken correctly before editing a video. A wrong word means regenerating the voiceover and re-editing, which cannot be patched cheaply once the video is edited.
items.why: One mispronounced ingredient cannot be patched cheaply once the video is edited.
items.when: AI voiceover for product videos that name ingredients

items.title: Reuse a sound page by swapping product variables
items.text: When a landing page structure already works, reuse it for a new product by switching out the product details, then re-read it for the core points and research competitors for the new product. The structure is proven; only product-specific proof and competitor angles need new work.
items.why: The structure is proven; only product-specific proof and competitor angles need new work.
items.when: launching a new product's landing page

items.title: Trigger copy runs from new customer objections
items.text: When customer service surfaces a new objection, queue a draft pre-sale page that answers that objection. It turns real customer pushback into tested pages quickly.
items.why: It turns real customer pushback into tested pages quickly.
items.when: ongoing pre-sale and advertorial page production

items.title: Treat generated copy as a B-player first draft
items.text: Treat AI-generated copy as a B-player first draft for pages and offers, then have a person refine it. It saves time on baseline work but is not world-class copy.
items.why: It saves time on baseline work but is not world-class copy.
items.when: AI copywriting for pages and offers

items.title: Load marketing basics and an asset map into the machine
items.text: Load core marketing knowledge such as awareness levels into the AI system, plus an index of where logos, product photos, reviews and before/afters live. It then picks the right assets and writing level without being told each time.
items.why: It then picks the right assets and writing level without being told each time.
items.when: setting up an AI marketing production system

items.title: Preselect the bundle on the offer page
items.text: Show the {offer} as a bundle with the larger multi-unit option preselected (three units in the example) while still letting buyers pick a smaller one. It shifts buyers toward the bigger bundle without removing choice.
items.why: It repositions the offer toward the bigger bundle without removing choice.

items.title: Clone the one-time page for the subscription offer
items.text: Build the subscription offer page by duplicating the finished one-time offer page and changing only the language and what the purchase does. The layout is already proven.
items.why: The layout is already proven, so you only change what differs.
items.when: adding a subscription version of an offer page

items.title: Write a checklist handoff for each new funnel
items.text: For every new funnel, hand off a checklist of the pages and the links they go to, stating clearly which preview links are not live. Anyone can then check or finish it without asking.
items.why: Anyone can then check or finish it without asking.
items.when: building and handing off new funnels

items.title: Make the build pull from the offer bank
items.text: Have page builders read prices and offers from one documented offer bank, and write any missing offer there in the same structure. One source keeps prices and offers consistent across pages.
items.why: One documented source keeps prices and offers consistent across pages.

items.title: Keep quizzes simple, give offer pages more design
items.text: Spend design effort on offer pages and keep quiz questions plain so the quiz does not look complex. Conversion matters more than polish on a quiz.
items.why: Conversion matters more than polish on a quiz.

items.title: Keep a full inventory of funnel images
items.text: Keep a full inventory of every image in a funnel, including small carousel images, so the replacement list is complete. Small images get missed unless you count them all.
items.why: Small images get missed unless you count them all.

items.title: Remake mobile versions when resizing will not work
items.text: Resize images for mobile when it fits, but when an image (such as a product-worn-on-body shot) cannot be resized cleanly, generate a new mobile version. A simple resize can break the picture.
items.why: A simple resize can break the picture.

items.title: Do funnel image swaps before new image ads
items.text: Finish the quick funnel image swaps before working on new image ads for the same launch. The funnel has to be live for the ads to send traffic to.
items.why: The funnel has to be live for the ads to send traffic to.
items.when: launch sequencing for a new product or funnel

items.title: Run image jobs in parallel and batch them
items.text: Run several AI image sessions at once and batch the briefed images, treating them as a team of AI designers that report back at different times. Parallel jobs finish the batch faster than one at a time.
items.why: Parallel jobs finish the batch faster than one at a time.
items.when: AI image ad production in batches

items.title: Build the video brief with character, element, scene and product checks
items.text: Build the video brief with a character sheet, then check elements, scenes and products before generating any video. Catching mistakes in the brief is cheaper than in finished video.
items.why: Catching mistakes in the brief is cheaper than in finished video.

items.title: Use ElevenLabs to check ingredient pronunciation
items.text: Run the ingredient list through a voice-generation tool first so you know how each name should sound. Default voices often mispronounce ingredient names.
items.why: Ingredient names get mispronounced by default voices.

items.title: Run one QC pass once the page is ready
items.text: When a page is ready, run one quality-check pass on {brand} language, fix what it flags, and launch. One QC round catches the leftovers.
items.why: One QC round on brand language catches leftovers.

items.title: Tell Claude to apply existing work to the page builder
items.text: If the offer doc or code already exists, tell the AI to apply it to the page builder instead of re-brainstorming inside the builder. It keeps the build as fast as the idea.
items.why: It keeps the build as fast as the idea.

items.title: Do not assume a duplicated funnel works for a new product
items.text: Do not expect to duplicate a funnel for a new product, add videos and win immediately; the new product needs its own tests and research. It has different proof, price and buyer questions.
items.why: A new product has different proof, price and buyer questions.
items.when: launching a second product on an existing funnel

items.title: Consider a cheap entry offer or a gift for a better product
items.text: When a new product is clearly better, test a lower entry price or a free gift or samples to get it into customers' hands. People love free things, and unused inventory costs money.
items.why: People love free stuff, and unused inventory costs money.
items.when: launching an improved product or clearing inventory

items.title: End-of-season offer: buy two, get one free
items.text: For an end-of-season product, run buy two get one free: it moves inventory and shows a lower price per unit while the economics still work.
items.why: The economics still work and the per-bottle price looks better.
items.when: seasonal products at end of season with excess inventory

items.title: Do not over-analyze price without take-rate data
items.text: Before you have take-rate data, pick a reasonable price by gut and test it rather than over-analyzing the perfect price. Analysis without take-rate data is not real data.
items.why: Before you have take-rate data the analysis is not real data anyway.
items.when: setting price for a new offer or upsell

items.title: Screen hires with a direct response question
items.text: In job posts, ask candidates which brands are really good at direct response. The answer shows whether they know the craft and filters out people who only make filler.
items.why: A good answer filters out people who only make filler.

items.title: Media buyers get an hourly report
items.text: Give {media buyer}s an hourly report with ROAS, new-customer ROAS and CAC, and have them act on it through the day. Fast checks catch problems before spend is wasted.
items.why: Fast checks catch problems before spend is wasted.

items.title: Buy the talent for AI song ads
items.text: If the team cannot make a hard new format (AI song ads in the example), hire an {editor} who already has rather than learning it. The format is hard to learn quickly while competitors are scaling it.
items.why: The format is hard to learn quickly and the other teams are scaling it.
items.when: adopting a new ad format competitors are scaling

items.title: Pay editors per concept
items.text: Hire an {editor} with a small paid test, paying per concept or per brief, and give them access to the generation tools and team chat. A paid test shows quality and speed before you commit.
items.why: A paid test shows quality and speed before you commit.

items.title: Jump on trends early
items.text: As soon as a concept or content trend pops off, make your own version right away. The first movers get the advantage.
items.why: The first movers get the advantage.

items.title: Collect organic formats by avatar
items.text: Keep the organic swipe feed separated by {avatar} so each audience gets its own formats, then tear down the ones that fit. The best format for one {avatar} may not fit another.
items.why: The best format for one avatar may not fit another.
items.when: organic format research for multiple avatars

items.title: Clean records stop the slop
items.text: Run each swipe through a teardown that writes a full, clean record before the next stage, so every stage knows its job. Sloppy output appears when stages do not share one clear record.
items.why: Slop appears when the stages do not share one clear record.

items.title: Swap the product into a proven script
items.text: Keep a proven script and its characters and tell the system to swap in a different product. You skip rewriting scripts by hand.
items.why: You skip rewriting scripts by hand.
items.when: making new ads from a winning script

items.title: Test an AI-built page against the old one
items.text: Swipe a page, inject your {brand} language, generate new images and deploy in one session, then compare CPA against the old page. In one test CPA went from $58 to $38 on the AI-built page.
items.why: CPA went from $58 to $38 on the test page.
items.when: landing page tests with AI-assisted builds

items.title: Run the triple discount
items.text: Test the 'triple' offer: a discount, free shipping and a money-back guarantee together. Other brands in the same space reported it working.
items.why: Other brands in the space say it is working for them.

items.title: Pull a brand's top ads and tear them down
items.text: Have the AI swipe a competitor brand, pull its top five winning ads, tear them down and rewrite them for your {brand}. You study proven ads instead of guessing.
items.why: You study proven ads instead of guessing.

items.title: Ask Claude for a picture-based explainer
items.text: When you do not understand something, tell the AI you are not technical and ask for a visual explainer with pictures and flow charts. A visual is faster to understand than text.
items.why: A visual is faster to understand than text.

items.title: Layer offer, upsell, then quiz
items.text: Layer tests in order: once a new offer page lowers CPA, test new upsell structures, then launch a quiz funnel to see if CPA drops further. Each step is tested against the last baseline.
items.why: Each step is tested against the last baseline.

items.title: Tear a page into elements
items.text: Break a page into its specific elements, then recreate it with your own {brand}. It makes pages faster to remake.
items.why: It makes pages faster to remake.

items.title: Label new assets and variations
items.text: Label every asset as either a new original or a variation, and run variations as a separate step after the original. It keeps testing clean.
items.why: It keeps testing clean.

items.title: Match elements to awareness level
items.text: Put specific elements in each ad according to the viewer's awareness level. Different awareness levels need different content.
items.why: Different awareness needs different content.
items.when: ad scripting and briefs for any channel

items.title: Use GPT for realistic images with references
items.text: When you need realism and reference images, use the image model that tests best for realism (a GPT image model in the example) with prompts written for that model.
items.why: It tested best for realism.
items.when: AI image generation needing realistic output

items.title: Pick a frame, then change one thing
items.text: Extract every frame of a clip, pick the one you want, and change one element while keeping it realistic. You edit only what you clearly define.
items.why: You edit only what you clearly define.
items.when: AI image editing from video footage

items.title: Animate the mechanism
items.text: Use AI animation for visual explanations of the product's mechanism, such as molecules at work. These visuals are not meant to look real, so AI fits them well.
items.why: They are not meant to be realistic.

items.title: Fix a glitchy clip by re-sending only that clip
items.text: Fix a glitchy AI clip by cutting out only that clip and re-sending it to the generator with a fix prompt; a good version usually appears by the third or fourth try. Re-rolling one clip is faster than redoing the scene.
items.why: Re-rolling one clip is faster than redoing the scene.

items.title: Trace each ad back to its swipe
items.text: Tie each ad back to the swipe that inspired it, along with its purchases and spend, then base variations on that real data. You see which inspiration produced which result.
items.why: You see which inspiration made which result.

items.title: Aim for good design, not perfection
items.text: Aim for good design without obvious AI flaws, not perfection; checks happen afterwards. Perfection slows output.
items.why: Perfection slows output.

items.title: Start all briefs and walk away
items.text: Start many briefs at once (20 in the example) and review later, since most of a 30-minute job is waiting. The briefs aim for close enough, then you refine.
items.why: The briefs aim for close enough, then you refine.

items.title: One brief gives three videos
